R10-CLOSEOUT-CLEANUP, instrument half (Part of #201; issues #2505, #2727, #2728). Lands the closeout instrument and folds in the two fly-ins: `prune_refs.py` (batched push arm, keep guards, `--topic`) and `worktree_gc.sh` (unpushed keep, `on-remote` class, a leased class A branch delete, a leased worktree removal for classes A and B, and now a leased orphaned-seat removal for class C). `closeout.py` step 3 uses the same lease. The `--apply` run is the orchestrator's final act and was not run here. Merging this sets the group carries-open, not done.

Carry dispositions, for every carry of the group's roster entry (`dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`, numbered from 1 in roster order). origin/main's copy holds 7 carries, and the round roster ref handoff/audit-r10-roster, which the review packet reads, holds 9 (`carry` length 9 at 386f291d8). All 9 are named:
- Carry 1 (delete the probe refs for #2654 #2656 #2657): residue-no-pr in `prune_refs.py`'s plan, deleted by the final run. No new rule.
- Carry 2 (the `--apply` run is a separate, last step, the orchestrator's, roster-gated): `closeout.py` refuses while any other group is open, naming each one. Arms and mutants `closeout-1` and `closeout-2`.
- Carry 3 (folded R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS, issue 2727): the batched push arm (0 gh calls, tags before deletes, every delete leased at the planned sha and atomic per chunk, null control 2N), and the `claude/*`, open-group `design/` and age keeps. Its inner carries (dispatch/`brief/` residue, stranded handoff refs) fall to the same plan as archive-delete residue.
- Carry 4 (folded R10-FLY-WORKTREE-GC, issue 2505): the `unpushed` keep on both the classify and apply paths, and the `on-remote` class with its cwd, fetch and lsof controls. Class A's branch delete is leased at the head the porcelain read. Every worktree removal, class A and class B, is leased at that head too. The class C orphaned-seat removal is leased at the HEAD read in the orphan's own `wt/` (this round).
- Carry 5 (s9 script census, `prune_refs.py --topic <t>`): archive-then-delete, refused on a `+` cherry line or an open PR. Mutants `prune_refs-5` and `prune_refs-6`.
- Carry 6 (plan-regain study, build the tooling now, run last): the instrument lands here. The `--apply` run is not made.
- Carry 7 (s9 local cleanup: worktree_gc "eligible 0, kept 131" at 7.8 GiB free): not built here. It needs a seat-branch to PR-topic mapping read from the live PR list, a configurable seats root and a class for plain repo copies with no `.git`. Its text, failing test and null control already sit as this group's `carry[6]` in the roster, which is where it is routed. It stays pending there, so the group cannot be set done while it is neither built nor re-carried (`carry_audit.py roster` reads a pending carry on a done group as STRANDED).
- Carry 8 (closure check, s11 replan: give every entry of the carry files under `dev/programme/carries/` its destination or answering commit before the closure stamp): not built here, and out of scope. It is a pre-stamp act over files this diff does not touch, and it sits as `carry[7]` of this group on handoff/audit-r10-roster, where it stays pending.
- Carry 9 (`worktree_gc.sh` keeps any worktree a live process has its cwd in, on every removal arm: call `cwd_inside` on classes A and B as well as `on-remote`): not built here. It adds a keep to two removal arms, which is new behaviour outside this round's brief ("one site, one self-test case, one mutant"; "do not widen scope"). This round's class C lease does not touch it: a lease keeps a worktree whose HEAD moved, and a cwd holder that has not committed moves no HEAD. It sits as `carry[8]` of this group on handoff/audit-r10-roster, where it stays pending, with its fixture arms and mutant as written. Like carries 7 and 8, the group cannot be set done while it is neither built nor re-carried.

Design notes: `--topic`'s `git cherry` refusal covers `handoff/` code refs only, since body and dispatch refs are orphan commits that always carry a `+`. Local branches holding commits no remote or tag has are never deleted.

The class this PR closes is "a delete with no lease removes something that moved after the read, so a commit or tip made after the read is lost". Earlier rounds closed it in `prune_refs.py`, closeout's local branches and worktrees, worktree_gc's class A branch delete and `remove_worktree` (classes A and B). The fix review at 5aae1e12 (`Fix review: blocked 5aae1e12ea1dea099edc87f94a914a33eabd1baf class-open`) found it open at class C, the orphaned-seat `rm -rf`. This round closes it there:
- `worktree_gc.sh` class C now reads the orphan's own HEAD once, right after the branch read, for both the attached and the detached arm (`ohead`). A wt that git reads as a checkout but whose HEAD does not resolve is kept as `unreadable-head`. Before the `rm -rf`, the removal deletes that HEAD with the value read: `git -C <wt> update-ref --no-deref -d HEAD "$ohead"`. That is the same atomic local lease `remove_worktree` uses. If a seat committed after the read, the lease refuses, `worktree_gc: FAILED to remove <seat>: its HEAD is no longer <sha>, kept` is reported, and the seat stays with its commit. On an attached HEAD, git compares the old value with the resolved branch tip, and deleting the symbolic HEAD leaves the branch ref itself in place (measured on git 2.43: stale old value refused, fresh one deletes `.git/HEAD`, `refs/heads/main` file untouched). For an orphan that is a worktree of another checkout, the branch therefore survives in that checkout. A wt that git cannot read as a checkout (the pruned class, `seat-orph-old` in the self-test) has no HEAD to hold a commit and goes unleased, as before.
- Alternatives: keeping every orphan whose wt is a git checkout would also close the race, but it re-opens the 9.5 GB class the instrument exists for, since every merged orphan is a git checkout. Re-reading HEAD just before `rm -rf` narrows the race and does not close it. The lease is the existing mechanism (`remove_worktree`), applied in the one place it was missing.

## Head

`e093052af2bb7d9a46167fb9b458706ffe55f4bb` merges main `78a2be7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`31e0bab01a714bf949cb99efce04dab19c44563b` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`5a8fd981f53c00dc69836d23ab7273493c37f8fc`. It merges origin/main `499162c89d0f4f8369e16e6e41fb3a620bc1ecb0` into `7f80e2dc2415ed2ef058009557fd4421a8c6ddcc` with no conflict (`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exit 0). `7f80e2dc` is two commits on the PR head `5aae1e12ea1dea099edc87f94a914a33eabd1baf`: the class C lease with its self-test arm and mutant (`b1320783`), and the header and instrument-doc clauses (`7f80e2dc`). It is a fast-forward of the PR head. Merge base with origin/main: 499162c8. Main's delta over the branch's own files is three `echo ... --no-renames` lines in `.github/workflows/governance.yml`, outside the seat steps. `tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh`, `closeout.py`, `prune_refs.py` and the mutants harness are byte-identical between 7f80e2dc and 5a8fd981 (`git diff --quiet 7f80e2dc 5a8fd981 -- <those four>` exit 0). origin/main was 499162c8 at 2026-11-05T01:26Z.

## Re-cut

Round 9 of the repair seat, a minimal re-cut past the three-round rule. The scope is only what the 5aae1e12 verdict names: the unleased class C orphaned-seat `rm -rf` in `worktree_gc.sh` (one site, one self-test case, one mutant), the corrected class C disposition, and `## Red checks` read at the PR head. Nothing else was widened. The verdict recommended a split or a re-cut, and the brief took the re-cut.

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py M0 closeout-1 closeout-2 closeout-3 closeout-4 prune_refs-1 prune_refs-2 prune_refs-3 prune_refs-4 prune_refs-5 prune_refs-6 prune_refs-7 prune_refs-8 prune_refs-9 prune_refs-10 worktree_gc-1 worktree_gc-2 worktree_gc-3 worktree_gc-4 worktree_gc-5 worktree_gc-6 cloud_relay-50 cloud_relay-51 cloud_relay-52 cloud_relay-53 cloud_relay-54 cloud_relay-55 cloud_relay-56 cloud_relay-57`, run at b1320783, printed M0 `0 seat step(s) red`, all 28 mutants KILLED, `RESULT survivors=0`, rc 0. Between b1320783 and the head, `worktree_gc.sh` gained only comment lines (`git diff b1320783 7f80e2dc -- tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh`, every changed line an added `#` line), and the merge leaves the four instrument and harness files byte-identical. Main's three changed `governance.yml` lines each add `--no-renames` to an `echo` that prints a restored-file count, and none is a `tools/audit/seat` step that M0 runs. The 27 earlier ids stay KILLED (`worktree_gc-1..5`: 105 checks, 5, 2, 2, 3 and 17 failed; `closeout-1..4`: 28 checks, 6, 5, 1 and 2 failed; `prune_refs-1..10`; `cloud_relay-50..57`).
- New: `worktree_gc-6` drops the class C lease's old value (`update-ref --no-deref -d HEAD "$ohead" 2>` becomes `update-ref --no-deref -d HEAD 2>`): `worktree_gc self-test: 105 checks, 3 failed`, namely "the orphan removal leased at the head the read gave (class C)", "orphan with a merged branch: removed" and "null control: the unmoved detached orphan in the same run is removed". The second and third fail because the self-test's git stub refuses an argument-less lease as an unexpected call, so the stub kills this mutant through the lease-argument row, not through the moved-HEAD row. The property itself is shown on real git: the reviewer's harness run against the mutated file gives race `RESULT race=1 orphan-detached-moved-head-lost=1` and null `=0`.

Failing first: the final self-test hunks run against the PR head's unfixed production code (`$EXPORT/gc-before-tests.sh`: the head's file with this diff's self-test section spliced in) gave `worktree_gc self-test: 105 checks, 3 failed`: "the orphan removal leased at the head the read gave (class C)", "the orphaned seat whose HEAD moved is kept" and "and the refused removal is reported". ## Forward-carry

- After a lease refusal, the moved ref's archive tag `archive/<name>` already sits at the old sha. A re-plan at the new tip then has its tag push refused (`tag-FAILED`, abort). This is safe, because nothing is deleted, but a re-run stays blocked on that ref until the old tag is retargeted or a per-sha tag name is adopted. It is a `prune_refs.py` defect, and #2727 is the issue for those. Carry: #2727

3085.title: R10-CLOSEOUT-CLEANUP: closeout cleanup

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked 7f95f9084b42aa5bd651a9aa98cc5b4292adcaaa class-open: prune_refs.apply_plan_push deletes a ref that moved after the plan was read, untagged

bus-nonce: 09ce08fe08438b697a4b84f370b3c6bb

## Round

First review of PR #3085 (R10-CLOSEOUT-CLEANUP, instrument half), at the live head 7f95f9084b42aa5bd651a9aa98cc5b4292adcaaa, from a detached worktree at that SHA. The fixer's history is five repair rounds; this verdict is the first review, so fixer.md's re-cut threshold is not reached by review rounds.

## Block

`tools/audit/seat/prune_refs.py` `apply_plan_push` (new in this PR, called by `closeout.py` step 2 and by `prune_refs.py --apply`/`--topic --apply`) pushes `git push --delete refs/heads/<name>` with no lease. The only guard, the missing-tag read-back, compares the remote's archive tag with the sha *the plan read*, not with the ref's tip at delete time. Its own docstring and `closeout.py`'s header promise "a ref to delete without its tag at its own sha refuses the whole step before any delete". That promise does not hold for a ref that moves between the plan read and the delete push: the ref is deleted and its new tip is archived nowhere. For a ref the plan deletes untagged (`ci-probe/*`, a tip in main), the new commits are archived nowhere at all.

Reproduced at this head with the module's own function against a throwaway bare remote (ev/lease-race.py, ev/lease-race.txt): plan at a1484914, ref advanced to 96965aa6, `apply_plan_push` returns `tag` and `delete`, the remote ends with no `fix/x` head and `archive/fix/x` at a1484914 only. `RESULT moved-tip-deleted-untagged=1`. Null control (ev/lease-null.txt): the same plan taken at the live tip archives and deletes with nothing lost, `RESULT ... moved-tip-deleted-untagged=0`. Candidate fix, tested on a copy (ev/lease-fix-candidate.txt): one `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<n>:<planned sha>` per ref in each delete chunk; the moved ref is rejected (`delete-FAILED`, the chunk aborts as the arm already does on a refusal) and survives at 96965aa6, `RESULT moved-tip-deleted-untagged=0`. The repair owes a self-test arm that plants the moved ref and fails without the lease, plus a mutant that drops it.

The old gh-api arm (`apply_plan`) had the same unconditional DELETE. The push arm is new code written for this group's carry 3, though, and its archive-first guarantee is the property the owner's request rests on, so this is a block on the new arm and not only a carry. `--topic --apply` runs mid-round, while seats still push, so the window is not confined to the round's last act.

Part of #201. R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY parts (a) to (c), the Lean flow pre-study's K12: ruling R4 made true in the tool, so a body fix no longer moves a clean head. Built on #3037 (V147, the `Code:` trailer).

The group's carries, numbered as the roster's `carry` list numbers them (from 1):

- Carry 1 (the Lean flow pre-study, K12): built here, parts (a) to (c) below.
- Carry 2 (`app_approve.sh --carry` until this lands): released once this merges; a body-only move no longer needs a carry.
- Carry 3 (self-test hygiene): (a) this PR's mutants take per-file ids inside their instrument's block (`cloud_relay-50` to `-58`, `update_pr-1` to `-7`); (b) the new rows reuse the fixtures' existing throwaway origins, and `tests/throwaway_git.py --check` refuses 0 sites; (c) no new git push site: body-only PATCHes through `body_patch.sh`; (d) `## Red checks` below.
- Carry 4 (V147, the `Code:` trailer and the stale-body refusal): landed in #3037; part (c) reads that trailer.
- Carry 5 (P321): landed with carry 4 in #3037.

As built:

- Part (a), `tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh`: origin/main is merged only when `gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus` says `DIRTY` or `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` fails. An unread merge state counts as not DIRTY, because merge-tree is the local proof either way.
- Part (b), the same script: when the merges and the row leave the head exactly where origin had it, nothing is pushed; `body_patch.sh` runs the body contract at that head, from the run's worktree, and PATCHes the body (`update_pr: BODY-ONLY:`). With code `-`, a `handoff/<topic>` tip the head lacks refuses. A head that is the live head plus one commit asks `--row-only`.
- Part (c), `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh` `handoff_arm`: a PR whose head holds its handoff tip, and whose `handoff-body/<topic>` tip this relay has not applied and names that tip in `Code:`, gets `HPO_UPDATE_BODY_ONLY=1 update_pr.sh <branch> - <body>` once per body move, recorded in `cloud-handoff-bodied`. The hold applies; the review freeze does not, and `update_pr.sh` now guarantees the reason it does not: under `HPO_UPDATE_BODY_ONLY` a run whose merges or row would leave the head other than the live head refuses (`update_pr: REFUSE: body-only update would move the head ...`) and pushes nothing, and the relay records that refusal as owed `handoff-update`.

Alternatives not taken:

- A commit-time rule for "this body is new": runner and host clocks skew, and a re-body of an unchanged head is legitimately newer. The applied-body record needs no clock.
- Body-only only for code `-`: a code sha the head already holds leaves the same unmoved head, and refusing it keeps the prepr re-run cost.
- Running `body_patch.sh` from the main checkout: its lint resolves cited paths in the caller's tree, so a body citing a file the PR adds is refused.
- Round 7's guard in the relay (apply the freeze unless the move is guaranteed body-only): the relay cannot know DIRTY or a missing row without re-deriving what `update_pr.sh` computes after its merges, so it would duplicate that logic. The flag puts the check where `H` and `LIVE` already are: one guard line in `update_pr.sh` plus one env assignment on the relay's launch line.

## Re-cut

Round 7 of R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY, a minimal re-cut answering `verdict/3089` round 2 (blocked at `2fd46f26`, class-open): `handoff_arm` skipped the review freeze on a body-only move, but `update_pr.sh <branch> - <body>` still moved the head when (a) the PR was `DIRTY` and the local merge of main was clean, or (b) a contained head lacked its delivery row (`ensure_row`, `--row-only` push), so a head holding a merge verdict or a dispatched review could move with no `cloud-handoff-release` entry and no `HELD-*` line. Closed at one seam, `update_pr.sh`'s head check, driven by the relay's `HPO_UPDATE_BODY_ONLY=$bonly` (commit `62673524`); `9da59904` documents the refusal in both instrument guides. The verdict's second finding: `## Red checks` below is retaken from the whole check-run set and names `tests / nightly-status` as main's inherited red. Every figure below was re-taken in this body-only retake by running its command, at the handoff tip that holds `9da59904`.

`ecf4ef3fe30087e5a47ddbddcedcb6d2584f5c1d` merges main `3583448` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`98beb50fd6e7de0142a2e2ec96c55a43475eb00b` is the PR head: it merges the authored handoff tip `39e9abd5009448270215222943aa0fd0ac76b1e1` (which holds the code head named below, `9da59904cc9a3ea2d7a941ea3e24dab5f6d52017`, plus origin/main `8e90d8144`) into the previous PR head `2fd46f26`, by the orchestrator's script; no code was resolved by hand.

Part 1 of R10-SUITE-HOST-DETERMINISM (issues #2726, #2730): the suite's host-zone, gate-lease-timing and coverage-descendant nondeterminism. This round closes the host-zone class across every script `tests/run.sh` invokes, not only `tests/features.py` and `tests/finite_boundary.py`. The parts named under Forward-carry are not built here.

## Re-cut note

This is the final body-only round for verdict/3170 (round 4, blocked at 5ee2be2d). The orchestrator ruled, under the owner mandate, that the host-zone class is closed and the PR merges as is; no production or test file changed in this round, only origin/main was merged in. Earlier: round 3's answer to verdict/3170 (round 2, blocked at 0a459e60). The finding was: "class-open: tests/finite_boundary.py still fails host-zone checks at the head under America/New_York (1 of 108) and Asia/Kolkata (2 of 108), and passes under UTC". The body is retaken whole from the template headings, and round history is deleted. Every figure below was re-taken in this pass.

The class is a suite check whose result moves with the host zone (`TZ`) or Home Assistant's configured zone (`HASTUB_TZ`), when it should not. The rule that enumerates the class is `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/host_zone_features.py --suite`. It runs every script `tests/run.sh` invokes (its `run` and `run_always` lines, 38 commands) under seven rows:
- `gate`: `TZ=UTC`, `HASTUB_TZ` unset. This is the null row.
- UTC.
- America/New_York, Asia/Tokyo, Europe/Stockholm and Asia/Kolkata (half-hour).
- Europe/London, a DST zone whose 2026 transitions fall on the EU dates the suite's own instants read (2026-03-29, 2026-10-25). Its winter offset is zero, so a leak there shows only across a transition.

Each zone row sets `TZ` and `HASTUB_TZ` together. Every red row is a seam. The seams the sweep returned at the round-3 tip and at the merge base are below, each with its disposition.

What this round changes on top of the round-3 commits (the finite_boundary instant arm, card.mjs's seam clock, guard_pins' idle-cooling clock):
- **`tests/ha_contract.py`**: four default-case `util.dt` contracts asserted `HASTUB_TZ` unset. So the script read `4 of 96 contracts FAILED` under every configured zone, UTC included. Each contract now evaluates in the zone that a fresh copy of the provider's own `util/dt` module sets with `HASTUB_TZ` absent (`_unconfigured_zone`, `_in_default_case`). The default case is constructed rather than read off the host. The nightly lane copies upstream's module in the same way.
- **`tests/golden.py`**: the `coord_*` payloads move with Home Assistant's configured zone, as a time-of-use grid fee's peak hours and the energy totals' local day rightly do. Under America/New_York, 5 of 56 golden payloads differed from the gate capture (`coord_grid_fee`'s forecast prices took the peak fee five hours early). The configured zone is an input of the installation the scenario describes, so `capture_coordinator` now sets `DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE` to `SCENARIO_ZONE` (UTC, the zone the fixtures were recorded in) at the capture boundary, and restores it after. In that zone the naive `START` freeze is the instant it names, so round 3's aware-freeze workaround is dropped, and one mechanism covers both leaks.
- **`dev/audit/harnesses/host_zone_features.py`**:

comments.body:

## Head

Merge base dfb4ce2b52fafb340e0320bc2efb870099a53884. `git diff <mb>...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract is current.

## Block

1. **class-open (carries 0 and 3, 0-based).** The group brief's class is "the features checks that fail under a non-UTC `HASTUB_TZ`". The body measures one zone, Europe/Stockholm (UTC+1), and its new comments claim correctness "under any `HASTUB_TZ`". No enumeration rule is named. I ran the head under two more non-UTC zones, and the same failure shape (a naive or UTC-literal instant against the configured zone) is still red there:
   - `HASTUB_TZ=America/New_York`: base `6 of 4770 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, head `3 of 4770 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`. Still red at the head:
     - "with no meter, a month of DHW-only mornings bills what the stated rule bills ..." (tests/features.py:17145)
     - "a naive stored tick adopts the clock's zone and detects the same gap" (tests/features.py:47485; `_T3_OUTAGE_NOW` is UTC-aware, and the naive tick is replaced to naive UTC wall clock)
     - "the humidity entry nearest NOW wins, not the first in the list" (tests/features.py:50527; `_T6_HUM_NOW` is naive)
   - `HASTUB_TZ=Asia/Tokyo`: base `8 of 4770 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, head `3 of 4770 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`. Still red at the head:
     - the DHW-only mornings bill check
     - "#943: the honest sizer leaves a power-limited heavy house at the full nameplate step ..."
     - the humidity-nearest-NOW check

   These are neither fixed in the diff nor dispositioned in the body. The fix pattern the PR already uses (name the instant in `DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE`, or make it aware) applies to each. Whether any of them is a production zone defect rather than a test assumption has to be settled per check by the fixer.
2. **The gate-lease carry (carry 1, 0-based) is marked BUILT, but the flake is still live at the head.** Without any planted defect, `one_winner` read red once at the head on a quiet runner with the CI signature `queued=True overlaps=1 order=['b', 'a']` (ev/gl_head_quiet.txt). Overall it was 1 red in 190 head runs and 0 in 160 base runs.

   The mechanism is a TOCTOU in production `_free_slot` (tests/gate_lock.py:708-715). `_read_at` sees `is_file()` False and returns None. The rival's `os.link` then lands. `_free_slot`'s own `if not path.is_file()` re-check is now True, so it unlinks the rival's live, just-created slot. Every waiter runs `_free_slot` on every poll, including a waiter that is not at the head of the queue.

   A pure 30 ms delay after `_read_at` returns None for a slot path, with no logic changed, makes the case red 2 of 10 at the head and 2 of 10 at the base (ev/gl_toctou.py, ev/gl_head_toctou.txt, ev/gl_base_toctou.txt). So the race predates this PR. The PR's test-side change (a condition wait instead of the 0.15 s hold) is sound and keeps the planted control red, but it does not fix the flake the carry exists for. The body's "cause is not established" should become the cause above, and the fix belongs in `_free_slot`: do not unlink on a missing-then-present file, or re-read before unlinking. That fix also needs a planted-delay control like the one here.
3. **root-cause-unanswered: `tests / replay`** (check-run 125168587530) concluded `failure` at this head: `1 of 176 replay checks FAILED`, "synthetic-dhw-only.json: cycle_cost [1 offender(s): cpu_ratio 2.389 over its budget 2.173]". `## Red checks` says "none from this diff" and does not name it, and `pr-contract` refuses on exactly that (run 125180207180: "check `tests / replay` is red and `## Red checks` does not name it"). The diff writes no runtime code (see Evidence), so this is likely runner CPU noise, but the body owes the answer.

## Findings

- features.py zone checks still red at the head under America/New_York (3) and Asia/Tokyo (3): DHW-only mornings bill, naive stored tick (`_T3_OUTAGE_NOW`), humidity nearest NOW (`_T6_HUM_NOW`), and #943 sizer. Fix or disposition each, and measure Stockholm, New_York, Tokyo and UTC at both ends. Carry: R10-SUITE-HOST-DETERMINISM
- Gate-lease flake still live at the head (1 of 190 unplanted). The cause is the `_free_slot` is_file TOCTOU (tests/gate_lock.py:708-715), demonstrated with a delay-only plant at base and head (2 of 10 each). Build the fix in `_free_slot` with the delay plant as its control; the CI history's earlier `overlaps=1` reds before 2026-10-24 were fab4a07c1's torn create. Carry: R10-SUITE-HOST-DETERMINISM
- `tests / replay` red at the head (cycle_cost cpu_ratio 2.389 > 2.173 on synthetic-dhw-only.json) is not named in `## Red checks`, and `pr-contract` is red on it. Carry: R10-SUITE-HOST-DETERMINISM
- No committed finder's harness exists for carries 0-3. I built my own and disclose them as the reviewer's, not the finder's: ev/crv.py (it runs the head's `_coverage_revalidation` against either tree's coverage_tree.sh), ev/gl.py (repeats `_priority_cases`, optionally with the pre-fab4a07c1 O_EXCL-then-write create planted), and ev/gl_toctou.py (the delay-only plant). The fixer should land the gate-lease one with the `_free_slot` fix (fixer.md 18). Carry: R10-SUITE-HOST-DETERMINISM

## Red checks

Every check-run at the head (55 runs, one page, read live after all workflows concluded):
- `tests / replay` (125168587530) is red; see Block 3.
- `pr-contract / pr-contract` (125179056639 and 125180207180) is red on the unnamed replay red, the only ERROR in its body check.

## Evidence

The AST with docstrings blanked is identical at base and head (ev/coordinator_ast.txt). `_comparable_ts` already returns `dt_util.as_local(ts).replace(tzinfo=None)` for an aware stamp against a naive grid, so the old docstring ("keeps its own wall clock") was wrong and the new one matches the code. There is no runtime change, and the behaviour is preserved. The features check over it (`_t6_comparable_ts`) passes at the head under Stockholm, UTC and unset.
- RESULT features at both ends (`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`):

Keys the synthetic fixture's replay cost budget by runner class. The class signal is the run's own BLAS ruler: the median reference-solve `ref_ms` that each `cost` line prints. This round admits a fourth class, ref24, on its own CI readings. The class also keys `loop_cpu_ratio`, because ref24 reads 0.1282, over the shared 0.1278. A ruler in no band is still refused by name, and no default budget is assumed. The refusal is now probed in every gap between bands and at the two rulers CI read that no band admits. Closes #3129.

## Re-cut note

This is repair round 4 of #3174. Under the past-three rule this body is retaken whole, and round history is deleted. The finding: CI replay job 125461180429 (run 41498701363, at `acec536b`) ran on a runner whose ruler reads `ref_ms` 23.77-24.31. That is in no band of `COST_RUNNER_CLASSES`. So `cycle_cost` and its three doubled-arm checks failed on `runner class unknown`, and `pr-contract` failed because the body did not name `tests / replay`. The ruling for the later review: "CI exposed a runner class the r3 harness never ran; repair of the named band seam only".

What changed against `acec536b` is `tests/replay.py` only, in the band seam:
- `COST_RUNNER_CLASSES` gains `ref24` (22.64, 25.53).
- `COST_CLASS_BUDGETS` gains `ref24` `cpu_ratio` 3.630 and `loop_cpu_ratio` 0.1813.
- `COST_CLASS_READINGS` rows now name their metric and gain that job's two readings.
- New `COST_RULERS_REFUSED` (28.01, 34.35).
- `control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown` probes every gap between bands, a ruler under the lowest band, `COST_RULERS_REFUSED`, and NaN.
- The comments state the rule and the census.

No band is widened. No `*_budgets.json` is touched, nothing is refactored, and no existing budget moves.

**Why a band of its own, and not a wider band or a fallback.** The data says the per-class cost ratio is not a function of the ruler. ref24, the fastest ruler, reads synthetic `cpu_ratio` 2.5671, which falls between ref46 (2.27-2.42) and ref30 (2.61-2.81). The 28.0 runner (job 125000687320) sits 2.5 % under the ref30 floor, yet reads 1.8924, 0.67-0.72x of ref30's ratios. Grade that runner on ref30's 3.934 and its doubled arm, 3.8922, is not over budget. A widened band would therefore hide exactly the 2x regression the lane exists to see. Interpolating or borrowing a neighbour fails the same way. So the sound rule keeps r3's refusal: a class is admitted only on its own cited readings, and anything else fails closed by name. The standing cost is one red lane per new runner SKU. Its own `cost` lines are the readings that admit it.

## Head

`d52dc26f20770bed8fbf1b8fb0b154c42cc773d6` is the orchestrator's recarry of main into the previous head. It is not a clean merge of the live head and main (parent 1 372c21ac is not the live pull-request head 558c54a0), so prepr checked this head.

`372c21ac6cf2cc8b230a8ab8ec1d5b47de52bd6b` merges main `fad43b0` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`558c54a0f0f0617678caa9acc87a426a8ddb19bc` merges the authored code head `4de0f6565221868a0da1b5c88626f052e88d0eda` and then merges origin/main `b8e823699` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`4de0f6565221868a0da1b5c88626f052e88d0eda` fast-forwards `acec536b4ba1dc000126671f1f727defd21f1925` by three commits. Every local figure below was taken on that head. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict against origin/main `871a20da138592ac892f4652a4f82992a6626783`, nor against `b8e823699981866383f1afa54ce708ded3419316` (read 2026-11-02T20:16:14Z), so main was not merged, as the brief allows a merge only on a conflict. Main's delta `871a20da..b8e82369` is 17 files of triage batches and delivery rows. It touches no `custom_components/` file and no replay file, so nothing the figures measure moved. Merge base: `38dcb6c5dbade5206f2fae885334483082f36d10`.

## Red checks

I read the whole check-run set at `acec536b` through the PR's `get_check_runs`: total_count 55, one page. Three concluded failure.
- `tests / replay` (job 125461180429). Four checks failed: `cycle_cost` and `sees a doubled cycle` cpu, memory and loop, each with `runner class unknown: ref_ms 23.83 lies in no band of COST_RUNNER_CLASSES`. Cause: a runner SKU that the r3 readings never sampled. Process state: the refusal worked as designed, failing closed at first sight and by name. Cheaper detector: none exists. A runner's SKU is assigned at job start and is unknowable before CI runs, and the 22-job census found no earlier ref24 reading at current code. The refusal is the detector, and its standing cost is one red per new class. Answered here by admitting the class on that job's readings.
- `pr-contract / pr-contract` (job 125483440211): `check tests / replay is red and ## Red checks does not name it`. Answered by this section.
- `gate` (jobs 125483784051, 125484217523): `FAIL pr-contract / pr-contract`. It follows pr-contract and has no cause of its own.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is a `sed` edit to `tests/replay.py`, made at the head. The probe is `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests'); import replay; [print(n, ok, d[:120]) for n, ok, d in replay.controls() if 'class' in n]"`. After each run the file was restored and compared with `cmp` against the head copy, and a `cmp` hit on the mutant itself was checked so that no edit is vacuous.

**Per class: a budget that cannot see its own planted 2x.** The planted 2x is each class's `cpu doubled` arm from CI, held in `COST_CLASS_READINGS`. Each mutant loosens one class's budget past its own doubled arm:
- K24, `s/"ref24": {"cpu_ratio": 3.630,/"ref24": {"cpu_ratio": 5.3,/`: `FAIL control:cycle_cost:class_budgets [(23.83, ['cpu_ratio 2.567: budget 5.3 cannot see a 2x cycle; re-record 3.63'], [])]`. **Killed.**
- K24L, which drops ref24's loop key so it falls back to the shared 0.1278 (`s/, "loop_cpu_ratio": 0.1813}/}/`): `FAIL ... [(23.83, ['loop_cpu_ratio 0.1282 over its budget 0.1278'], ...)]`. **Killed.**
- K24B, which deletes the ref24 band: `FAIL control:cycle_cost:class_budgets [(23.83, ['no recorded budget: ...'])...]` and `FAIL control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown`. **Killed.**
- K30, ref30 3.934 to 5.76: `FAIL ... [(30.32, ['cpu_ratio 2.81: budget 5.76 cannot see a 2x cycle; re-record 3.974'], [])...]`. **Killed.**
- K46, ref46 3.357 to 4.83: `FAIL ... [(45.65, ['cpu_ratio 2.325: budget 4.83 cannot see a 2x cycle; re-record 3.287'], [])...]`. **Killed.**
- K53, ref53 2.081 to 2.96: `FAIL ... [(52.76, ['cpu_ratio 1.456: budget 2.96 cannot see a 2x cycle; re-record 2.06'], [])...]`. **Killed.**
- M1, one budget 3.614 for every class: `FAIL ... [(52.76, ['cpu_ratio 1.456: budget 3.614 cannot see a 2x cycle; ...'])...]`. **Killed.**

**Unknown class.**
- M4, an unknown class falls back to ref46 (`s/... and c in keyed), None)/... and c in keyed), "ref46")/`): `FAIL control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown bad=[] good=[]`. **Killed.**
- W30, ref30 widened down over the 28.0 runner (`s/"ref30": (28.72, 32.69)/"ref30": (26.0, 32.69)/`). At `834d0074` this **survived** (33 of 33 ok), because no control pinned a known foreign ruler. `4de0f656` adds `COST_RULERS_REFUSED`, and it now reads `FAIL control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown bad=[] good=[]`. **Killed.** This is a disclosed self-correction within this round.
- W46, ref46 widened down to 33.0, and W30u, ref30 widened up to 35.0, over the 34.35 ruler: both read `FAIL control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown`. **Killed.**

## Null control

- **Head unmutated:** `33 of 33 controls ok` (the probe above, counting every control).
- **The failing job, base against head.** I put the four `cost` lines of job 125461180429 through the production `class_budget` + `cost_offenders`:
  - At `acec536b`, all four read `runner class unknown`. That is the CI red, reproduced.
  - At the head, the clean run reads `[]`. `cpu doubled` reads `cpu_ratio 5.209 over its budget 3.63`, `memory doubled` reads `peak_kib 3861 over its budget 2686`, and `loop doubled` reads `loop_cpu_ratio 0.2603 over its budget 0.1813`.
  - The owner fixture's clean 269.8155 at `ref_ms` 24.06 reads `[]` at both (unkeyed, 337.8).
- **The census, every reading.** I graded all 22 jobs at the head (Figures).
  - The 19 jobs whose rulers lie in a band read `within`, and each `cpu doubled` arm reads `seen` (over its class budget).
  - The three outside every band read `REFUSED`, both clean and doubled: 28.01 (job 125000687320), 34.35 (nightly job 123225871060) and 22.16 (nightly job 121370544228, 10-26, older cycle code, not admitted).
  - Had a band been widened to fit these, at least one of them would read `NOT SEEN`. 28.01 graded on ref30's 3.934 gives 3.8922 < 3.934.
- **ref24 budget placement.** 2.5671 / 3.630 and 0.1282 / 0.1813 are each 70.7 %, inside (budget / 2, budget]. The class's `ref_ms` spread within the job is 2.3 %. The band is the extremes widened 5 % each way, and it is disjoint from ref30 (28.72).

## Figures

- **Readings source.** Each reading is the `cost {...}` line of a job log. Re-take one with `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/jobs/125461180429/logs`, keeping lines holding `cycles over` and `doubled:`. Job 125461180429 read:
  - clean `cpu_ratio` 2.5671 and `loop_cpu_ratio` 0.1282 at `ref_ms` 23.83;
  - `cpu doubled` 5.2086 at 23.99;
  - `memory doubled` `peak_kib` 3860.7 at 24.31;
  - `loop doubled` 0.2603 at 23.77;
  - owner fixture 269.8155 at 24.06.
- **Band rule.** min / 1.05 floored and max x 1.05 ceiled to 0.01, over every clean and doubled `ref_ms` of the cited job: 23.77 and 24.31 give 22.64-25.53.
- **Budget rule.** sqrt(2) x the geometric midpoint of the class's clean extremes, the rule every budget in the file uses. One job gives sqrt(2) x 2.5671 = 3.630 and sqrt(2) x 0.1282 = 0.1813. The lane's own `record:` line printed `cpu_ratio=3.63 ... loop_cpu_ratio=0.1813`.
- **Census of 22 jobs.** These are every `tests / replay` job that ran in the 60 most recent `ci.yml` runs (4) plus earlier replay-branch runs (7, from PRs #3174, #3170, #3167 and #3078), and all 11 scheduled nightly `slow` jobs. Each was graded with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests'); import replay as r; s='synthetic-dhw-only.json'; [print(x, r.class_budget(s, x)[1][:1] or r.cost_offenders({'cpu_ratio': c}, r.class_budget(s, x)[0])) for x, c in ((23.83, 2.5671), (28.01, 1.8924), (34.35, 1.8747), (22.16, 1.9455), (47.73, 2.2746), (54.55, 1.4448))]"`, the same call over each job's clean and doubled pair. Result: 19 in band read `within` and `seen`, and three read `REFUSED`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` at the head.
- Scoped gate, re-run at `4de0f656`, `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 3 script(s) run, 30 scoped out` (`debug_collect`, `entities`, `features`). That run was against origin/main `871a20da`. Main has since moved to `b8e82369` with no conflict and nothing this diff reads (Head), and under the brief's merge-only-on-conflict rule there was no merge, so there was no second run.

## Carries

Closes #2259

Part 2 of R10-ARCHSCORE-SPELLINGS, the rest of the split ruling. Part 1 (#3169, merged as 871a20da) added `card_rule_copies` (counter C24) for `&&`/`||` rules. Part 2 does two things:

- It makes C24 read a rule spelled as a **template literal**.
- It pays for what the new census reads by deduplicating the real copies in the card.

No budget is raised. `archscore.card_rule_copies` stays capped at 72, and the tree now reads 70.

- **The census** (`tools/audit/archscore/metrics/card.py`). With `strings=True`, `tokenize` keeps each template text segment as one token: a backtick, its place (`W`, `H`, `M`, `T`) and its text. `_templates` lists every template that has a `${..}`, nested templates included. In `rule_copies`, each run of two or more of a template's `${..}` is keyed by `_rule_key`, with the text between them as joints and `roots=True`. Under `roots=True` a value is its root name, numbered, and its members stay as spelled. A run is a rule when some value is read twice, it is `RULE_TOKENS` long, and it carries content. A site is one template. The chain census still reads a template's text as `S`, so its keys are unchanged.
- **The generic exclusion.** A MARKUP template is left out: one whose own text opens or closes a tag (`_MARKUP = <[A-Za-z/!]`). Its `${..}` fill different slots of what it draws, so it is not a rule, and markup belongs to `card_clone_copies`. This criterion excludes the SVG coordinate markup (shared bands, value axis and grid, chart rects, series paths, setup pipe paths) and the quiet-window form. It does not exclude a path string written without a tag, such as `pathPoint`.
- **The payment** (`heatpump-optimizer-card.js`). Every real copy the census reads is now shared:
  - `edgeKey`: `setupSvgHtml`, two sites in `evaluate`, and `removeEdge`.
  - `windowRange`: `formatWindows`, `draftSignature` (through a local `windowSig`), and both clash messages.
  - The overlap `span` in `quietOverlapProblem`, now one loop over the hot-water windows and then the silent ones, in the same order.
  - `storageKey`, built on `storageKeyLegacy`, which is its prefix.
  - `pathPoint`: `steppedLine` and `smoothLine`.
  - One `dropText` in the what-if `summary`.

  Every string the card writes is unchanged (Null control). The brief named four of these. `windowRange` and `dropText` are the two further real copies the census reads; without them the count would have been 77, over the cap.

## Head

`f5f56576b13dbcd8687dfabdbfbef587dcfaf3b9` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3179.md`. The authored code head is `79420455c0717f1fb4f8161787e1603a60304f60`.

`79420455c0717f1fb4f8161787e1603a60304f60`: the fix commits plus a merge of origin/main.

Merge base `b8e823699981866383f1afa54ce708ded3419316`. origin/main was at `b8e82369` on 2026-11-02 at 19:53 UTC. It had moved from the dispatch base 871a20da, by `dev/programme` records only, before any `tools/pr/prepr.sh` run. So it was merged once, by the brief's rule, and every figure below is taken at this head. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` with this body ended `rc=0` at this head. origin/main was still `b8e82369` afterwards, so no second run was owed.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant was run in a detached copy of the fix commit `d85ff06ac` and then restored; `git status --porcelain` was empty afterwards. The C24 checks were driven through `tests/arch_score.py`'s `card_rule_spellings` and `card_template_spellings` with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`.

- **M1, the template arm off**: in `rule_copies`, `enumerate(_templates(body))` -> `enumerate(_templates(body)[:0])`. Red: `FAIL card_rule_copies: a template rule respelled inline at a second site reads both sites  [0 -> 0]`. rt_47 on the pinned tree 7952d8f9 read `card_rule_copies` 53 -> 53 under M1 (no rise, so no WORSENS) and 77 -> 78 restored.
- **M2, the markup criterion off**: `if not any(_MARKUP.search(x, 2) for x in texts):` -> `if True:`. Red: `FAIL card_rule_copies null: markup drawn again reads nothing  [0 -> 2]`. On the real card it reads 85, not 70.
- **Failing test first**: commit `9ac93f83e` (the test, rt_47 and its `expected.json` row) comes before the census commit `41450b407`. At that commit the check above fails (`0 -> 0`).

## Null control

- **The census's own nulls**, green at this head:
  - an unrelated one-value template `${h.a}/${h.b}`
  - the same template over two values `${h[0]}>${cfg[1]}`
  - markup drawn again

  None of them moves the count. Part 1's three chain nulls are still green.
- **The card's strings, base against head.** A `node` differential loads every top-level card function from origin/main's card and from this head's card and compares their outputs over 229 cases:
  - `formatWindows`
  - `quietOverlapProblem` on 216 spec triples, 128 of which return a clash message
  - `steppedLine` and `smoothLine` at 1, 2, 3, 5 and 17 points

  `229 cases, 0 differ`. The perturbed control (`pathPoint` x to 3 decimals) printed `229 cases, 10 differ`. The other dedupes are textual identities, checked by eye: `edgeKey`, `storageKey` (legacy prefix plus `:${title}:${cfg.hours}`), `windowSig` and `dropText`.
- **No new undefined name.** `eslint` with `no-undef` reports 69 findings on origin/main's card and the same 69 on this head's (browser globals). A planted `edgeKeyX` was reported, so the check can see one.
- **The old instrument on both trees.** origin/main's `card.py` reads `card_rule_copies` 72 on origin/main's card and 70 on this head's card: the shared `dropText` also removes a chain copy.

## Figures

- **Architecture score.** `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff origin/main HEAD` prints `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`, with `card_rule_copies 93 -> 70  (gate only)`. Both trees are read by this head's instrument; 93 is origin/main's card under the template-aware census. No metric gets worse.
- **Census at head.** `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/audit'); from pathlib import Path; from archscore.metrics import card as K; m=K.measure(Path('.')); print(m['card_dead_definitions'], m['card_clone_copies'], m['card_rule_copies'])"` prints `0 103 70`. The rule is `card.measure`. The cap in `tests/ci_budgets.json` is 72 and is untouched.
- **Seams of the class.** The enumerating rule is `card.rule_copies(card.card_tokens(root, strings=True))`:
  - On origin/main's card it returns 7 template classes (21 sites, 93 - 72 + 0). All 7 are closed in this diff: edge key ×3, window range ×5, overlap span ×4, path point ×3 + ×2, storage key ×2 and signed drop ×2.
  - At this head it returns 22 classes and 70 sites, of which 0 are template-site classes.
  - The 15 markup sites (M2's 85 - 70) are dispositioned by the stated `_MARKUP` criterion.
- **Structure ratchet.** `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- **Scoped gate.** `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 10 script(s) run, 23 scoped out.` `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub bash tests/run.sh`: ended `13 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED; 22 SCOPED OUT AND NOT RUN`, rc 0, with `ALL 2602 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, `ALL 269 ARCHITECTURE SCORE CHECKS PASSED`, `ALL 18 ARCHITECTURE SCORE HEAD CHECKS PASSED`, `ALL 4777 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, `ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED`.
- **Closures.** `tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/arch_score.py` and `--single tests/entities.py`, run on Linux, add `47_card_template_respelled.py` to both closures (commit `49ebf21fd`). The new file is classified that way.
- **Claim files and version.** `git diff --quiet $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) HEAD -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt VERSION` exits 0.

## Architecture score

dS +0.0000 NULL. No gate metric rises: `card_rule_copies` falls 93 -> 70 on the head's instrument and 72 -> 70 on main's.

## Red checks

none: no PR exists yet for this head.

## Unpinned sites

The `tools/audit/archscore/metrics/card.py` sites are pinned by `tests/arch_score.py`'s `card_template_spellings`, which are value checks on `card_rule_copies`; M1 and M2 above are its in-tree mutants. The card's new helpers under `custom_components/` are pinned by `tests/card.mjs`, which drives `quietOverlapProblem`, `storageKey`, `smoothLine`, `steppedLine`, `removeEdge` and `evaluate`, and by `mutation-autofix`'s lane.

3180.body:
R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-3. main's required `gate` has been red on every push from 8f286293b on `tests / ci-ratchet`: `GREW critical_path_minutes: 40.817 (budget 34.267, band 1.3)`. 8f286293b is a diff of seven `dev/programme/delivery/*.md` rows, which cannot move CI work.

**What was measured.** Runner queueing is not the cause: `run_minutes` already removes each job's queue. No job's work grew either. Each heavy lane draws hosted runners of different speed on the same work. On a slow/quick pair of `fast` logs (c3a279e32 against c7aa12165), both running the same 31 scripts on 3 lanes, the per-script ratio had a median of 1.85 (range 1.6–2.9), and the CPU-bound reference solve read 45.0 ms against 18.8 ms. The fleet is **not two-speed**: over the 40 runs this PR carries, `tests / closures` reads 1117–1613 s, 2040–2401 s, and values in between. The critical path is a max over three ~18-minute lanes, so the median of per-run paths sat on slow draws.

**Fix: change the statistic, not raise the budget.** `critical_path_minutes` is now `window_work_minutes` over the newest `PUSH_WINDOW` (16) push runs:
- Each job is priced at its fastest **`success`** run in the window. A run under a third of the job's window **median** did other work (for example a consumed proof) and never prices the job.
- Prices are summed along each run's own critical chain (`run_chain`), and the longest chain is kept.
- A record keeps the largest value any 16 consecutive runs of a wider window read.

**Repair round 2** (review of 563c8e6db, `claim-refuted`). The round-1 floor was keyed on the window **maximum**. One run of a lane above 3x its fastest lifted the floor over every genuine fast run, which moved the grade +6.95 with no work grown.
- The floor is now the median of the job's `success` runs.
- Cancelled and failed jobs never price, and a ran job with no conclusion refuses.
- The round-1 claim "a slow host draw moves it only if every one of 16 runs drew slow" was false. The docstring now states what the minimum costs:
  - Losing the fastest draws reprices the job on a mid host.
  - 15 of 16 runs drawing slow moves the grade as growth would.
  - Growth reads only once it fills most of the window.

Candidates measured on the same 40 runs with the replay's perturbations. The figures are a scratch run of `replay.py`'s arms with the pricing rank swapped. Only A and B are in the committed harness: A is its `retired` arm and B is production.

| statistic | 25-window range | 3.2x outlier on `fast` | +300 s on closures, all 16 runs | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: max-keyed floor, minimum price (round 1) | 20.817–22.0 | **+6.95** | +2.283 | lost: one outlier moves it |
| **B: median-keyed floor over `success`, minimum price** | 19.967–21.983 | **+0.0** | +3.233 | **taken** |
| C: same floor, second-fastest price | 21.95–27.7 | +0.0 | **+0.0** | lost: blind to closures growth (a mid-host `fast` price dominates the chain) |
| D: same floor, lower-quartile price | 23.283–30.583 | +0.0 | **+0.0** | lost: same blindness, wider spread |
| M: same floor, median price | 33.008–40.583 | +0.0 | +5.0 | lost: reads the host draw again (the original red) |

B is the reviewer's variant. Measured here, it reproduces the reviewer's figures: 20.75 unmoved under the outlier, and +3.23 under +300 s on every closures run.

**Detection lag, disclosed (k = the newest runs carrying the growth; new / retired round-1 statistic):**
- +300 s on `tests / closures`: k=1, 4, 8 read +0.0/+0.0; k=12 reads +1.383/+1.383; k=15 and 16 read +3.233/+2.283.
- +300 s on `tests / fast (3.14)`: nothing moves until k=15, which reads +5.0/+4.05.

The red lands 12–16 merges after the cause. The retired median-of-8 moved at k=8 (reviewer's measurement), so the lag roughly doubles. That is the price of reading work instead of host draw.

**Slow fleet, disclosed:** when every fast draw in the newest 15 runs is made 1.9x slower, the grade moves +6.417 (closures), +6.95 (fast) and +5.167 (arch-instrument). A minimum prices the fastest host the window drew; no candidate above both ignores this and still detects growth on every lane.

Fix review: blocked 563c8e6db0eec229e3d5b402c263092722905f31 claim-refuted: one run of a heavy lane above 3x its window-fastest lifts the other-work floor over every fast run and moves the grade +6.95 min past the 1.3 band with no work grown

Round 1. Head measured: 563c8e6db0eec229e3d5b402c263092722905f31 (authored code head 27d410595), merge base c3a279e3252a8b57bb00b5a677318cd4fe20387f, origin/main unmoved. `git diff <merge-base>...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` empty: contract current.

## Block

The body and the new `window_work_minutes` docstring claim the grade reads work, not host speed: "a job that drew a slow host does not move it unless it drew one in every run of the window" / "A slow host draw moves it only if every one of 16 runs drew slow". Planted on the real 16-run window (the 40 newest ci.yml push runs on main, gathered at this review, `ev/runs40.json`), that is false:

- One outlier. The newest run's `tests / fast (3.14)` set to 3.2x the window's fastest `fast` run (one slow or hung draw, nothing else changed): grade 21.717 -> 28.667, +6.95 min, GREW on 22.0 + 1.3. The cause is `floor = max(seen) * OTHER_WORK_FRACTION`: the floor keys on the window **maximum**, the least robust order statistic, so a single slow run past 3x the fastest re-classifies every genuine fast run as "other work" and prices the job on a slow draw. The same shape is already in the data on a lane off the critical chain: `tests / coverage` max 3070 s (a failed run, a9c149289) puts its floor at 1023 s and excludes completed runs of 690-901 s.
- 15 of 16 slow. Each fast draw of `tests / closures` in the newest 15 runs made slow (x1.9, slow draws untouched): 21.717 -> 28.133 (+6.4); `fast` -> 28.667; `arch-instrument` -> 25.933. The fleet is not two-speed (closures reads 1117, 1234, 1245, 1306, 1449, 1608, 1613 s ... 2401 s), so losing the single fastest run reprices on a mid host; "every one of 16 runs drew slow" assumes a two-speed draw the data do not show.
- With the floor taken off the window median instead of the maximum, and only `success` job conclusions pricing, the same single 3.2x outlier moves nothing on any of the three lanes (20.75 -> 20.75) while +300 s on every closures run still moves it +3.23 (ev/perturb_oldmedian_variant.txt; my variant, not a prescription). The repair is local to `window_work_minutes`.

This is the false-red class this PR exists to remove (host draw read as growth), reintroduced through one outlier rather than a median. The self-test pins the floor only against a low "other work" run; it has no high-outlier case, which is the cheap detector the body's own Red-checks section prescribes (feed the statistic the same work with one host far slower; require the grade not to move).

## Findings

- Detection lag, undisclosed: real growth moves a window-minimum only once every pre-growth fast run has aged out. +300 s on `tests / closures` in only the newest k runs reads 21.717 at k = 1, 4, 8; 23.1 at k = 12; 24.95 at k = 15-16 (`fast`: no move until k = 15). The body's planted perturbation adds +300 s to every run of the window, which hides this. The retired median-of-8 also lagged (closures +300 moved only at k = 8), so it is a doubling, not a new defect, but the red now lands 12-16 merges after the cause; the body and docstring should state it. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-3
- `critical_path_minutes_band` 1.3 was measured on the retired statistic and not re-measured: the new statistic's own window-to-window spread is 19.95-22.0 per the body (2.05) and 20.817-22.0 over the 25 windows of my 40 runs. Recording at the window maximum makes 1.3 above it a plausible margin, but no measurement in the body says so. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-3
- Cancelled and failed jobs price: `_walk` drops only `skipped`, so a cancelled job truncated above a third of the window maximum would set the job's price low (under-reads the grade, and a record taken over it records too low). No instance moved the grade in the 40 runs (planted: one closures run cancelled at 45% -> no move, because a faster complete run was present). Carry: R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-3
- No committed harness exercises the critical-path statistic on real runs: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_u9a_ratchet_nulls.py`'s critical-path arm refuses at both ends ("carries no jobs list"), per the body. The figures here come from my own instrument (ev/gather.py, an*.py, pert*.py), disclosed as mine. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-3

## Evidence

Chains are prelude->closures|fast->ci-ratchet in most runs. Queueing is removed by run_minutes. I did not re-read the per-script wall-clock tables or the 45.0/18.8 ms solve lines: not re-derived.

3181.body:
Repair round 3 of #3181 (R10-CI-RUNNER-FIXES), answering the blocked verdict on 3339aa92b: the lane report's new `>>> ENDED BEFORE ITS SUMMARY:` line was not read by `merge_train.py` FAILED_SCRIPT, so `culprit()` named no script for a proof job whose script crashed before its summary.

Reader fix, and why this one: FAILED_SCRIPT now accepts `>>> (?:FAILED|ENDED BEFORE ITS SUMMARY): `. Chosen over appending the wording after a `>>> FAILED: <label>` prefix because it is a one-token change in the one reader that needs it, leaves the plain FAILED line byte-identical for every other reader (quiet.sh strips `^>>> FAILED: ` to get a bare label and would otherwise carry the suffix into its failed-script list), and keeps the two outcomes distinguishable in the log.

## Head
`cd88b3fc3f68f7748bfd173612c38eff05fc4c4c` merges main `783d8dc` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`bb730c1eeeb63880bc42336f347f6587564a57b1` merges the authored code head `4f379445e4c4a8f0ef9a001b5b96d4aa2d451644` and then merges origin/main `8e90d8144` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

Code head 4f379445e4c4a8f0ef9a001b5b96d4aa2d451644 (repair commit 3173cce2d156676ebffc2d49d752d0a107f9f630 on PR head 3339aa92b6a60e6492263da1a6b6dd5efaa39b64, plus a merge of origin/main fad43b0471b9cef3c563d2c2ae1eab3d87a34190, which had moved; the merge brought no change to tests/run.sh or tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py). `tools/pr/prepr.sh` re-ran at this head after that merge with PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1: rc=0. Partial delivery stands: carry 0 (actions: write dispatch step) is NOT built and stays in the roster carry list. Carry: dismissed: statement of scope, not a finding
Roster numbering (1-based, as the review packet counts): Carry 1 = brief carry 0 (the actions: write dispatch step, NOT built, see Forward-carry); Carry 2 = brief carry 1 (run.sh ENDED BEFORE ITS SUMMARY, done in round 1, its reader and call site pinned in this round); Carry 3 = brief carry 2 (closure.py `--cached`, done in round 1, unchanged here). Carry: dismissed: numbering note, not a finding

## Mutation proof
Fixture: `_failed_marker_self_test` in tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py, run by `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`. It lifts `SUMMARY_LINE`, `ended_before_summary` and the report if/else out of tests/run.sh, drives them on a crash log and a failed-check log (rc=1), and feeds each printed line to FAILED_SCRIPT.
- Mutant 1, reader reverted to `>>> FAILED: `: `1 failed`, check "FAILED_SCRIPT names the script from the crash line and from the failed-check line".
- Mutant 3 (the verdict's), run.sh if/else reverted to the one-line `echo ">>> FAILED: $label"`: `1 failed`, check "run.sh's lane report still has the SUMMARY_LINE / ended_before_summary / if-else this check lifts" (the lift finds no if/else).
- Mutant 4, the negation dropped from `ended_before_summary`: `2 failed`, the crash-prints-ENDED and failed-keeps-FAILED checks.
- Each mutant restored from a byte copy afterwards.

## Null control
Unmutated head: `merge_train self-test: 442 checks, 0 failed`, the four new checks ok. The failed-check log prints exactly `>>> FAILED: python3 tests/entities.py`, not the ENDED line.

## Figures
- Self-test: `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test | tail -1` prints `merge_train self-test: 442 checks, 0 failed` at the code head before the origin/main merge (the merge touches neither file; CI's governance self-test is the authority after it).
- Verdict's harness, both ends: evidence/failed_script_regex.txt applied to the new line returned `[]` at 3339aa92b; FAILED_SCRIPT.findall on the line run.sh now prints returns `['tests/entities.py']` (the fixture's third check).
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` at 3173cce2d: ALL 2603 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED (run before the origin/main merge; CI reruns it). `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED. Scoped gate: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `MODE: FULL` (tests.yml is a gate file), left to CI.
- Toolchain: numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1 equal tests/requirements-ci.txt; no golden was run, CI is the authority.
- Class enumeration, rule: `grep -rIn ">>> FAILED\|>>> ENDED\|ENDED BEFORE" .` over the tree (null control: the same grep matches tests/run.sh:418, the known writer). Every hit:
  - tests/run.sh:418 (writer, serial `run()`, only when JOBS<=1): unchanged, serial runs never print ENDED.
  - tests/run.sh:811 and :813 (writers, lane report): pinned by the new fixture.
  - tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py FAILED_SCRIPT (the only live reader of the lane line): fixed here, pinned.
  - merge_train.py fake-gh job log `>>> FAILED: "$PYTHON" tests/ratchet.py` (self-test fixture, job 11): still a valid FAILED line, left.
  - tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py:3633 (test fixture text `>>> FAILED: tests/stress.py`): a fixture of the plain line, not a reader; left.
  - dev/audit/rounds/round10/intake/quiet.sh:61 (live reader, `grep -E '^>>> FAILED: '`): runs the gate with GATE_JOBS=1 (serial), where only run()'s FAILED line exists, so it never sees ENDED; unaffected, left.
  - dev/audit/rounds/round3/D11/conformance_raw.json, round4/quiet-window.md, round7/QUIET.md, round6/D13/fixtures/*.json, dev/archive/handoff/r9-f2-solver-4/ev/gate_round1_head.log: recorded measurements, not readers.

## Red checks
No check is concluded red at this head (CI has not run on it). The ancestry reds the contract lists:
- `tests / fast (3.14)` at 241f47e62: 1 of 2603 entity checks failed, "every `bash -c` / `sh -c` a check runs carries errexit", naming the new site `tests/entities.py:_gl_ended_before_summary`. Countermeasure: none built; the detector exists and the gap was skipping it.
- `tests / nightly-status`: inherited from main, grades main (`NIGHTLY FAILED: slow failed 1 night ago`, scheduled run 41555367389, predating this branch); the diff touches no nightly lane and it is not required by main-protect. Nothing to repair here.

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked 3339aa92b6a60e6492263da1a6b6dd5efaa39b64 class-open: tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py FAILED_SCRIPT no longer names a crashed script

bus-nonce: c1959f04865f382337a99ea2f216d677

## Round
First fix-review round of #3181 (R10-CI-RUNNER-FIXES), head 3339aa92b6a60e6492263da1a6b6dd5efaa39b64. The entities.py errexit repair round (code head 554d06a90) is included in this review. The role files under dev/governance/roles/ match between the merge base and origin/main (the three-dot diff is empty).

## Block
In lane mode, the CI default (tests.yml sets no GATE_JOBS, so run.sh uses min(nproc, 3) lanes), the diff changes the `>>> FAILED: <label>` line in tests/run.sh's report (tests/run.sh:809-815). A non-zero script whose log holds no summary line now prints `>>> ENDED BEFORE ITS SUMMARY: <label> (...)` instead. In lane mode the old `>>> FAILED:` line is the only one a script gets: run() prints its own `>>> FAILED:` only when JOBS<=1 (tests/run.sh:417-419).
The marker is parsed downstream. tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py:695 `FAILED_SCRIPT = re.compile(r">>> FAILED: .*?(tests/...)")` is how `culprit()` (merge_train.py:2670-2693) names the failing scripts in a red proof job, so that it can attribute the batch entry that owns them. At this head the regex returns [] for the new line (ev/failed_script_regex.txt). So a proof that is red only because a script crashed before its summary, which is exactly the host-dependent case this carry exists to surface, now attributes no culprit. With more than two entries kept, merge_train.py:2862-2870 then falls back to proving every all-but-one set side by side, which costs extra CI runs, where before it dropped the one owning entry.
The diff does not change this consumer, and the body does not disposition it. The body's Figures section describes the new line's shape but names no enumeration of the line's readers. A `grep -rn ">>> FAILED"` over the tree returns merge_train.py:695 (live), dev/audit/rounds/round10/intake/quiet.sh:61 (serial GATE_JOBS=1, so unaffected) and test fixtures in orchestrator_tick.py and merge_train.py.
Cheapest repair: make FAILED_SCRIPT also accept `>>> ENDED BEFORE ITS SUMMARY: `, and pin it with a merge_train self-test fixture that holds the new line. Or keep the `>>> FAILED: <label>` prefix and append the distinct wording after it.

## Findings
- Follow-up: the run.sh call site that picks between ENDED BEFORE ITS SUMMARY and FAILED (tests/run.sh:809-815) is pinned by no check. The entities.py pin lifts only SUMMARY_LINE and ended_before_summary, and no file other than tests/run.sh names `ENDED BEFORE`. Reverting the if/else to the old one-line `>>> FAILED` therefore survives the suite (ev/run_sh_pin_mutants.txt, mutant 3). The repair round should pin the report line itself, which the FAILED_SCRIPT repair can share. Carry: R10-CI-RUNNER-FIXES
- Residual: the group's first carry (the owner's "Build it now" item, plan-regain card 9: an edit run exits without holding a runner, and the code run's gate re-dispatches the body units) is not built at this head. The body says so and gives its reason (a new `actions: write` dispatch step in the read-only `gate` job, on a code-owned path that cannot be exercised locally). It stays verbatim in this group's roster carry list on origin/main (dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json, group R10-CI-RUNNER-FIXES, carry[0]). The orchestrator must not close the group when this PR merges. Carry: R10-CI-RUNNER-FIXES

3182.body:
R10-PARTLOAD-PRICING: the residue of R10-COP-PARTLOAD (#2872, #3006). The brief says to measure first and to change a cost law only where the error is material. This pull request does three things:

- It closes the last inline small-buffer fallback (carry 1).
- It lands the instrument that measures carries 2 and 3, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_partload_pricing.py`, with a zero-derate null on every arm.
- It re-measures carry 0 at this merge base.

It changes no cost law. Carry 6 and the decision on carry 2 wait, as stated under each carry below.

**Carry 1, built.** `ThermalModel._substeps_and_loss`'s two-zone throttled branch had its own copy of the `c_buf < 1e-6 -> 0.04` fallback. Its comment says it mirrors `_simulate_step_two_zone`, and that function has called `_buffer_capacity` since #3006. Now this branch calls `_buffer_capacity(p)` too. The predicate and the value are the same, and the substep counts are identical bit for bit (Null control). This was the last copy (Figures, Class enumeration). The carry names `optimizer.py`, but the copy was in `thermal_model.py`.

**Carry 2: linear valuations under a convex cost. Measured, not segmented.** The scenarios are #3006 round 2's: `r10_cop_partload.py`'s 16 installs on its spread and flat days, at d=0 and at the central plant's derate d=0.112.

- The hot-water LP's objective `price * E / cop`, evaluated on the plan it published, under-prices the derated per-step cost by at most 0.173/day (spread) and 0.267/day (flat). The hot-water cost those plans pay is up to 8.07 and 7.01/day, so the error is at most about 3.8 % of the figure it prices. That is below what I would call material for a planner whose COP law itself carries larger errors. I did not segment the LP.
- `_terminal_cost` and `_deferred_energy_cost` state no refill rate, so their error is a range, not a number:
  - At a modulation-floor refill it is 0.
  - At a max-power refill it is the figure times `d / (1 - d)` (12.6 % at d=0.112): up to 4.37/day for the terminal and 2.13/day for the deferred figure.
  - Which end is true depends on a refill rate the tree does not state. Choosing one is the D0 decision the carry reserves for "a later D0 pass on `_plan_dhw_min_cost` and `_terminal_cost`". I made no change, and the measurement goes forward to that pass (Forward-carry).
- The wood advisor's pump-heat price (`wood_fuel.cheaper_hour_count`, `_scan_wood_night`) has the same secant factor, `P_r / heat_per_cop_kw(P_r) - 1`, at whatever rate the pump would run. It was not measured separately. It goes to the same destination.

**Carry 3: mean-draw pricing. Measured; no change.** Each production cost law was re-run with its module's `power_for_heat_per_cop_kw` swapped, for that call only, for run-power pricing `E * P_run / heat_per_cop_kw(P_run)`. `P_run` is the published hot-water plan's own peak draw (4.0 kW on every hot-water cell).

- **The setpoint sweep's chosen setpoint moved in 0 of 16 cells** at d=0.112 (8 hot-water cells, each on 2 price days). This holds by construction: `P_run` does not depend on the candidate, so run-power pricing scales every candidate's cost by the same factor and cannot reorder them. Only the displayed `cost_per_day` would change.
- **The always-hot baseline's cost rises by up to +0.673/day** against a baseline of about 23/day (+2.9 %). It rises in the same direction on every derated cell, and never falls. The baseline today is the cheaper of the two laws, so `predicted_savings` errs low, which is the conservative direction the baseline's own docstring states for the wood coil.
- Neither change is material to a decision, so neither cost law changes. The carry calls this a design change. Without a decision that moves, I judged it not worth making.

**Carry 0: live buffer store CPU. Re-measured; no fix built.** `r10_buffer_store.py bench 3` at this head (production code identical to the merge base except carry 1's bitwise-identical line) gives:

- owner shape: median 1.57 s, max 2.853 s;
- null: median 0.797 s;
- ratio 1.97x. #3006 measured 2.44x at `507a9ec26`.

The null differs from the owner shape in two levers, flat prices and no buffer, so the ratio is not a one-lever figure. The 272 s owner-box outlier does not reproduce here: max 2.85 s on a 4-core x86_64 container. R10-OVERBOOK-RESIDUAL refutes the #2499 residual. The over-booking was in the reference, not in the plan. The harness's DP reference (`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_demand_overbook.py`, `_dp_reference`) priced comfort against one flat band, `target_temp` 21 with floor `min_temp` 20, at every step. The solve prices the day/night schedule that `OptimizationConfig.get_comfort_temp` / `get_temp_bounds` return: target 19.5 and floor 19.5 outside 07:00-22:00. So the reference read the night setback the solve is allowed as a breach and a pull deficit, and it priced the plan's pre-heating ahead of 07:00 as waste. With the reference reading the solve's own per-step schedule from `HeatPumpOptimizer._build_comfort_bounds`, the one site that builds it, the flat-price arm's plan reads plan_kwh at the DP's and the plan's cost equals the DP optimum. The owner arm's plan costs less than the relaxed DP on the same objective.

No production code changes. The diff corrects the instrument and adds the cross-check that would have caught it: `_production_cost` scores the plan on the optimizer's own full objective (`_solve_objectives`, captured from a real `optimize`), and the row prints it as `prod_cost` beside the reconstruction's `plan_cost`. When the two disagree, the reference measures a different problem.

Refs #2499. The group's roster entry (`R10-OVERBOOK-RESIDUAL` on `handoff/audit-r10-roster`) lists #2499 in `fixes`, but main's in-tree roster does not carry that entry yet. Until it lands, `tools/pr/prepr.sh` step 7's preflight, which derives its intended list from `dev/programme/rosters`, refuses a closing keyword on that issue because no group there names #2499 in `fixes`. The closing keyword is the orchestrator's to restore once the roster merges.

Carry 1 is answered by refutation. That is the brief's carry from R10-STORE-RACES / #2887, null 11.78 against 9.88 and owner_i01 5.37 against 3.88. Both arms were re-run at this merge base before any figure here was quoted, and `## Figures` shows them at both ends. The flat-price arm now reads plan_kwh within the DP's. The owner arm's remaining kWh difference costs no more on the same objective, so it is not price-side either. The precondition on `valve_charge_demand` does not bind here, because both arms are unvalved and this diff quotes no savings figure.

## Head

`02d6df06cbf8fd7d0387a3dca40161c219b51d8c` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3183.md`. The authored code head is `91a7c9c2e727c59e523af81faae212dd3aa17b50`.

Code head `91a7c9c2e727c59e523af81faae212dd3aa17b50`, cut from origin/main `c3a279e3252a8b57bb00b5a677318cd4fe20387f`, which is also the merge base. ## Mutation proof

The fix is the harness's comfort schedule. Mutant: the per-step `targets, floors, ceilings, bands` in `_dp_reference` replaced by the flat `cfg.target_temp` / `cfg.min_temp` / `cfg.max_temp` band they replaced, from a scratch copy, run as `--one null --dp`. The mutant reproduces the base reading exactly: `dp_learned` gap 0.2601, dp_kwh 8.62 against plan_kwh 10.74. Its own cross-check flags it: `plan_cost` 20.384 against `prod_cost` 17.801. Restored, the head reads gap 0.0 with `plan_cost` = `prod_cost` = 17.801. No `custom_components/` line changes, so there are no production mutants and no golden claims.

## Null control

The unmodified tree (origin/main's harness, sha1 `f0575c58b587d9a41e922fb5393e1a30a7ddba0b`) at the merge base: the null arm reads `dp_learned` dp_kwh 8.62 against plan_kwh 10.74 (gap 0.2601) and `dp_true` dp_kwh 9.00 (gap 0.2928). The owner_i01 arm reads dp_kwh 3.75 against plan_kwh 5.27 (gap 0.158; `dp_true` gap 0.1598). The plan is the control for the reference: plan_kwh, plan/deliv, the learned scale and the per-day series are identical at both ends (null 10.74, 1.165, 0.98; owner 5.27, 0.854, 0.616), because only the reference changed. The perturbation that shows the corrected reference still detects a worse plan is the base reference's own DP schedule. Scored on the production objective it costs 19.744 against the plan's 17.801. So the plan beats it, and the flat-band "optimum" was not optimal on the solve's objective. That figure comes from a scratch probe and not from an in-tree instrument. The in-tree equivalent is the `prod_cost` cross-check above.

## Figures

All rows: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_demand_overbook.py --one <arm> --dp`. Head harness sha1 `edc0b3c076a8fd4ad62db1defcb5a8a79ddc0281`; base sha1 `f0575c58b587d9a41e922fb5393e1a30a7ddba0b`. A field name below is the name the harness prints. gap = (plan_cost - dp_cost) / dp_cost on the DP's relaxed objective, and is >= 0 up to the (room, slab) grid's interpolation error.

- null (flat prices, unvalved), base: dp_learned dp_kwh 8.62, plan_kwh 10.74, gap 0.2601; dp_true dp_kwh 9.00, gap 0.2928.
- null, head: dp_learned dp_kwh 10.75, plan_kwh 10.74, gap 0.0, plan_cost 17.801 = prod_cost 17.801; dp_true dp_kwh 11.00, plan_kwh 10.74, gap 0.0. This is the brief's close condition: the flat-price arm's plan_kwh is within the DP's.

The extra energy buys pull and terminal value that the objective prices, so it is not over-booking against the reference. A negative gap is the DP grid's interpolation error, which is the bound the docstring states.
- plan/deliv, the closed-loop ratio the carry quoted, reads 1.165 (null) and 0.854 (owner) at both ends. It compares two 12-hour plans with the energy one day delivered under receding-horizon replanning. It is not measured against any optimum, and its sign differs between two flat-price arms, so it is not an over-booking measure. It is left as printed.
