What changed:
- `footprint._chain` counts the branches of a conditional-expression TREE: every `IfExp` reachable through `body` as well as `orelse` (`(a if q else b) if p else c` is three branches, as its nested if/else spells). `_extras` skips every `IfExp` nested directly under another, so the tree is charged once at its root.
- `footprint._bound`: a tuple target holding a starred element against a display value reads the names it binds. `a, *b = e1, e2, e3` reads 2, as `a = e1; b = [e2, e3]` does (it read 3).
- Plant 54 (`planted/redteam/54_footprint_ifexp_body_chain.py`), the reviewer's `x = ((A) if (p) else (B)) if (p) or (q) else (C)` respelling of each if/elif/else of the coordinator: recorded GAME, NULL, admissible.
- Plant 55 (`planted/redteam/55_footprint_boolop_control.py`), `if p: x = A / else: x = B` respelled `x = (p) and (A) or (B)`: it reads IMPROVES (admissible), so it is recorded KNOWN-OPEN through `planted/cases.py` `KNOWN_OPEN`, not closed. The disposition is in ABOUT.md (design choice, below).
- `tests/arch_score.py`: four new rows of the packed/plain table (the body-arm tree, a tree in both arms, `a, *b` and `*a, b`).
- ABOUT.md dispositions, each with the reason: `for` over a literal of tuples and its `async for` twin (over-count, safe direction; the loop body is written once); `p and A or B` (attempt 55, KNOWN-OPEN); a comprehension used as a loop over a literal (open by design, not planted: a comprehension is also a mapping).

Design choice, said where it is made: counting a `BoolOp` as control flow was not built. `a or b` and `a and b` are idioms and no structural test separates control flow from them, so a counter would charge ordinary code; the respelling is the same bounded 3-to-1 as the lone `a if p else y` already disposed in ABOUT.md. The alternative (count `A and B or C` as a two-branch tree) was rejected for that reason; a class fix flips attempt 55 and `tests/arch_score.py` then refuses until it is re-recorded.

R10-FLY-REPLAY-MASK repairs the empty-replay refusal (`seal` refusing "entity id(s) not masked to a role or a hashed id"). The mask now takes roles from the same entry keys and items that `sanitise` keeps, through the one predicate `_entry_shape`. Round 3 of the repair: round 2's `prepr` step 6d refused the body for omitting two unpinned `replay_doc.py` sites.

Closes #3219's finding R10-FLY-REPLAY-MASK.

## Head

`2ecd546699d8c7f748316660c9b5d2164dc70a9e` merges main `cd0dd16` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`2cfa51a43dea225ad55adf1ac3826f58da613655` is the PR head: the bot commit `ci: pin killed mutants` on top of `aca500910b8917fd41516f5f290c6a18f1727b8b`, the reviewed head (`review_carry.py` reads CARRY between them). Merge base with `origin/main` is `662b29669ec5beb6773fa8b62ac98f2b020be90e` (measured with `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`). `prepr.sh` was run once, on the handoff head.

## What changed

- `_role_claims` (`replay_doc.py`): with `conf`, each kept entry value goes through `_entry_shape(key, value)`, the function `sanitise` applies, so the roles `entity_roles` hands out cannot disagree with what `_unmasked` re-derives from the sanitised entry. Alternatives: (a) delete the list filter only: leaves `_entities` lists with non-id items refused; (b) a second hand-copied `endswith("_entities")` predicate: duplicates the concept and can drift; both lost to the shared function.
- Round 3: the `if value is _DROP: continue` that followed the `_entry_shape` call is deleted. Its mutant (`if False:`) survived `replay.mask_checks()`, and no check can kill it: the only consumer of `_role_claims` is `entity_roles.claim`, which ignores any value that is not a `str` matching `ENTITY_ID`, and a `_DROP` is a bare `object()`. The branch was an equivalent mutant, so I took the deletion over a check that cannot fail (owner-directed alternative was a new check reaching the skip; it cannot exist for this reason, shown by the mutant below). Design choice: `_role_claims` yields the sentinel and the consumer's id test passes it over; the comment at the call says so.
- Checks in `tests/replay.py` (`mask_seam_checks`, `_conf_reaches_writers_checks`) from round 2, unchanged: `mask:id_in_list_under_a_kept_key_beside_a_non_id_seals_masked`, `mask:id_in_list_under_an_entities_key_beside_a_non_id_seals_masked`, `mask:build_export_passes_conf_to_document`, `mask:debugger_replay_document_passes_conf_to_document`.

## Mutation proof

Harness: `replay.mask_checks()` (PYTHONPATH `tests/hastub:.`, `tests` and `tools/replay` on `sys.path`), each mutant one line, restored after. Null control first.

- null at this head: 23 checks, none failed.
- `if conf is not None:` (the `_entry_shape` guard) turned `if False:`: killed by `mask:id_in_list_under_an_entities_key_beside_a_non_id_seals_masked`.
- `value = _entry_shape(str(key), value)` replaced by `pass`: killed by the same check.
- the deleted `if value is _DROP:` guard, measured at `1e25dcd8` as `if False:`: 0 failed (survived). Equivalent by the consumer argument above, so deleted rather than pinned.
- earlier mutants of the `conf=conf` call sites (`mask_ids`, `document`, `debugger.py`, `tools/replay/export.py`) are untouched by this round's one-hunk change.

## Null control

The base refuses `legacy_probe_entity` configured off the allowlist; the blocked round-1 head refused the kept-key list `after_save: ["abc", <id>]` the base sealed; this head seals both, and `mask:planted_unmasked_id_still_refused` still refuses a planted unmasked id.

## Escaped class on the live export of 2026-11-04

I cannot read the owner's live export and did not. The reachable class, by reasoning and not measured: an entity id configured under an entry key off the installed allowlist (a key `sanitise` drops); `entity_roles` gave it a role from the dropped key, `seal` re-derived a different role from the sanitised entry and refused the whole replay. No id is quoted anywhere in this diff, tests or body.

Carry 1 (roster item 31ee5e06, the empty `debug.manifest.replay` refused for an unmasked id): answered by this fix at the seam above; the owner's export itself was not read, so whether the refused id is this class is by reasoning, not measured.

## Figures

- `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path[:0]=['tests','tests/hastub','tools/replay']; import replay; r=replay.mask_checks(); print(len(r), [n for n,ok,w in r if not ok])"` with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:.`: prints the count and failing names (every `mask:` check).

## Unpinned sites

- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/replay_doc.py:535 GUARD_OFF (`if conf is not None:`, the `_entry_shape` guard in `_role_claims`): killed by `mask:id_in_list_under_an_entities_key_beside_a_non_id_seals_masked`; pinned by `mutation-autofix` after the push.

Red on main's ancestry at the merge base `662b29669ec5beb6773fa8b62ac98f2b020be90e`, not caused by this diff: it is the CPU-time cost ratio on a shared runner, and this diff touches neither `tools/replay/` nor the cost budget (`replay_doc.py` is the diagnostics export masking, not the replayed solver). ## Block

- The body's mutant 2 does not die. At this head, replacing `value = [v for v in value if isinstance(v, str) and ENTITY_ID.match(v)]` in `_role_claims` with `pass` (the same as the body's `if False else value`) leaves `replay.mask_checks()` at 19/19 passing. `mask:id_under_list_beside_a_non_id_seals_masked` is not killed, though the body says it is. The cause is that the check's key, `room_sensor_entities`, is not in `conf`, and `conf` contains no key ending `_entities` at all. So the key guard (mutant 1) skips the list before the filter is reached, and the list filter is unreachable under the real allowlist. The body's "Mutation proof" and "Unpinned sites" entries for lines 539 and 540 do not hold.
- The filter is also the wrong shape. `sanitise` (`_entry_shape`) filters list items only under keys ending `_entities`, but `_role_claims` filters every list once `conf` is passed. Plant a list holding a non-id beside an id under any kept conf key (for example `after_save: ["abc", "sensor.zzz_probe"]`). The base seals it, and this head refuses with "1 entity id(s) not masked to a role or a hashed id": the empty-replay symptom on a new class (ev/plant.txt). Today the config flow writes no list-valued key (scout read of config_flow.py, const.py and entry_config.py), so this is latent, but it is a regression in the very refusal this PR fixes.
- To clear it: drop the list filter, which is dead under `conf`, or make it the same predicate as `_entry_shape` (only keys ending `_entities`). Then give it a check that reaches it (an `_entities` key inside `conf`) and a check for the planted non-`_entities` list above.

## Findings

- Follow-up: the body names the escaping class by construction ("I could not read the live export"). The brief asks for the class seen on the 2026-11-04 v7.1.1 export. The off-allowlist entity key is the only seam reachable under the real conf, which makes it the likely class, but no one has matched it against that export. The re-cut should state this, or derive the shape from the bundle. Carry: R10-FLY-REPLAY-MASK
- Follow-up: the regression and the dead filter described under Block. Carry: R10-FLY-REPLAY-MASK

The owner's month row read nonsense on a valved house with a wood tank (tvofi, 2026-11-04): November's reference far below the meter, a percent clipped at -100. The settlement booked the thermostat's first step of a plan re-made every interval, and behind a valve that step read the stores' transient. ## Null control

- The zero-demand probe is not vacuous: on the head the held tank stays at its measured 37.5 C, and the mutant at line 595 sets it to 21.0 C (`valve_hold_temperature` at a need of 0), measured by a direct call before the check was written. At 30 C outdoor and 800 W/m2 the steady demand is 0 on every step, so `total` is exactly 0.0 and the line-5552 mutant divides by it.
- The feasible-start check asserts its own precondition: the reference peak must exceed the pump (`max(_hz_baselines) > p_max`), so it cannot pass on a horizon where the clamp never bites. Over a 27-case probe (pump 3, 4 and 6 kW; -25, -15 and -5 C nights; 0, 400 and 900 W/m2 midday sun; manual valve), the reference peak reached 1.226x the pump at 3 kW, -25 C and 400 W/m2 (the check's case), and every start the solve was handed read at most 1.000x its bound at the head.
- The stamp check uses the literal 1.0 a v2 store holds on disk. The first-booking check beside it (`a month's first savings booking stamps the reference in force, once`) compares against the constant itself, which is why the CONST mutant survived it.
- Wood stand-in null: the 192-case differential drive below with the constant unchanged against itself is the head's own run; the mutant's run is the same driver with `optimizer._NO_WOOD_TANK_C = 1.0` set before any solve. The same 192 cases were also driven with the CLAMP_DROP mutant: 0 differ, and over those cases the seed never left [0, p_max], so that grid is the reason a targeted horizon was needed for the check.

R10-HANDOFF-PATH part 1 (triage `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch121.md#P386`, the owner's directive of 2026-11-04): a fixer's prepr is not repeated at open or update. Part 1 is P386's carry with roster carries 3 and 4 and no other; one checkout per pull request, exit 75, the retry and the `open_driver` repairs are part 2. Carry 9 is answered by #3089's merge.

- **The receipt.** `tools/pr/prepr.sh`'s `receipt_write`: a run with a body that ends rc=0 writes `<HEAD sha> <tree sha>` to `hpo-prepr-receipt` in the checkout's git dir. The main flow removes an earlier receipt first, so a failing run leaves none. `--body-check` and `--fill-red` exit before the main flow and write none. A run that sets any `PREPR_SKIP_*` except `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES` writes none, and neither does a run over a dirty tree.
- **The trailer.** In `tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh`, `prepr_trailer` adds `Prepr: <sha> <tree>` to the `handoff-body/<topic>` commit, under `Code:`. It does so only when the receipt's sha is the handoff's code head and its tree is that head's tree. Otherwise one line says that no trailer was written.
- **The verdict.** `tools/pr/app_push.sh --reuse`'s `reuse_verdict` sits beside `recarry_verdict` and `row_only_verdict` and fails closed. Every one of these must hold:
  - (a) the tip of `handoff-body/<topic>` carries exactly one `Prepr: C T` trailer;
  - (b) C's tree is T;
  - (c) C is in HEAD, and C merges cleanly with the live head and then with the origin/main commit HEAD holds, which is on main's first-parent chain;
  - (d) HEAD's tree is that merge's tree, or that tree plus this pull request's own row;
  - (e) HEAD carries no commit beyond C, the live head and main except that one row commit.

  When the verdict holds, prepr runs under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE=C`, and then `row_only_checks` runs. Otherwise the full prepr runs, exactly as today. One `app_push: REUSE:` line names which path ran and why. `open_pr.sh` p1 asks for `--reuse`. `update_pr.sh` asks for `--reuse` on every head that is not a row-only push.
- **What still runs, with no heavy slot.** Under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE`, prepr takes no slot. It still runs transport, ancestry reds, ref privacy, temp paths, no version edit, claim files, claims hygiene, layout guard, preflight, pr-body, figures, carry, unpinned sites and push order. `merged_steps` adds two checks on HEAD merged with origin/main: `tests/structure.py` (carry 4, in every run) and ci predict (in this mode only). The merged tree is HEAD itself when HEAD already holds main; otherwise it is the `merge-tree` result. The skip is not keyed to main standing still under a closure (`s6-batch95.md#P346`).

**Each step's input, checked before dropping it** (read from `tools/pr/prepr.sh`'s main flow). The triage's split was a reading, and the input check differs from it in four places:
- **transport: kept.** Not listed by the triage, but it reads the commits since the merge base, which the merge and the row add, and it costs 0.0 s.
- **push order: kept.** Not listed either; it reads the remote head ref.
- **claims register: dropped.** Not listed either. It reads `BASE...HEAD` paths against `CLAIMS_READS`, and that is the code's diff alone.
- **gate mode and diff mutants: dropped.** The first prints the scope of the code's diff. The second is report-only, and `MUTANT_CMD` is code-keyed.

The other drops read the code alone:
- `policy_lint`, `rules_sync`, `fragments`, `hooks`, `codeowners_gap`, `brief_lint`, `field coverage`, `register check`, `pinned graders`, `self-test`, `wave-script`, `no-copies` and `throwaway git` read the tree's corpus and its own scripts. Main's half of that corpus passed on main.
- `agreement lane` reads the first-parent subjects since the tag. The only new ones are the open's or update's automatic merge and the row, both shapes the full prepr already passes at every open today.
- `closures` is already `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES` at every open.

**Merge resolution.** The open refused this head (`91a75ed8`): `merging origin/main into 91a75ed8 conflicts` in `tools/pr/prepr.sh`, because main had moved by 23 commits. Main's three commits to `prepr.sh` since `af941ad4` are `8f6f0ea2f`, `18481fd52` and `1584530f3`. They add the lazy `take_slot`, `closures_owes_slot` and the early `## Head` arm, step 1a3 (P208). The change over the reviewed content is a merge of origin/main, `c0b082bc`, with one conflict, in `tools/pr/prepr.sh`. It is resolved with both sides kept. Main's step 1a3 runs first, right after the ancestry-reds arm 1a2: it is keyed to the body, so it also runs under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE`. Next come this branch's recorder cache and its `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` gate. Main's five lazy `take_slot` calls are in these steps: mutants, field coverage, self-test, closures and diff mutants. Mutants and field coverage are in the first code-keyed group, self-test in the second and diff mutants in the third. Closures is behind `elif [ -n "${REUSE:-}" ]`. So a reuse run still defines and takes no slot. No other file of this diff changed on main since `af941ad4`: `git diff af941ad4a origin/main -- tools/pr/app_push.sh tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh` is empty.

Alternatives:
- A separate check list in `app_push.sh` would have duplicated prepr's steps beside their owner. It lost to one mode of prepr's own flow.
- Reading the receipt from the body's prose is what the ruling had to do, and prose cannot be verified. A trailer on the body commit carries a sha and a tree that can be checked.

**Repair round 2** (the first fix review blocked `794fe6a7` on two defects, each letting a receipt skip a check the body says still runs):
- **The main flow's `merged_steps` call is pinned.** The `(a)` arm's real `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` prepr now runs with a body and asserts that one `merged structure` line and one `ci predict` line appear. Under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` that call is the only ci predict and the only `tests/structure.py` on HEAD merged with main, and the function-level arms (d) and (e) could not see it deleted.
- **The receipt names the HEAD the run started on.** `receipt_line` reads `<HEAD sha> <tree sha>` once, where the main flow starts (`RUN_START`, right after the early receipt removal). `receipt_write` gets it as a third argument and writes that line, never a fresh read. When HEAD or its tree differ at the end, it refuses through `step "receipt" 1`, so the run ends rc=1 and writes no receipt. When no start was read, it writes none. A commit landing mid-run is therefore code the receipt never claims.
- **The five follow-ups, one row each, in the self-tests already touched:** reuse_verdict's first-parent arm of (c) (real git: HEAD holding a side commit main merged); two `Prepr:` trailers; `row_only_checks` after the reduced prepr under `--reuse` (a copy whose `reuse_verdict` is a stub that reuses, so the wiring past a reusing verdict runs: prepr under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE`, then the body contract and the carry check, and a contract refusal stops the push); the early receipt removal (the `(a)` run plants a stale receipt and asserts it is gone); and body_push.sh's sha comparison (a receipt whose tree is the head's but whose sha is not).
- The unsigned-receipt finding stays as it is: P386 dismissed it.

Alternatives for the starting HEAD:
- Re-reading HEAD at the end and comparing it to `## Head` alone was rejected. A seat that moves both the code and the body mid-run, which is the reviewer's real run 2, passes that check.
- Taking a lock on HEAD for the length of the run was rejected. It is heavier, and it would still need the same comparison at the end.
- Writing the start line, after checking that it is unchanged, makes the receipt the measured HEAD by construction.

**Repair round 3.** The second fix review blocked `20d5aab0` on two defects:
- **`governance / instrument-self-tests` was red: pr_args.sh's fixtures had not been updated for the `--reuse` code push.** `bash tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh --self-test` gave `172 checks, 19 failed` at `20d5aab0`, and `0 failed` at base `8364e624`. There were three causes:
  - The stubs shifted only `--row-only`. Under `--reuse` their `$2` was the repository, not the worktree, so the stub pushes failed. That accounts for the race, row-close, kept-worktree and lock rows.
  - The open row and the two update null controls still expected no flag on the code push.
  - The pusher census found two new files naming `app_push.sh` with no disposition: comments in `body_push.sh` and `prepr.sh`.

  The repair:
  - Every stub drops either mode flag.
  - The open row now asserts `--reuse` on the code push and `--row-only` on the row push. Both update null controls assert `--reuse`, never `--row-only`. They stay meaningful: each still separates a new-code head from a row-only head, which `mut:rowonly` crosses.
  - Each runner now carries `--reuse` on a line of its own, so a mutant can delete it without deleting the push. In `open_pr.sh` that is `RU=--reuse  # mut:opreuse`, and the push takes `${RU-}`. Before, the marker sat on the whole p1 push line. In `update_pr.sh` it is `[ -n "$RO" ] || RO=--reuse  # mut:updreuse`, placed after the restored `RO=""; … || RO=--row-only  # mut:rowonly`. Each mutant has a row that kills it.
  - The census gives both files `mention` entries.
- **The mutation-vacuous condition (e).** One real-git row in app_push.sh's reuse block has the shape of the reviewer's F9: the clean merge of C and main plus two commits that net to no tree change. It asserts (e)'s refusal, `HEAD carries 2 commit(s) beyond code …`. The same head reset under those two commits reuses again, which is its null control.

Alternatives for (1):
- Reverting the code push to no flag would have restored the old fixtures and dropped P386's reuse at open and update. That is the feature this PR exists for.
- Keeping the marker on the whole push line would leave a mutant that deletes the push itself. The run would then stop at `pr_wait` for a reason other than the missing flag, which is a vacuous pin.

`0f6771a7a4b8ca1146d74b81e66bc5b357e45f9b` merges main `0ae75bf` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`fd0d130a7e040c64da4fcd93c1ca2aa2a2fc9f56` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Neither `dad3178d` nor `79f765e6` reaches a path under `tools/`, `.claude/` or `.github/`: `git diff --quiet fff00030 533b00b3 -- tools .claude .github` exits 0. So the self-tests of `app_push.sh` and `pr_args.sh`, taken at `fff00030`, were not re-run. Main's only commit to this diff's files is `3ec5178c`'s step 3e2 in `tools/pr/prepr.sh`, the machinery ratchet. `git diff --stat 6777ec33 3ec5178c -- tools/pr/prepr.sh tools/pr/app_push.sh tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh` prints only `tools/pr/prepr.sh | 9 +`, and `git diff --stat 8364e624 6777ec33` over the same files prints nothing.

Seat commits and pushes carried a runner identity (P253, P320), the handoff body ref could be written over a commit the opener would refuse (P274), and `prepr --body-check` did not judge body text as the comment gate does (P317).

- Carry 1 (P253) and Carry 4 (P320): `ref_privacy.email_leaks` gains an `anthropic-identity` class (an @anthropic.com or subdomain address) with self-test arms; `tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh` exports GIT_AUTHOR_* / GIT_COMMITTER_* from SEAT_NAME/SEAT_EMAIL in the profile and in `variables`, and (Carry 6) sets RUNNER_TEMP under the install prefix (not a /tmp literal, which `tmp_paths` refuses).
- DEVIATION, for the owner: the brief named `hpo-fixer`; SEAT_NAME/SEAT_EMAIL are `seat` / `seat@users.noreply.github.com`, the identity `cloud_dispatch.py` already pins, so there is one source. The cloud_dispatch self-test asserts the two agree.
- Carry 2 (P274): `body_push.sh` runs `ref_privacy.py guard --over refs/remotes/origin/main` on the handoff head before writing the body ref. The P274(1) prompt pin in `cloud_dispatch.py` already exists; P320 showed it did not hold, hence the exports.
- Carry 3 (P317): `prepr.sh --body-check` calls `body_privacy_line` and folds its rc.
- Carry 7: ref_privacy `--check` push-site enumeration now includes `git send-pack` and `gh api graphql -F query=@file`.
- Carry 5, the home-directory carry: re-measured at this merge base, an Identity whose home is the root account yields no private names (`root` is in PUBLIC_ACCOUNTS) and `dev/governance/roles/root-cause.md` is not refused; the existing `_home_re` / R10-FLY-REFPRIV-HOME-SEGMENT arm already satisfies it.
- Hot files `tools/pr/prepr.sh` and `tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh` overlap open PR #3221 (different regions); a merge-resolution round may follow. Hot files merged origin/main at 0ae75bf3146566bffca4490464dcc8d6d45c29ab (main has not moved since the last prepr run, so no second run). No budget raise.

## Head

`09c5e9710cd179f7d5b382965fe4e188da5f2ac5` merges main `8b49d50` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`e5c33700f9ed6b80b18961419ac7f88101ca218c` merges main `8bf45e5` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`645f009eb00999f26bb93b469412e5ef8c21e0d7` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

ab764c5862fb9aacf2f29b5d0b61f97022bc609c

## Mutation proof

- Drop the anthropic-identity class (line 252 of ref_privacy.py made unmatchable): `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --self-test` goes 109 checks, 4 failed (the class arm, two guard-CLI arms, the body_push runner-default arm).
- Drop the guard call in body_push.sh (replaced by `true || {`): the same self-test fails 1, "body_push refuses a handoff head authored by a runner default, and writes no body ref". That arm keys on the guard's stderr line, because an earlier fixture run stopped at a missing prepr.sh.
- Drop the `body_privacy_line` call in prepr.sh (`bline=$(true)`): `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test` fails "--body-check applies body_privacy_line and folds its rc (P317)", 489 passed, 1 failed.

## Null control

Unmutated tree: all of the above pass. Without the exports, the config identity authors a commit (cloud-setup self-test control); a clean topic is pushed by body_push (ref_privacy self-test null control).

## Figures

- 109 ref_privacy checks, 0 failed: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --self-test`
- 126 cloud_dispatch checks, 0 failed: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py --self-test`
- 19 cloud_setup checks, 0 failed: `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh --self-test`
- 490 prepr self-test checks, 0 failed: `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test`
- 2622 entity checks passed: `python3 tests/entities.py`
- structure ratchet passed: `python3 tests/structure.py`
- Scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out` (tests/entities.py); run_always scripts closure selftest, layout, harness_headers also passed.
- Toolchain numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1 match tests/requirements-ci.txt; no solver file touched, so no golden run.
- Repair round 2: `bash tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh --self-test` read 172 checks, 1 failed (row: the pusher census) before the edit and 172 checks, 0 failed after; ref_privacy 109, cloud_dispatch 126, cloud-setup 19, cloud_relay 332 checks, all 0 failed; `tools/pr/prepr.sh` at the final head exited 0 (ci predict clean, body check skipped as no body passed).
- Measured: base 0ae75bf3146566bffca4490464dcc8d6d45c29ab (earlier figures were taken at 6777ec33337b256d29ea145d98da413dbf076a2a); a full prepr run on the pre-merge tree (base 8364e62460f6) was clean; on this tip prepr was clean through the closures step and was then stopped by the 30-minute background limit before ci predict, so those last lines were not re-read here.

## Red checks

Final head, all check-run pages:

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` was red at 97cbe20b: the comment this diff added to `tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh` named the two pushers by file name, so `PR_PUSHER_RULE` (applied by `git grep` without skipping comments) read body_push.sh as an undispositioned pusher and the row "the pusher census: the rule returns exactly the dispositioned paths, and every runner reaps" failed (172 checks, 1 failed); the job then ran into its 30-minute timeout and was cancelled. Repaired: the comment names the guard by what it does, with no literal pusher token. body_push.sh is not a pusher (it writes an orphan body ref and never opens or updates a pull request), so no PR_PUSHERS entry. Null control: the pre-edit run is the control, the same token on the same row failed 1 and the edit made it 0; I did not re-add the token after the main merge.
- The earlier `governance / policy-docs` and `instrument-self-tests` reds of 749a3161 came from that head predating #3208 (no dev/governance/config/machinery_budgets.json) and were cured by merging origin/main.
- `governance / delivery-status`: red on the base's ancestry (3ec5178c, cd0dd169); the diff touches no delivery file.
- `tests / nightly-status`: red on the base's ancestry (3ec5178c, cd0dd169); the diff touches nothing the nightly closure reads.
- Skip reds at e5c33700 (transient, both cleared on rerun at this head): `tests / fast (3.14)` failed `tests/harness_headers.py`'s CPU-limit check, a timing check that passed on rerun with no change to the diff; and `pr-contract / pr-contract` returned an HTTP 500 from the check-runs call, rerun and green. Neither names this diff; causes as read from the logs by the coordinator.

## Block

Round 1. Measured head `749a3161dbbc18db74050036f96bc40acea1e0d1`, re-read at 2026-11-05T08:19Z and still the head of `fix/r10-seat-identity-guards`.

Every workflow on this head has concluded. `pr-contract / pr-contract` (job 127127243614) started at 08:12:29Z, after the last red concluded, and refuses the body:
`check governance / instrument-self-tests is red and ## Red checks does not name it` and the same for `governance / policy-docs` (`PR-BODY: 2 error(s)`). The body's `## Red checks` says "none" because it was written before CI ran.

Cause, reproduced by this review. Both reds come from this branch predating main's #3208 (R10-MACHINERY-RATCHETS, merge 3ec5178c6 at 06:56:47Z). The code head c34c211dd was committed at 06:42Z, before that merge. CI runs the base's (dad3178d6) restored graders against a head tree that lacks `dev/governance/config/machinery_budgets.json`:
- `governance / policy-docs`: `machinery_ratchet: dev/governance/config/machinery_budgets.json is absent at 749a3161…`, exit 2.
- `governance / instrument-self-tests`: main's `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py --self-test` on this head's tree gives `FAIL the tree has budget files to read`, 267 checks, 1 failed (reproduced locally). On the tree `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 749a3161…` the same self-test gives 272 checks, 0 failed, and machinery_ratchet's self-test gives 54 checks, 0 failed.

No earlier detector existed: main moved after the handoff, and `ci_predict.py` predicts against the merge base, which it reports as 6777ec33337b, so it predicted nothing. These checks are themselves the cheapest detector, which makes the block `root-cause-unrecorded`, not `-detectable`.

Repair: merge origin/main (it merges cleanly), then name and answer both reds in `## Red checks`, or re-run until they are green and say so. After a main merge, step 12 re-reviews only the resolution delta; every other measurement below carries.

Everything else this review checked passes; see Evidence.

## Findings

- Follow-up: the `email_leaks` docstring added at tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py:245-247 says "(a seat commits as hpo-fixer)", but the identity this PR exports is `seat` / `seat@users.noreply.github.com` (the body's DEVIATION). The docstring should name the identity actually used, or the owner's ruling. Carry: R10-SEAT-IDENTITY-GUARDS
- Residual: the DEVIATION (`seat` instead of the brief's `hpo-fixer`) waits on the owner's ruling, which the body asks for. Carry: dismissed: surfaced in the PR body for the owner, who rules at the merge review; not this reviewer's to settle
- Out of scope: five guarded push sites guard only the message of a `commit-tree` commit, never its author or committer: bus.sh:333-334, heartbeat.sh:31-33, wt_sync.sh:41-42, state_docs.py:584, roster_edit.py:940. Carry: dismissed: they publish orchestrator-side refs (bus, heartbeat, wip-sync, state, roster) under the orchestrator's identity. A commit only reaches main through app_push.sh's `--commits` guard, whose identity check this diff extends, and on a cloud seat the new profile exports set the identity
- Residual: the P317 call-site row in `prepr.sh --self-test` matches source text; it is not a driven `--body-check` run. Carry: dismissed: the carry's own named mutant (drop the call) is killed by that row (489 passed, 1 failed), and this review drove `--body-check` end to end. The head refuses a planted host path and the mutant passes it (ev/bodycheck-and-carry5.txt)

## Evidence

- Head reviewed: 749a3161dbbc18db74050036f96bc40acea1e0d1 (ev/HEAD.txt). Merge base 6777ec33337b256d29ea145d98da413dbf076a2a; origin/main dad3178d6c81cfe2bb410e7045de28f686a6f845. The diff to roles/ since the base touches only proposal-triage.md, so this contract is current.
- Finder's harness: none is committed (the packet says "none named"). This review built its own: ev/plant.sh, run at both ends with output in ev/plant-harness.txt. It plants commits in a throwaway repository and runs `ref_privacy.py guard --commits HEAD --over refs/remotes/origin/main`.
  - RESULT head: author-only Claude rc=3, committer-only rc=3, both rc=3 (all three `anthropic-identity`), trailer-only `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` rc=3 (`co-author-trailer`); each passes rc=0 once re-authored.
  - RESULT head: the hpo-fixer@users.noreply.github.com null control rc=0. A Claude-authored commit already on main, under a clean top, rc=0, so main's history is not judged.
  - RESULT base: author/committer/both rc=0, so the class is new; the trailer arm was already rc=3 at the base.
- Mutation proofs, my own targeted mutants (tree restored after each):
  - Drop the `anthropic-identity` branch of `email_leaks`: ref_privacy self-test 109 checks, 4 failed. The plant harness then gives author/committer/both rc=0.
  - body_push guard call replaced with `true ||`: 1 failed (the runner-default arm).
  - `--over` dropped from body_push's guard: 1 failed.
  - The cloud-setup profile's `GIT_AUTHOR` export dropped: 1 failed. The four `GIT_*` entries dropped from `variables`: 2 failed.
  - `RUNNER_TEMP` export dropped: 1 failed.
  - SEAT_EMAIL changed in cloud-setup.sh: cloud_dispatch self-test 1 failed (the agreement check).
  - The send-pack site pattern dropped: 1 failed. The graphql `query=@` pattern dropped: 1 failed.
  - `bline=$(true)` in prepr `--body-check`: prepr self-test 489 passed, 1 failed (ev/prepr-selftest-mutant.txt), which matches the body.
- Figures re-derived at this head:
  - ref_privacy self-test 109 checks, 0 failed.
  - cloud_dispatch 126 checks, 0 failed.
  - cloud_setup 19 checks, 0 failed.
  - prepr self-test 490 passed, 0 failed.
  - structure ratchet passed.
  - `closure.py select --files <three-dot names>`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out` at both c34c211dd and 749a3161. Bare `closure.py select` in a detached worktree prints FULL ("no changed files could be determined"), so the body's figure needs the file list.
  - The 2622 entities checks were not re-derived; that is CI's heavy run.
- Under the head's exported variables (`GIT_*=seat`, `RUNNER_TEMP=/opt/hpo/runner-temp`; ev/exported-vars.txt), these self-tests all pass: ref_privacy, cloud_dispatch, bus (128), handoff_push (6), heartbeat (7), wt_sync (ev/selftests-under-exports.txt). No self-test that asserts an author from `-c` config was found.
- Carry 5: with HOME=/root, `body-lines` passes `dev/governance/roles/root-cause.md` (rc 0, both at the head and at the base) and refuses `/root/x`. This agrees with the body's re-measurement.

- Merges:

  - Against PR #3221's head 20d5aab00a01cb3bf3738e1e78a13273089bc523 it exits 0 (ev/merge-tree-3221.txt). #3221 edits body_push.sh's prepr receipt trailer, a different region with no semantic coupling.
  - The prepr.sh edit is the `body_privacy_line` function, its call in `--body-check`, and its self-test rows only.
- Claim files, VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES, `*_budgets.json`, tests/structure.py, closures.json and closure.py are byte-identical to origin/main and untouched three-dot. There is no budget raise.
- CI on this head: merge_train classify rc=1, `RED … red: gate` (ev/classify.txt). 42 check runs over all pages (ev/check-runs.txt); the failures are gate, pr-contract, instrument-self-tests, policy-docs, delivery-status and nightly-status.
  - delivery-status is red on other PRs' OVERDUE rows (#3206, #3189 …); this diff only adds its own open row.

- Forward-carry: the body says none, and its carries are all settled in-diff. Its `carry_audit` reads 0 items.

3223.body:
R10-RAISE-GATE-SHIM (issue 3128), repair round 4: the round-3 fix review blocked on `body-stale` (the body described code head `289fe24b`, not the deny-by-default shim). This body is retaken whole for the head below, and the three cheap findings the review measured are closed in the code.

Closes #3128

## Head

`b1abbac61034cbdbec79c765db94ed3a132e5876` merges main `7d95405` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`81ee61752cff8ba51d41546f540e50ff1c950fac` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Code head `88d809f841a1fadc7ccdb34badc142dc65ef522e` (`handoff/r10-raise-gate-shim`): the PR head `6b416a18fc8752eaa3c10404cec43f896df3ed60` plus three commits of this repair, merged with `725410a6b` (the round-3 seat's commit already on `handoff/r10-raise-gate-shim`: `queue_pre_flight.py`'s self-test answers the train's measured score, three added lines; kept so the handoff ref stays a fast-forward). `6b416a18` merges the authored code head `6027fe3e`, which carries `1d4ed28e4`. The merge base with origin/main is `8b49d50b0a4c3eebee0edeb6ec98aa365e3d004f` (`git merge-base origin/main HEAD` at `81ee61752`). The PR head `81ee61752` has first parent `4404f5e74`, a merge of `origin/main` at `8b49d50b0` (4 commits past `8bf45e5dc`, the base the round-3 and round-4 text named); the resolution delta of that merge (`git diff 88d809f84 81ee61752`) is main's own three files, `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, `tests/ci_budgets.json` and `dev/programme/delivery/3228.md`, none of them this PR's.

The shim under review is `1d4ed28e4`: `tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh` carries a deny-by-default `gate()` over `api_gate`, `issue_gate` and `pr_gate` (there is no `api_hits`). A call that could write a comment on the tracking issue (#201) is refused unless the caller is python running the tree's own `tools/pr/gh_comment.py` by real path, or the call is on gh's own explicit table of calls that cannot write one: reads, `issue view/list/status/create`, `issue comment/close/...` on one plain number other than 201, `pr` with no word reading 201, `api` reads, `api` writes at paths that are neither `issues/201/comments`, `issues/comments/<id>`, an unreadable path nor a graphql mutation, and the command groups with no issue-comment surface. Everything else (an unknown subcommand, an alias, an extension, an unknown flag) is refused.

This repair changes three things on top of `1d4ed28e4`:
1. `norm()` lower-cases the api path before matching, so `repos/o/r/ISSUES/201/COMMENTS` is the tracker's (review finding: the case gap).
2. The kill word is built from fragments at runtime in `gh_calls.py` (the `planted` argv and the `gh issue comment 201` refused row) and the id is the fixture id `fixture-mandate-0000`, replacing the fake numeric id.
3. `seat_venv.sh --self-test` has a row for the installer's `gcpy=` bake (review finding: the surviving installer mutant).

No budget file, claim file, `VERSION`, manifest version or `RELEASE_NOTES.md` is touched.

The brief's four carries and where each stands:
- Carry 1 (the mandate-revoke fixer's gaps): (a) a raw `gh api` or `gh issue comment` post to #201 is refused by the shim (`1d4ed28e4`, this PR); (b) merge_train and `--check-body` check the dS value (landed in round 1; mutants M2 to M4 of the review kill it); (c) is Carry 3.
- Carry 2 (the value check re-routed from #3045): built as (b) above and unchanged by this repair.
- Carry 3 (item 870f6b21, `(c)` measured, no change needed): the `budget-raise-gate / budget-raise-gate` job against its 5-minute timeout. The round-3 seat's measurement over 31 jobs (min 19 s, median 28 s, max 48 s) is carried as it stands; this repair adds two more runs read at `6b416a18` (jobs 127348404149 and 127322514552, 29 s and 25 s). The scorer's cost on a raise diff stays unmeasured (no raise diff runs it).
- Carry 4 (item aae60647, `exec -a` argv0 spoofing): the declared residual, under Forward-carry.

## Mutation proof

All counts are `python3 tools/audit/seat/gh_calls.py --self-test` at the head, `195 checks, 0 failed`.
- Predicate `[ -n "$ok" ] || {` changed to `true || {` in the shim (the refusal never fires): `gh_calls self-test: 195 checks, 67 failed`; restored, 0 failed. (The reviewer measured 190 checks, 65 failed at `6b416a18`; the difference is this repair's own rows.)
- The lower-casing line in `norm()` deleted: 4 failed (`gh api an upper-cased issues segment is refused`, `gh api an upper-cased comments segment is refused`, `mutant killed: path segments not lower-cased` and its `(comments segment)` twin); restored, 0 failed.
- The installer's bake line in `seat_venv.sh` (`[ "$l" = 'gcpy=@HPO_GH_COMMENT@' ] && l=...`) replaced by `:`: `seat_venv self-test: 27 checks, 1 failed` (`FAIL --install-shims bakes the tree's gh_comment.py path into the installed gh shim`); restored, 0 failed. The same mutation left 25 checks, 0 failed before this repair.
- The in-suite `guard_mutant` rows of `1d4ed28e4` (each kills one rule of the guard) are unchanged and pass.

## Null control

- A post to another issue with upper-case segments (`repos/o/r/ISSUES/202/COMMENTS`) reaches the real gh (stub rc 7), so the lower-casing refuses only the tracker. The existing nulls (GET of #201, posts to 202 and 2011, dot segments to 202, `%`-encoded 202, `issue comment 202`, `issue view 201`, an api read with Accept, a non-issue path write) still reach the stub.
- The unmodified shim at `6b416a18` lets both upper-case spellings reach the stub (the review's measurement); the deleted-lower-casing mutant reproduces it.
- The source `seat-gh` carries the `gcpy=@HPO_GH_COMMENT@` placeholder, asserted by its own row (the bake row's null control).
- **No control wrote to GitHub.** Every shim control ran against the self-test's local stub `gh` (exits 7, no network call); the refused rows assert the stub never ran. The only mandate id in tests is the fixture `fixture-mandate-0000`. The kill word appears whole in no added line: `git diff origin/main...HEAD | grep '^+' | grep -ci 'revok'` prints `0` (it printed 2 at `6b416a18`: the `planted` argv and the `issue comment 201` row).

## Figures

## Block

The guard reads a #201 comment write only as `gh issue comment <target>` or `gh api .../issues/<n>/comments`. gh 2.89.0, the version on this host (`gh issue close --help`), also posts an ordinary issue comment through `gh issue close <n> -c/--comment <text>` ("Leave a closing comment") and through `gh issue reopen <n> -c/--comment <text>` ("Add a reopening comment"). Both calls name the issue as a plain number, which the shim can read, so they are not the declared residual (PATCH, graphql, `gh pr comment`).

I ran both offline against the stub, with the kill pairing built at runtime from fragments and the fixture id. Three calls reached the stub with rc 0 and one argv line each:
- `gh issue close 201 --comment <kill pairing>`
- `gh issue close 201 -c x`
- `gh issue reopen 201 --comment x`

The evidence is ev/shim-cases2-head.txt (`issue-close-comment-201`, `issue-close-c-201`, `issue-reopen-comment-201`). The gate's revocation reader takes any owner-account comment on #201 (the thread read of `issues/201/comments` in budget_raise_gate.py), so a closing comment counts exactly as a `gh issue comment` would. The class the body states is "a #201 comment write spelled so the shim cannot read the number", and this is a #201 comment write the shim does not read at all.

A sound repair treats a `--comment`/`-c` value on `issue close` and `issue reopen` as a comment write on that command's target. It runs the target through the same `num()`, and fails closed on an unreadable one. The `-c`/`--comment` value is skipped by gh's flag table, attached or detached. It needs pinned refusal arms in `gh_calls.py --self-test`, plus a null control: `issue close 202 --comment x`, and `issue close 201` with no comment, which writes no comment. It would be best to enumerate gh's issue subcommands that take a comment-writing flag, so the class closes by rule rather than by spelling.

R10-CI-SLIM: two of the three slip-study cards the owner accepted on 2026-11-05 land here (C2, C3), and C7 lands as (a) and (b). (c) is dropped, because once its premise is checked its saving measures 0. This change does four things. Main's critical-path ratchet becomes report-only. Edit runs stop holding a runner while the code run works. Product pull requests stop paying for machinery lanes. Tools-only pull requests stop paying for PR CodeQL. No product file changes (`custom_components/` untouched).

**Repair round 3.** The review at 84a7c456f blocked C7(c). `prelude.pins_due` skipped `tests / mutation-pins` and `tests / mutation-autofix` on a non-product delta from `before`. The rule never checked that the previous head's pins had concluded. cancel-superseded cancels them, and in the PR's own sample that held in 3 of 3 skips.

The repair is in two commits:
- 2c51d07b5 adds the reviewer's sound rule. The delta counts only from a head whose code run concluded the measurement (`prelude.pins_measured`): `tests / mutation` success, or failure with every pins shard and the autofix succeeding. Anything else measures. Eleven self-tests were added. On round 2's rule, 7 of them fail: previous pins cancelled, autofix failed, pins still running, pins skipped on a failed mutation, one shard of several cancelled, an unreadable runs listing, and no run at the previous head.
- 4056a2c5e drops C7(c). With the premise checked, `c7_replay.py` reads (c) as 0 runs and a saving of 0. Even with the read moved to the latest moment it could happen (each run's prelude end), the saving is still 0. One reason is that the autofix's own pin commit lands while that autofix is still running, so the previous head is never concluded at the next prelude.

The card asked for a measurement guaranteed at review-ready, and a saving that is not real is not kept. So `prelude.pins_due`, the `pins` output, tests.yml's `pins` input and both `inputs.pins` job conditions are removed. The `mutation`, `mutation-pins` and `mutation-autofix` jobs are YAML-identical to main's again. `gate_satisfiable.py` now refuses any caller input in either pins job's `if:`, and it reads `GATE NOT SATISFIABLE` on round 2's workflows.

Alternatives not taken:
- Keeping 2c51d07b5's rule: it is sound, but it costs one runs read and one jobs read per synchronize for a measured saving of 0. Per fixer.md step 17, the simpler tree wins.
- Taking the delta from the last concluded head, the reviewer's equivalent form: it walks history for the same 0 saving.

**C2. `critical_path_minutes` is report-only.** `tests/ci_ratchet.py` adds a `REPORT_ONLY` set holding that one metric. `compare` prints it as `info critical_path_minutes: X (reference R; report-only, never graded)` and never counts it. Every other `ci_budgets.json` row is still graded at zero tolerance. The band row `critical_path_minutes_band` and `BAND_KEYS` are deleted. The recorded value stays as the reference that `orchestrator_tick.py`'s ETA reads. `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py` types that reference `free`.

**C3 (option A). An edit run holds no runner.** `prelude.defer_to` finds an unfinished code run at the same head and PR whose `pr-contract / pr-contract` has not started. When it finds one, the edit run's workset is `arch-score budget-raise-gate` and the run does not wait. `pr-contract` reads the body off the API when it starts, after every unit, so the code run's gate judges the LATEST body. The edit run's gate takes the prelude's workset (`WORKSET`, `gate.deferring`), and a unit skipped in a deferring run is no source. If `pr-contract` has started, the code run is finished, or there is no code run, today's wait applies. A deferral read in a race is a false RED, which `gate-sweep.yml` re-judges. It is never a false green.

**C7.** (a) `prelude.machinery`: a pull request whose every changed file is product stands down three lanes at step level, each reporting success: `tests / arch-instrument`, the `tests / closures` recording and `governance / env-matrix`. `governance / instrument-self-tests`, which is not required, skips whole. Product means `custom_components/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, a script that `tests/closures.json` measures, `tests/golden/` or `tests/mutation_ledger/`. Any other file runs the lanes, and so does every push. (b) `codeql_scope.decide` skips every leg of a pull request with nothing under `custom_components/` or `.github/`. The stand-in reports success, and a push to main always analyzes.

**Owner constraint (tvofi, 2026-11-05), per change.** For each change: the check that still guards each production path, and why the risk to production quality and to future throughput is acceptable.
- C2: no production path. `tests / ci-ratchet` still grades every other CI metric at zero tolerance (a planted `script_runs_per_push` 54 -> 55 is GREW at the head). The accepted risk is that a slower critical path goes ungraded. It is still printed and still feeds the ETA. Throughput gain: no more re-record and band-widening PRs (#2839, #3045, #3180, #3189, #3201, #3228). Before: grew=1. After: grew=0 (`## Null control`).
- C3: no check is skipped. The code run's gate still judges every production unit, and its `pr-contract` reads the latest body. Opus review dispatch is not touched. A race gives a false red, never a false green. Before: 4438 edit-run job-minutes. After: 660.
- C7(a): the idled lanes measure machinery only. On a diff that touches `custom_components/`, these still run: `tests / fast`, `tests / mutation` with its pins and autofix, goldens, features, CodeQL and review. `gate_satisfiable.py`'s production-only case reads every CodeQL leg as `analyze`. Before: 4988 job-minutes. After: 4988 (0 runs idled in the sample, so it pays after C1, as the card says).
- C7(b): CodeQL still analyzes every pull request reaching `custom_components/` or `.github/`, and every push to main. It skips only tools/dev-only pull requests, which main's push analysis covers. Before: 2955 job-minutes. After: 1764.
- C7(c) dropped: mutation testing on production changes is main's again, byte for byte (YAML comparison, `## Figures`). Throughput risk removed: the skip that left `mutation` red with no pins table at a head the seat could not re-trigger is gone.

Toolchain: `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh --check` read `OK python3 is /opt/hpo/venv-ci/bin/python3`. No golden ran: the scope is MODE: FULL, so the goldens are CI's.

## Block

**C7(c) skips measurements that never happened.** `prelude.pins_due` gates `tests / mutation-pins` and `tests / mutation-autofix` on the push's own delta (`before...head`). Its docstring states the premise: "the sites still unpinned were measured at the head before". The rule never checks that premise. Cancel-superseded cancels a previous head's run, and its pins shards with it. When the next push is non-product (a delivery row, a body fix-up, a tooling commit), those sites go unmeasured.

Measurement, on the PR's own recorded sample (`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_ci_slim/sample.json`, my script `ev/c7c_probe.py`, output `ev/c7c_probe.txt`, `ev/c7c_three_runs.txt`):

- In all 3, the previous head's survivors were never pinned:
  - PR 3219, run 41937668180: the previous run 41937637106 had `tests / mutation-pins` **cancelled**. Its own pins succeeded in reality, and that was the only completed measurement of those sites. C7(c) removes it.
  - PR 3220, run 41951544787: the previous run 41951503566 had pins **cancelled**. Its own 7 pin shards succeeded, the only completed measurement. C7(c) removes it.
  - PR 3219, run 41951472711: the previous run's pins succeeded, but its autofix **failed**, so nothing was pinned.
- Control: runs where `pins_due` is True keep today's behaviour by construction. The planted production defect below shows `pins_due` True on a product diff at the head.

Consequence: at such a head, `mutation` stays red with no pins table and no autofix. The seat cannot re-trigger the measurement. A dispatch never runs pins (`github.event_name == 'pull_request'`), and an empty commit or a close-and-reopen is forbidden. Only a later push touching the package does. This does not weaken production quality, because `mutation` still fails closed. It is a throughput risk: in this window every C7(c) skip hits it.

Card sentence it contradicts: C7 (c) "mutation-pins runs once when the PR is review-ready, not at every head", with the accepted risk "(c) A survivor is found at review-ready instead of per head". The implementation guarantees no single measurement. A survivor whose only measurement was superseded is not found at review-ready or at any later non-product head. That goes beyond the card.

Minimal sound repair (the fixer's call): `pins_due` is False only when the head the delta starts from actually concluded `mutation-pins` (success, or skipped because `mutation` passed). Otherwise, measure. Equivalently, take the delta from the last head whose pins concluded, not from `before`. Add a self-test whose previous head's pins were cancelled. 3231.body:
Accept a `water_heater` entity as the DHW set-point (`dhw_setpoint_entity`).

Some pumps expose their hot-water set-point only as a `water_heater` entity — Luxtronik's `water_heater.<id>_domestic_water` is one (state = operation mode, target in the `temperature` attribute, range `min_temp`/`max_temp`, step `target_temp_step`, all in the instance's unit). The selector offered only `number`, `input_number` and `climate`, so such an install could not configure the slot. A `water_heater` carries the climate shape, so this treats it as one: read, range, step and unit follow the climate path, and the write goes through `water_heater.set_temperature`.

Changes: `inputs.py` (`SETPOINT_SERVICES`, `_RANGE_KEYS`, `_STEP_KEYS`, and `setpoint_unit` now keys on `_ATTRIBUTE_TARGET_DOMAINS = ("climate", "water_heater")`), `config_flow.py` (selector domain list), the `dhw_setpoint_entity` help text in `strings.json` / `en.json` / `sv.json`, the #1526 service table and one new check in `tests/features.py`, and `tests/golden/config_flow.json` re-recorded (the two `dhw_setpoint_entity` filter lines move, nothing else).

**Contributor credit.** This change is by the outside contributor Bankaifan, first opened as PR #3224 (https://github.com/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/pull/3224, head `a1fc6edb0e7fb51015bb50cb66b4c9bbbecfe877`). It is re-authored here as a seat pull request because decision 0011 gives an outside contributor no way to author one: the contributor's three commits are cherry-picked unchanged, each keeping its author (Bankaifan), with no squash and no edit, and their three-dot diff is the same patch as the original (identical patch-id). The feature measurements below are the contributor's, from their own head.

**Repairs on top of the contributor's commits.** The contributor's three commits are untouched. 3232.body:
Bound the process worker's reply. Before this change `_run_in_process` wrote the job and blocked in `pickle.load(stdout)` inside `with _PROCESS_LOCK:` with no deadline. A worker that is alive but silent never raises, so the #511 fallback never fired; every later solve queued on the lock, a reload did not help, and Home Assistant's stop ran into the supervisor timeout. The branch adds the reply deadline (`PROCESS_REPLY_TIMEOUT_S`, 1800 s; the contributor's change), the off-loop route's re-raise and held warning, the frame deadline (`_REPLY_FRAME_TIMEOUT_S`, 60 s), the frame size cap (`_REPLY_FRAME_MAX_BYTES`, 256 MiB), the stop path's bounded lock (`_SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S`, 5 s), and the diagnosis service's translated failure (`diagnose_interval_failed`). The worker checks live in `tests/worker_deadlines.py`, a module `tests/features.py` calls, so CodeQL extracts them as a separate small file (round 3).

This round (5) repairs the review block at `bba5b4d4` (verdict `mutation-vacuous: measure`). The mutant that deletes `left_bytes -= size` in `_frame_reader.read` (`coordinator.py`, the running count that makes `_REPLY_FRAME_MAX_BYTES` a bound on the whole frame rather than on each `read()`) survived every feature check, and the real reader then accepted a 1,200,044-byte frame over a 1,000,000-byte cap. The repair adds one check pair to `tests/worker_deadlines.py` and changes no production code.

**Trust boundary.** Unchanged by this round. The worker is the integration's own child process, launched by `_ensure_worker` from the installed package; its reply is unpickled in the parent as at base; `_frame_reader` feeds the same `pickle.load` under a time bound and a size bound. This round touches no file under `custom_components/`.

## Acknowledgements

Thanks to @Bankaifan for the original change in #3226: the bounded reply deadline on the process worker, and the field report and shutdown traces that found the hang. This pull request is a seat re-author of that contribution: decision 0011 gives an outside contributor no way to author a pull request here. His four commits (`61cec72ac`, `010534bbc`, `dd4416f1a`, `5088d3688`, author Bankaifan) are kept intact, no edit, squash or rebase; the seat's repairs are separate commits on top.

## Head

`28e4375441e6011083dce278e3ffdee9cbbbf26f` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`dc8cbd06c1da1e258c082015bc10aa206f884780`: the round's one test commit merged with `origin/main` `80016a71f567d936450d8708abcbb79d9e8071d7` (a merge, no rebase), on top of the previous handoff `79f202f8e`. `origin/main` has since moved to `f2a015142714383722bf49d7ab20d8398ec9674c`; the figures below name the base they were taken at. Every figure below was taken at this head unless it names another SHA.

## Mutation proof

The mutant `measure`: delete the line `        left_bytes -= size` in `_frame_reader.read` and run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`.
- At the head with the mutant: `1 of 4904 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`. The one failure is the new check "a reply whose reads each fit the frame cap but whose total exceeds it is refused and the worker reaped" (`raised None after 0.00 s`, the whole oversized reply returned). The null control beside it still passes.
- With the line restored: `ALL 4904 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, and `git diff -- custom_components` is empty.
- The check drives the real worker: with `_REPLY_FRAME_MAX_BYTES` shortened to 1,000,000 it sends `tuple([bytes(600_000), bytes(600_000)])`, two reads that each fit the cap and total 1.2 MB, and requires a `ProcessWorkerUnavailable` saying `exceeds 1000000 bytes`, no returned value, the lock free and `_PROCESS_WORKER` reaped.
- No `killed_by` ledger row was added for this site, and none can be: `tests/mutation_table.py` generates no mutant that deletes an augmented assignment, and `completeness_problems` refuses a disposition naming a site the inventory does not generate, so a hand-written row would turn the driver red. The mutant is killed by a check, which is the proof; the 20 rows from earlier rounds are unchanged. The operator gap is the verdict's own Findings item, which the orchestrator routes.

## Null control

`null control: a reply of two reads whose total is under the frame cap returns whole` (two 400 kB strings under the same 1,000,000-byte cap) prints `ok` at the head and with the mutant. Base `9a54629e` has no cap, so it accepts both replies; the review measured that (`ALL 4898 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`). The pin runs of earlier rounds recorded `null control ... NULL_COMMENT survived` against a comment-only edit.

## Figures

- `ALL 4876 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` at base `origin/main` 80016a71f, and `ALL 4904 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` at this head (+28 over base, of which 2 are this round's) — `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`, run in each tree
- `ALL 2640 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` at base and at this head — `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`
- `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` — `python3 -I tests/structure.py`
- scope `MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out.` (reason: `tests/closure.py` is in the diff), then `ALL TEST SCRIPTS PASSED` before the final merge — `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) ./tests/run.sh`. After the final merge I re-ran `tests/arch_score.py` alone (`ALL 279 ARCHITECTURE SCORE CHECKS PASSED`), `structure.py` and `entities.py`; the full gate was not repeated, and the merge changed no file this diff touches
- `PRE-PR: dc8cbd06c1da1e258c082015bc10aa206f884780 ... rc=0` — `HPO_ALLOW_STALE_TOOLS=1 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh`; its `diff mutants` step is skipped there (`MUTANT_CMD unset`, report only)

## Red checks

Seven check runs stand red in this branch's ancestry, all on one pushed commit, `e80a319c2` (round 1's head, runs 42135610131 `CI code` and 42135610164 `CI edit`, 2026-11-06). None stands at the PR head `bba5b4d4`: every run named below is `success` there, and `tests / mutation-autofix` is `skipped`. Cause and class by check-run name, read from each job's log:

- `tests / fast (3.14)` (job 127628215893): **genuine, at that head, since fixed.** `tests/entities.py` failed `R10 N-log-flood barrier ... mismatch {('coordinator.py', '_await_optimize'): (1, 0)}`: the round-1 diff had added a WARNING site the reasoned list did not carry. Class: a barrier the author's local run did not reach. Later commits on this branch changed that site and the list; `bba5b4d4` ran the same lane green (job 128172512678), and `ALL 2640 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` is the figure below at this head. The `a16:debug_*` FAIL lines in the same log are the nightly judge's own null controls, each followed by its `ok`.
- `tests / mutation` (job 127626804241): **genuine, at that head, since fixed.** `MUTATION TABLE REFUSED -- 3097 unpinned site(s) against 3091 at the ratchet base, 6 of them added by this diff`. Class: new guard sites without a recorded disposition. Later rounds pinned them (the `test(mutation): pin ...` commits, and `712ae748`/`2b538e6a6` re-pinning the 18 worker-deadline sites); `bba5b4d4` ran green (job 128172510303).
- `tests / mutation-autofix` (job 127646510068): **a consequence of the red above, not a second defect.** It reported `AUTOFIX: skip-measure-failed -- THE REPAIR DID NOT HAPPEN` because the measure step it repairs after had failed. `skipped` at `bba5b4d4`.
- `tests / replay` (job 127628215788): **runner variance, not this diff.** The lane ran 194 checks and failed 4, all `cycle_cost` arms on the synthetic fixture: `runner class unknown: ref_ms 27.26 lies in no band of COST_RUNNER_CLASSES`. The runner's reference timing fell between two recorded classes, so no budget applied; this diff touches no file the replay reads. `bba5b4d4` ran green (job 128172512924), and main's run at `80016a71f` needed an attempt 2 to go green (run 42307872956).
- `governance / delivery-status` (job 127626804351) and `tests / nightly-status` (job 127626804073): **grade main, not this diff.** The first listed overdue delivery rows of other pull requests (`#3206`, `#3189`, ...) and says it is not a required context; the second reported the last concluded scheduled nightly (run 41943946464, its `slow` job) red. This diff touches neither the delivery rows nor the nightly workflow. Both are `success` at `bba5b4d4` (jobs 128172511439 and 128172510882).
- `governance / instrument-self-tests` (job 127626804142, same head) was **cancelled** after 30 minutes, not failed; `success` at `bba5b4d4` (job 128172508458). Runs 42283173042, 42283167448, 42229351684, 42170673519, 42135586068 and 42135581414 on older heads are `cancelled` by newer pushes (the `cancel-superseded` job), not red.
- `pr-contract` and `gate` also failed at `e80a319c2`, on the body check and on the red jobs above; they are the aggregate of those reds, and both are `success` at `bba5b4d4` (jobs 128183982141 and 128184430555). The `CI edit` runs 42284985531 (head `0e59de557`), 42283942259, 42246412814, 42234575344, 42229785351, 42229350113, 42171094377 and 42170673297 failed only in those two aggregates, on body-check rounds already answered.

Nothing red stands at the PR head; no red above is an open defect of this diff. Two local reds were also seen and cleared while preparing the round-5 head, neither a CI check: `tests/arch_score.py` read one failure (`a head edit to tests/structure.py is not what the gate loads`) because a 230 s timeout of my own had left `/opt/hpo/runner-temp/base` behind, and it passed once that directory was removed; `prepr.sh` read `REFUSE self-test 512 passed, 1 failed` on the `no-matcher` policy-lint null control while four jobs ran at once, and passed alone, as the comment at `tools/pr/prepr.sh` 1932–1934 describes for that row.

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked e80a319c21f7b652fa579bab63e8997532aef22c regression: select.select refuses a worker pipe fd >= 1024 (FD_SETSIZE) that main serves, and tests/entities.py fails the N-log-flood barrier on the new _await_optimize WARNING

bus-nonce: ab1ee6d5f52ad8399c2670c58f685963

Round 1 of review for #3232 (seat re-author of outside PR #3226, contributor Bankaifan). Measured head: e80a319c21f7b652fa579bab63e8997532aef22c, base 7d95405e384e1ebf8223f04657c85996af55f3d9 (origin/main, 0 behind). `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract is current.

## Block

1. **Regression: `select.select` on the worker's pipe.** `_run_in_process` now calls `select.select([stdout], [], [], timeout)` (coordinator.py:1954). `select()` raises `ValueError: filedescriptor out of range in select()` for any descriptor >= FD_SETSIZE (1024). The generic `except Exception` translates that into a transport fault: the worker is killed and `ProcessWorkerUnavailable("exited rc=None: ...")` is raised, so every solve on such a host falls back in process. That repeats every cycle while the pipe's fd stays high (each respawn takes the lowest free fd), and the repair issue follows after WORKER_FALLBACK_CAP cycles. Main serves the same call.
   Home Assistant raises its own soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to 2048 (`homeassistant.util.resource.DEFAULT_SOFT_FILE_LIMIT = 2048`, read from /opt/hpo/venv-ha), because real installs exceed 1024 descriptors. This PR also adds a new respawn trigger (the timeout), and a respawn happens at runtime, when the fd table is fullest.
   Measured (ev/probe.out, ev/probe.py `fd` mode, 1100 fds held, RLIMIT 4096):
   - head: `RESULT fd FAIL ProcessWorkerUnavailable: process worker exited rc=None: filedescriptor out of range in select()`
   - origin/main (null control): `RESULT fd ok child=1430 stdout_fd=1106`
   The repair is one line, and the claim it rests on is shown in ev/poll.out: `selectors.DefaultSelector()` (epoll on Linux) or `select.poll()` reads the same fd. `RESULT select.select fd 1103 ValueError ...` against `RESULT selectors EpollSelector fd 1103 True`. Pin it with a check that holds >1024 fds before spawning the worker.
2. **tests/entities.py fails at the head: 1 of 2632 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED.** The failing check is `R10 N-log-flood barrier: every unlatched WARNING/ERROR is on the reasoned list with its exact count -- a persisting condition goes through log_held  [mismatch {('coordinator.py', '_await_optimize'): (1, 0)}; read 69 sites]`. The PR's new `_LOGGER.warning("%s; keeping the last plan, a fresh worker starts next cycle", err)` is an unlatched WARNING. It repeats every cycle while the worker keeps timing out, so it must go through `log_held` or be added to the reasoned list with a reason. The body's figures ran only features.py and structure.py, never entities.py. Run with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` (ev/entities_head.summary.txt). Null control at origin/main: `ALL 2632 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, with `ok   R10 N-log-flood barrier` (ev/entities_main.summary.txt).

## Findings

- Follow-up: `_await_off_loop` (sysid step, replay interval, recovery estimate, sensor advisor; coordinator.py:2007-2017) catches `ProcessWorkerUnavailable`, which now includes `ProcessWorkerTimeout`. It then reruns the timed-out job on HA's executor with no deadline. Measured (ev/probe.out `offloop`): with `PROCESS_REPLY_TIMEOUT_S = 0.5` and a 3 s job, head returned after 3.5 s (0.5 s deadline plus a full 3 s rerun on the executor); main returned after 3.0 s. So the contributor's open question resolves to yes: a genuinely hung model job, after 1800 s, moves to an executor thread and holds it unbounded. It does not hold `_PROCESS_LOCK`, so the wedge of every later solve does not return, but the thread and one core do. `_await_off_loop` should re-raise `ProcessWorkerTimeout` as `_await_optimize` does, unless a rerun is deliberately wanted. Owed in the same re-cut as the block. Carry: dismissed: owed by this PR's re-cut under the block above, not carried to another stage
- Residual: the bounded reap after a timeout (`worker.wait(timeout=_SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S)`, coordinator.py:1961, commit 5088d3688) has no mutation proof; the body says so. No check drives a child that survives SIGKILL, so the mutant `wait(timeout=...)` -> `wait()` survives by construction (not run: no test reaches that branch). Carry: dismissed: the branch needs a child in uninterruptible sleep, which no portable test can produce; disclosed in the body
- Non-blocking: the body and contract are the seat's re-author template. The quoted counts are stale: the body says `ALL 4836 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, while this head measures 4864 against main's 4858. The unpinned-sites list and mutation disposition are the orchestrator's to refresh. Carry: dismissed: external author, orchestrator repairs the body
- Non-blocking: `select()` on a pipe is POSIX-only. On native Windows it raises, and the same transport fallback would fire every cycle. Home Assistant supports Linux (HA OS, container, supervised, core on Linux) and macOS core, where pipes select fine, so this matters only if the selectors fix is not taken. Carry: dismissed: no supported HA platform lacks pipe select

## Evidence

- Re-author claim verified. The patch-id of `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main refs/pull/3226/head) refs/pull/3226/head` is `374d81b62985683137ea82b99325c6988289a9aa`; the same diff against this head minus the delivery-row commit (`e80a319c2^`) gives the identical id. Per commit, b5eeedbb2/61cec72ac, 585be114b/010534bbc, 530457f6d/dd4416f1a and ba704972f/5088d3688 have identical patch-ids. Each commit message differs only by the removed `Co-Authored-By` and `Claude-Session` trailers. Author Bankaifan is kept on all four. The seat adds only dev/programme/delivery/3232.md (1 line) and a clean merge of origin/main (1284c8058).
- Three-dot diff: coordinator.py, strings.json, translations/en.json, translations/sv.json, tests/features.py, tests/harness.py, dev/programme/delivery/3232.md. VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md and both claim files are untouched.
- Merges (ev/mergetree.out): `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 0 against origin/main 7d95405e3, against PR 3220 e70dfd645 (the same tree as main) and against PR 3198 e99f1555f. No conflict on coordinator.py or tests/features.py.
- features.py (`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`): head `ALL 4864 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`; origin/main null control `ALL 4858 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`. The 6 new checks are the 6 R.check calls in the new section.
- Mutation proof, re-run by me on full features.py in copies (ev/mutant_m*.diff, ev/feat_m*.summary.txt):
  - m1, deadline -> None (`select.select([stdout], [], [], None)`): `3 of 4864 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED` (raises ProcessWorkerTimeout `raised None after 30.0 s`; fresh worker; `_await_optimize keeps the last plan`)
  - m2, the `except ProcessWorkerTimeout` clause in `_await_optimize` removed: `1 of 4864 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED` (the in-process rerun and the solve_worker_fallback issue appear)
  - m3, stop-path `acquire(timeout=...)` -> `acquire()`: `1 of 4864 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED` (`_shutdown_process_pool took 9.95 s with the lock held`)
  The new tests drive the real select path through a real child, not a stub.
- structure.py: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` at head and main, with identical `ok` lines (ev/structure_*.log).
- Large-reply claim ("a readable pipe means the job is done"): holds for replies over the 64 KiB pipe buffer. Under a 2 s deadline, replies of 70 kB, 10 MB and 100 MB returned in 0.00 s, 0.02 s and 1.34 s (main 1.01 s). After select returns, `pickle.load` reads while the child's single `write(blob)` continues, so the load can block only on a writer stopped mid-write (e.g. SIGSTOP), which nothing produces (ev/probe.out `big`).
- Leaks after a timeout: 10 consecutive 0.3 s timeouts took 3.1 s in total (main, with no deadline, 50.1 s). The parent's fd count went 7 -> 5, with no zombie (`Z`) children (ev/probe.out `leak`). The reap is bounded at 5 s.
- `_PROCESS_LOCK` release: `_run_in_process` holds it only through `with`, so every exit path (the timeout raise, the transport raise, a BaseException) releases it. The stop path pairs acquire with `try/finally: release`, and skips the swap on timeout. That leaves `_PROCESS_WORKER` pointing at a killed child, and `_ensure_worker` replaces it because `poll()` is not None once the kill lands. All `_PROCESS_WORKER` writes are under the lock, except the stop path's read of the handle before the lock, which predates this PR.
- 1800 s deadline: the contributor's spread (median 18 s, p90 263 s, max 426 s, 168 values, one Pi 4 install) **cannot be re-derived**: it comes from their HA recorder, and the repo has no solver time limit or solve-time harness (no `time_limit`/timeout constant on the solve path). Taken as given, 1800 s is about 4.2x the reported max. Diagnosis (`async_diagnose_interval`, which calls `_await_process` directly) and sysid jobs share the same deadline, and no bound on their runtime exists in tree to check against.
- The UpdateFailed path reuses `_raise_update_failed` (the #1546 route that `process_worker_unusable` already takes), with the key `process_worker_timeout` in strings.json, en.json and sv.json and the placeholder `{minutes}`. The `_ET_KEYS` registration was added, and the features check asserts `translation_key == "process_worker_timeout"` and that no in-process job ran.
- No finder's harness applies (an outside contribution with no audit finding). The contributor's harness is the new features section, disclosed as theirs. The fd and offloop probes are mine (ev/probe.py).
- CI at this head: `merge_train.py classify` exited 1, `RED ... pending: none red: gate`. The red `gate` (run 42136508003) is `cancelled`, which is a superseded refresh run. In run 42135610131 at read time: `tests / replay` failed `4 of 194 replay checks FAILED`, all `cycle_cost ... runner class unknown: ref_ms 27.26 lies in no band of COST_RUNNER_CLASSES`. That is a runner-calibration gap in the instrument, not this diff. `tests / mutation` failed; per the body it is red by construction on 6 unpinned sites, but the log's tail I read held only the shard set-up, so I did not see its failure lines. `governance / delivery-status` failed on other PRs' OVERDUE rows and is not a required context. `tests / nightly-status` failed and is not this PR's. `tests / fast`, `coverage`, `closures`, `arch-instrument`, `mutation-pins (1,2)`, `instrument-self-tests` and `codeql / Analyze (python)` were still in_progress. CI is not GREEN at this head; the block stands on the code independently.
- Head check: the PR body's `## Head` names e80a319c21f7b652fa579bab63e8997532aef22c, the head measured.

bus: verdict/3232 at 985c64df4c17c904d1e02b92894174e942739290, confirmed from cloud-opus (review/3232 at f084d0bd39ba3b6331f3297c7ae81007c0fa1141); evidence: ~/.zcode/bus/verdicts/3232/985c64df4c17c904d1e02b92894174e942739290/evidence

Fix review: blocked 6e048afc6d857f65b62108e0648543dd611bd433 mutation-vacuous: dropping the off-loop timeout warning or its recovery (log_held off_loop_timeout) leaves every check green

bus-nonce: e3ffee93bf03b42feca3f39531bbb0a2

Round 2 (re-check of the round-1 block 985c64df). Measured head 6e048afc6d857f65b62108e0648543dd611bd433 (tree c11ea7441, identical to c9614abb7's, which the body's figures name). Role file unchanged since the merge base (`git diff merge-base...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` empty).

## Block

Repair 3 of the body says `_await_off_loop` "holds a per-job warning (`log_held(hass, "off_loop_timeout:<qualname>", ...)`, cleared when that job next completes)". No check pins either half:
- m4, the `log_held(hass, key, True, ...)` line in the `except ProcessWorkerTimeout` clause deleted (the re-raise kept): `ALL 4888 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (ev/features-m4.log, ev/mutant-m4.diff).
- m6, the clearing `log_held(hass, key, False)` before `return result` deleted: `ALL 4888 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (ev/features-m6.log, ev/mutant-m6.diff).

Without that warning an off-loop timeout is invisible at default log level: the replay (`_replay_interval`) and the sensor advisor (`_with_sensor_advisor`) catch it with `except Exception` and log only at DEBUG, so a worker reaped after 30 minutes on those jobs leaves no WARNING at all. The mutation table draws no mutant for a bare call statement, so its "8 sites, 0 unpinned" is true by its own definition and does not cover these two lines; the R10 N-log-flood barrier counts unlatched WARNINGs, so it cannot see a deleted one either. This is the brief's item (b) ("the held message reaches the log through the route, mutant: drop it, red") failing for the off-loop route. The `_await_optimize` route passes it (m3, m7 below).
Repair: one check in the worker read timeout section. Run `_await_off_loop` past a short deadline twice, then once within it, with a sink on `log_held`'s logger. Require [WARNING, INFO "Resolved"] and the job name in the message. m4 and m6 must then each turn it red.

## Findings

- Residual: once the reply pipe turns readable, `pickle.load(stdout)` still has no bound. A worker that stops partway through writing its already-serialised reply (SIGSTOP, or the host stalling mid-write) would hold `_PROCESS_LOCK` again. Measured: a 50 MB reply, about 760 x the 64 KiB pipe buffer, round-trips under a 5 s deadline in 0.56 s at the head (0.10 s at base). The claim "a readable pipe means the job is done" therefore holds for every writer that keeps running. The only failure left needs a writer that stops after it has started writing. Carry: dismissed: needs a writer stopped mid-frame after full serialisation, not reachable by the hang this PR bounds; measured clean at 50 MB
- Note: `async_diagnose_interval` calls `_await_process` directly, so a diagnosis timeout reaches the service caller as an untranslated `ProcessWorkerTimeout`, which is a `RuntimeError`. `ProcessWorkerUnavailable` already reached that caller the same way at base, and before this PR the same call could hang without limit. The class is closed: `_await_process` has exactly three callers (`_await_off_loop`, `_await_optimize`, `async_diagnose_interval`), and all three were judged here.
