R10-HOTFIX-STAMP-BASE (lane C, fix, size S), repair round 2. v7.1.2 was tagged by hand at b8e823699, on a tree whose VERSION, manifest version and notes still read 7.1.1. `tools/release/stamp.py` bumped from VERSION alone, so it proposed v7.1.2 again, and rule 3 refuses that as an existing tag. Rules "flush", 4 and 5 (`window_log_args`, `rule4_problem`, `disposition_gate`) also took their window from the newest v* tag, and no stamp had made that tag. v7.1.2 is kept. Nothing is deleted or retagged.

What changes:

- `stamp.py` gets two pure functions. `bump_base(current, tags)` returns the higher of VERSION and the highest `TAG_RE` tag. `last_stamped_tag(tags, version_at)` returns the newest release tag whose own tree's VERSION equals its name. The VERSION lookup is passed in, so the self-test needs no git. `tag_version` reads `git show <tag>:VERSION` through the module's `sh` seam. After Rule 1's `fetch --tags`, the Rule 3 block computes `base = bump_base(current, tags + remote)` and then `nxt = next_version(base, ...)`. `last_tag = last_stamped_tag(tags, tag_version)` feeds flush, rule 4 and rule 5. Rule 3's exists refusal and above-every-tag refusal stay as the backstop.
- `release.yml` gets a new step, `Refuse a tag whose tree does not carry its version`, which runs before `Create the GitHub release`. It refuses unless VERSION is the tag, the manifest version is the tag and RELEASE_NOTES.md has an exact `## $TAG` line, and it prints every problem it finds. The publish step reads the asset back `attempts=5` times, with a `sleep 10` between reads and none after the last, then fails. `RELEASE_READBACK_ATTEMPTS` names that bound in stamp.py, and the self-test pins the two to agree.
- The self-test cuts each step's own `run: |` block out of release.yml with `release_step_script`. It never runs a copy of the step's logic.

Round 2 builds the review's three findings at 66577738. None is carried.

1. The previous body's `## Head` figure was false. This body is re-taken whole from the template, and every figure below was re-derived at the final head by the command shown with it (see `## Head` for the corrected claim).
2. The pin `flush: main runs it after rule 3 and before rule 4` searched `main()` for `last_tag = "v"`, which this diff removed. `find` returned -1, so the after-rule-3 half held for any order. The pin is now anchored on `last_tag = last_stamped_tag(tags, tag_version)` and starts its chain with `-1 <`, so a missing anchor fails it.
3. The self-test ran the release.yml steps with no bound, so an endless read-back hung it instead of failing it. Both step seams now go through one runner, `_run_step`. It starts `bash -e -c <step>` in its own session, waits up to `RELEASE_STEP_TIMEOUT_S` (10 s) and kills the whole process group at that bound, returning `None`, which every caller's `== 0` / `== 1` check reads as FAIL. Two smaller fixes go with it: the publish stub's read count tolerates an empty file (`-1`), and the tree step uses the same runner (one more seam found by the census in Figures).

Alternatives considered for (3), and why each lost: (a) `subprocess.run(..., timeout=)`, which this branch took first (cb0909079). The kill reaches only bash, so the stub `gh` it started kept writing in the temporary directory. In 10 runs of the unbounded mutant at 60fb6879, 2 crashed with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''`. With the read made tolerant, 1 run in 10 still crashed with `OSError: [Errno 39] Directory not empty` while the directory was being removed. Killing the process group removes the cause, and 20 runs out of 20 then fail cleanly (Figures). (b) `TemporaryDirectory(ignore_cleanup_errors=True)` hides the symptom and leaves a live stub behind. (c) Bounding only by the CI job's timeout is what the review found: a hang, not a FAIL. Alternatives for the base fix: (a) reading the base from the tag list alone, ignoring VERSION, loses the case where VERSION is ahead of every tag (a first stamp after a manual VERSION fix). (b) Hand tags listed by name would be a spelling list the next hand tag defeats. (c) Deleting or retagging v7.1.2 is excluded by the brief.

## Head

3240.title: R10-PLANTED-DEFECT-AUDIT: planted defect audit

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 over-fire: a sustained trip dispatches once per sliding cut (37 audits for model:sonnet in 5.4 days) and one failed run leaves UNREADABLE in the digest forever

bus-nonce: bd1ba3ae797ee537a33db5779fb2cb39

Round 1 (first-round adversarial fix review), head f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4, merge base 9315526f8dca6dcd07f9cf3f2685bd1dd633b4f6, three-dot diff.

## Block

1. **The cut key slides with every new verdict, so one sustained trip is many dispatches, and the body does not state it.** Claim (body, Figures): a cut is keyed by the arm line's printed first..last verdict span, and its only stated limit is the missing year. Evidence: the span is the first verdicts of the arm's last N PRs, so each new reviewed PR on a tripped arm moves it and the row emits a fresh `DISPATCH` line on the next 1800 s pass. Harness (mine, ev/sweep.sh): `review_strength.py --window X=2026-09-07T00:00Z..<T> --guardrail` at every hour T from 2026-11-01T00:00Z to 2026-11-06T09:00Z on the bus as fetched 2026-11-06 (2091 verdicts), counting distinct (arm, cut) keys among would-trip lines, which is exactly the row's memory key. RESULT: model:sonnet would-trip at 125/126 hourly cuts with **37 distinct keys**, all at 1/126 with 1; 38 dispatches in 5.4 days from one sustained trip, each auditing a last-20 window that overlaps the previous one in up to 19 of 20 PRs (ev/sweep-summary.txt, ev/sweep-raw.txt). Hourly sampling undercounts the row's 30-minute cadence. Perturbation: the same sweep's all arm, tripping at one cut, yields one dispatch, so the multiplicity is the slide, not the harness. The ruling's "one per tripped arm and cut" admits this reading, but the brief asks that the cut key's limit be stated and judged; the stated limit (year) is negligible and the real one is not stated. Fix either way: key a dispatch by trip episode (once per arm until it reads `ok`/`insufficient` again) or by a cut sharing no PR with the last dispatched cut for that arm, with a self-test case for a slid cut; or keep per-cut and state the measured rate in the body for the owner to confirm.

2. **One failed `review_strength` run leaves `audit-dispatch: UNREADABLE` in the digest until the next new trip.** Claim (instrument doc, docstring): only a failed run is UNREADABLE. Evidence: `audit_dispatch` writes the job file only on UNREADABLE or on a new dispatch (`if new:`), so a recovered pass with nothing new never clears the UNREADABLE line; roster_drain, the precedent the comment cites, clears its HOLD-STALE line on an idle pass. Harness: ev/stale_probe.py drives the real `audit_dispatch` with a fake runner through trip, fail, recover-same-cut, recover-ok, ok-again. RESULT: after the failure the digest reads `audit-dispatch: UNREADABLE review_strength boom` at every one of the three recovered passes (ev/stale-probe.txt). Perturbation: the first pass (trip) writes the DISPATCH line and no UNREADABLE, so the stuck line is the failure's. `--fetch` hits the network every 30 min, so a transient failure is expected, and a stale UNREADABLE is a false actionable line on the orchestrator's one wake. Fix: on a readable pass with nothing new, rewrite the job without the UNREADABLE line (keeping any DISPATCH lines), with a self-test case and a mutant for it.

## Findings

- Surviving mutant: dropping the `" unclassified " not in ln` filter from `arms` (ev/mutants.txt, `unclassified_kept`) leaves the self-test at 116/0: no case feeds output whose only GUARDRAIL line is the unclassified one, which the filter exists to report as UNREADABLE. Carry: R10-PLANTED-DEFECT-AUDIT

## Evidence

- Head measured: f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 (ev/HEAD.txt); still the PR head at verdict time per the PR read.
- CI: `merge_train.py classify f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 --pr 3240` -> `GREEN f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 pending: none red: none`, rc=0 (ev/classify.txt). Red checks on this head: none, matching the body.
- Merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` rc=0, tree d4472e1d (ev/merge-tree.txt).
- Self-tests at head: beat_jobs 116 checks 0 failed, review_strength 116/0, beatd 119/0; at origin/main (null control): beat_jobs 107/0, review_strength 116/0 (ev/selftests-head.txt, ev/selftests-main.txt). Body figures 116/107/116/119 re-derived.
- entities.py: ALL 2632 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED at head and at origin/main; structure.py: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED at both (ev/entities-structure.txt). prepr.sh not re-run (CI cited, fix-review step 11).
- Stated mutants planted by hand in a temp copy, each named case red with self-test rc=1 and green at the head: audit_trip_any_arm (trip case and ok/insufficient null case FAIL), audit_no_memory (repeat null FAIL), audit_key_arm_only (repeat null and second-arm case FAIL), audit_rc_ignored (failed-run case FAIL). Extra: dropping `ctx.remember` and forcing the write on an idle pass are both killed (ev/mutants.txt).

One `read_text` now decides absent (`FileNotFoundError`, return the index; `Owner.create`'s hard-link arbitrates) against broken, and a broken slot is reaped through `_steal(path, None)`. Repair round 2 (verdict/3243, blocked at 3cbcbd5d: mutation-vacuous) adds the acceptance cases that pin the reap and its put-back, and one production change: `_steal` removes a directory-valued grave (`shutil.rmtree`) instead of raising `IsADirectoryError` out of `take_slot`.

Alternatives that lost: a lock around `_free_slot` (the pool takes no flock by design); a retry loop on the test side (hides the race); an inode re-check before the rename (narrows, does not close, and adds a second look of the kind this PR removes).

Carry 0: the free-slot race left open by PR 3170 (item 42008ca4), closed by this diff.
Carry 1: the gate-lease `_free_slot` `is_file` time-of-check/time-of-use race, closed by this diff; its delay-only plant is the null control above, made exact in `delayed_read`.
Carry 2: the group's own roster carry (`Carry: R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU`), discharged by this pull request.

`411270a40b14a235482fa37c2af55132cfc74760` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

## Mutation proof

Every row: mutate `tests/gate_lock.py`, run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/gate_lock.py --accept`, restore. Null control row: unmutated head.

| mutant | change | result |
|---|---|---|
| null | none | `ALL 46 gate lock acceptance checks PASSED` |

The M4 and directory cases use `_free_slot` plus `create`, not `take_slot`: `take_slot` retries a lost create forever, so with the reap deleted the first version of these cases hung (`timeout` rc=124) instead of going red. The final cases fail fast (rc=1, measured above). Reviewer M2 and M5 are not rebuilt: M2 (second read, reap via `_steal`) is near-equivalent because `_steal` puts back the rival; M5 (FileNotFoundError as broken) is equivalent because `_steal` returns on a missing path and the create arbitrates.

- M4 (delete the `_steal(path, None)` line): `ALL 42 ... PASSED`. R10-HOTFIX-SAV-ESTIMATE part 2 (part 1 merged as #3220), topic r10-sav-wood-heat. This is repair round 5, after fix review round 4 blocked `8bc540e0` as ci-red on CodeQL code-scanning alert 50.

## Re-cut

This is past the third round, so this body replaces the earlier ones. Every figure below was re-taken in this pass, at the head named under `## Head`.

**Carry A (owner ruling, tvofi 2026-11-04).** The reference has no wood, and wood's heat counts in the saving. Wherever wood is configured, the saving the integration states says that it includes wood's heat and excludes firewood's cost.

**What the PR builds.**
- `wood_fuel.py` `saving_includes_wood(data)` is the one definition. It is `True` where wood is configured (`show_whatif`).
- The receipt event (`notifier.py` `_monthly_receipt`) and the `MonthlySavingsSensor` attribute `saving_includes_wood` both read that definition.
- The card's receipt (`receiptHtml`) and savings table (`_savingsPageHtml`) show `savings.wood_note` on a wood house.
- The "Monthly receipt" message in `blueprints/automation/notifications.yaml` appends the card's `savings.wood_note` text, guarded by `data.saving_sek is not none and data.saving_includes_wood`. There is one wording, the card's.
- `docs/automations.md`, `docs/dashboard-card.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md` and the README's sensor row say so.
- `tools/policy/agreement.mjs` `SHARED_GRAMMARS` registers the card-string extractor that the pin and the render harness share, as `identical:`.
- The five `coord_*` golden captures each gain the one boolean key. They are claimed in `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` and were not re-recorded.

**This round: the CodeQL red, fixed at the root.** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_receipt_render.py` built `jinja2.Environment()`, whose autoescape is off, and CodeQL flagged that as alert 50, `py/jinja2/autoescape-false`. The harness now builds `jinja2.Environment(autoescape=True)`. The alert is not suppressed or dismissed.
- Why `autoescape=True` and not `select_autoescape()`: `select_autoescape()` keys on a template file's extension. This harness builds its template from a string, so the result would depend on that function's `default_for_string` argument. `autoescape=True` states the setting directly.
- The reviewer's warning, handled deliberately: autoescape escapes only an expression's output (`{{ … }}`), never a template's literal text. The note is literal text in the blueprint, outside any `{{ }}`, so its apostrophe is not escaped. The harness therefore counts the note as written, with no escaped form and no `Markup` wrapper. The expressions in the message render numbers and the currency code, which contain no escapable character. So the rendered text is the same as what Home Assistant's template engine (a sandboxed environment with autoescape off) sends.
- The perturbation that shows the warning was real but does not apply here: on a copy of the blueprint with the note moved inside a `{{ "…" }}` expression, the harness reads `RESULT wood notes=0 want=1 DEFECT`. The apostrophe becomes `'` there. So if a later edit moves the note into an expression, the wood arm goes red loudly rather than passing silently.
- Alternatives considered. Dismissing the alert with a reason: rejected, because the brief requires a root fix and a dismissal leaves the pattern in the tree. `select_autoescape(default_for_string=False)`: rejected, because it is still autoescape-off for this string template, and CodeQL's query reads it the same way.

**The pin and why it is a source pin.** `tests/entities.py` loads the blueprint and finds the "Monthly receipt" option. It requires three things: the card's `savings.wood_note` text occurs exactly once in the message; it sits inside `{% if data.saving_sek is not none and data.saving_includes_wood %}`; and the event declares `saving_includes_wood` (`notifier.EVENT_DATA`). It does not render the template, because CI's interpreter (`venv-ci`) has no jinja2. That is a design choice, stated here. The render harness measures the rendering under `venv-ha`.

**The class rule.** The question: where does the integration state the metered saving to a user?
- R1: `git grep -n -E 'savings_sek|saving_sek|savings_months|plan_monthly_savings|MonthlySavingsSensor|EVENT_MONTHLY_RECEIPT|monthly_receipt|saving_includes_wood' -- custom_components blueprints docs README.md ':!docs/design' ':!custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www'`
- R2 (prose that states the saving without naming a key): `git grep -n -i -E 'monthly receipt|savings page|plan monthly savings|than a plain thermostat' -- docs README.md blueprints ':!docs/design'`
- R3 (the card's keys): `git grep -n -o -E '\b(savings|receipt|headline)\.[a-z_]+' -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js`

`docs/design/2026-09-05-monthly-savings-history/` is excluded. It is a dated design record that recounts a past design (fixer step 10).

**Carry B (wood's unforeseen heat).** The `wood-plant` arm of `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_wood_reference.py` puts the fire in the plant only, unknown to the plan, over 9 fires (4, 8 and 12 kW; 06:00, 17:00 and 22:00; 4 h each). The figure is the applied calibration's error against the true meter factor `m`, less the same error with no fire. At `m` 0.8 and 1.0 it is +0.00 % at every fire. At `m` 1.2 it is mean −1.95 %, min −4.50, max +0.00, sd 1.47. `docs/how-it-works.md` states that as an upper bound for this simulated house.

**A measured limit, not changed here.** On a wood house the floor (calibration at least 1.0) also stops the calibration correcting a model that reads the meter high. With no fire at `m` 0.8 the error is +25.00 % (1/m − 1), and the row reads 44.9 % against 31.1 % at `m` 1.0. This follows from two owner rulings as built. `docs/how-it-works.md` says so, and changing it is the owner's call.

## Head

3246.body:
Part of #201. Hotfix topic r10-gate-busy-defer, repair round 3. Two `gate` jobs at one head each deferred to the other, so neither judged. Both were edit runs whose prelude had left `pr-contract` to a code run (C3). Each listed `pr-contract` skipped under the caller's bare name and never listed the `pr-contract / pr-contract` its title's workset owes. So `prelude.judging` read each as still adding a source, `gate.busy` named it, and `gate.deferring` set the wait bound to 0. Both published `FAIL run(s) [<the other>] ... their gate decides` within 9 s of starting (finder's logs: #3241 head 95c7e604, attempt 2 of runs 42192623509 and 42193153511).

The fix, in `tools/ci/gate.py`:
- `busy()`: a LATER run whose `gate` has started (`in_progress` or `completed`, the one predicate `started()`) is not waited on. Of two started gates, the lower id decides and the higher waits on it. A gate merely listed `waiting` is no proof (R3-2).
- `judge()`: a deferring gate waits only when ALL the runs it waits on have started their gate. Beside any other run (a code run, or an edit run in its prelude or units) it publishes the deferral at once, as main does, because such a run may sit in `prelude.wait_sources` waiting on this one. `busy()` leaves out later started gates, so every started run a deferring gate waits on is an earlier one, and the waits run down in id and cannot close a cycle.

This round adds no production line. It pins the `all` in that rule. The round-2 review's mutant M24 (`and not all(` to `and not any(` in `judge()`) re-opened the prelude/gate cycle and survived the self-test. This round adds the review's mixed scene as a self-test case and M24 to the mutant table.

Alternatives that lost:
- Make `prelude.judging` read a gate `in_progress` as judging (round 2's first fix, 3c66c9b3, reverted by b0bccab4, a disclosed self-correction). The approved design's replay reads DIFFERS on it: a gate `in_progress` while a unit re-runs must be waited on.
- Teach `judging()` to read the skipped bare `pr-contract` as finished. A skipped caller cannot be told apart in the listing from one the platform has not expanded yet.
- C3 at once only beside a code run (c0c60886, round 1). It re-opened the cycle with a later edit run in its prelude (M22 now pins this).

Claim: the brief's settle item (1) asks for no cycle of waits; the body's seam disposition says `prelude.wait_sources` is "already guarded ... a deferring edit run it waits on still ends", and the gate.py docstring says the waits stay acyclic. The judge() C3 change (`bound = 0` only when a code run is among the waited runs) breaks that for a gate-vs-prelude pair that main handled at once.

The scene: A = deferring edit run (its prelude ran EDIT_UNDER_CODE; its `pr-contract` listed skipped under the bare name) at its gate; C = the code run it deferred to, already completed; B = a later edit run at the same head still in its prelude. B's prelude: defer_to() is None (C finished), so it calls wait_sources, and waits_on(B, A) is True (earlier run) and judging(A) is False (the same `pr-contract / pr-contract` misread this PR names), so B waits on A for up to WAIT_MAX_S 8700 s. A's gate: busy(A) = [B] (B's gate not started, so the new tie-break does not exempt it); B is an edit run, so the new C3 condition is False and A's bound is GATE_WAIT_MAX_S. A waits on B and B waits on A; the cycle is broken only by A's 720 s bound, and A then publishes the same red deferral main published at 0 s. Carry: dismissed: the blocked defect itself, settled by this PR's re-cut

Evidence (reviewer's own probe, disclosed as mine, not the finder's harness: ev/probe_snippet.py inserted into a scratch copy of gate.py's self-test; output in ev/probe_cycle.txt):

- So at this head B's own verdict, the head's deciding one, comes 720 s later than at the base, a gate runner is held 12 minutes, and A still ends red, to be re-judged by the sweep. Every head with zero judging gates is avoided (B judges after A ends), but a wait cycle is reintroduced. None of r10_gate_defer_race.py's six scenarios (2754, 2754-red, pair, cascade, editcode, single) puts a later run in its prelude beside a deferring gate, so its `DEADLOCK no` lines do not cover this.

Perturbation: the scene differs from the self-test's `busy-defer: the higher deferring edit gate waits on the lower` only in that the waited edit run has not started its gate. Making B's gate `in_progress` (its prelude done) restores the claimed behaviour, because the tie-break then applies one way and B no longer waits in wait_sources.

A remedy the fixer may weigh (not prescribed): keep C3's zero bound unless every waited run is an earlier run whose gate has started (`r["id"] < ctx["run_id"]` and its gate in STARTED). Only such a run is known to end without waiting on this one. Add the probe's scene as a self-test case and a mutant, and a prelude-phase scenario to r10_gate_defer_race.py. - Carry 3 (P344): the source says "read the head's check-runs once (gh_read.py)". bus.sh:613 calls `gh api` directly with no retry, reads one page of 100 with no pagination, and discards stderr. A failed read leaves `fixing` empty, so the hold fails open and dispatch proceeds without a line saying the read failed. Evidence: pipeline exit status is paste's, so `|| fixing=""` never fires (code reading at bus.sh:613-615). Fix: route through gh_read.py, or at least print a line when the read fails. The source names "confirm on a second review commit whose tree equals the first's leaves verdict/<pr>'s tip at the first, posted commit" and says "removing the tree comparison must fail arms (a) and (b)". 3251.body:
ref_privacy read a cloud seat's own paths as a host identity. On uid 0 with HOME=/root, a line citing that home was refused as home-directory. With HOME=/nonexistent, it was refused as home-directory and account-name, where `nonexistent` is the name derived from the placeholder home's basename. `Identity.of_host` now drops homes that name no person before it derives names from them: the no-home placeholder, and a public account's own home (`_public_home`). `_HOST_PATH` is untouched, so a real `/Users/<name>` or `/home/<name>` path still refuses everywhere.

Repair (round 2): the drop also covers the CI runner's home and this seat's. Two self-test arms planted the real `$HOME` and expected a refusal, so both went red at the PR head and passed on main: heartbeat.sh's "a message carrying the host's home directory is refused and the reachable ref does not move", and gh_comment.py's `arm_privacy_post_dry_run_refuses_this_hosts_home`. Each arm now plants a private home outside `/home` and `/Users`, so only the home rule can refuse it. Each also gains a null control that passes another path under the same planted host. The alternative was to keep public homes in the identity and exempt them only in `--check`. It lost: two readers of one identity would disagree about the same host, and roster lines would still be refused under `guard`.

Carry 1 (the #3239 round-1 fix review, ref_privacy on a uid-0 cloud seat): closed here. The passwd name root was already in `PUBLIC_ACCOUNTS`.

Carry 2 (cloud seat identity, found 11-06): closed here, at the source. `cloud-setup.sh` already exported `GIT_AUTHOR_*` and `GIT_COMMITTER_*`, and its self-test already held the null control "control: without the exports the config identity authors the commit". The values were the wrong identity, `seat`. The seat identity is now `hpo-fixer` at the owner's noreply address, the one `dev/programme/HANDOVER.md`'s Identity bullet names. It is set in `cloud-setup.sh` (`SEAT_NAME`/`SEAT_EMAIL`) and in `cloud_dispatch.py` (`SEAT_NAME, SEAT_EMAIL`, which also feeds the fixer and probe setup line). A new `cloud_dispatch.py` check pins the value: the existing arms compare against the constant, so they read green for any identity, and that is how `seat` went unnoticed. This pin encodes a design choice.

The failures are "a uid-0 cloud seat (root) judges its own paths and names no leak" (['home-directory']) and "a uid-0 cloud seat (nonexistent) judges its own paths and names no leak" (['home-directory', 'account-name']). R10-ROSTER-WRITE-SWEEP, repair after fix-review round 1 (blocked at `21be201c`): the roster write path's residue in `tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py` and `tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py`, built carry by carry, each with a self-test arm and a plant. Part of #201.

What the repair changes, by review finding:

1. selftest-red. `roster_queue.py --self-test` crashed under `python3 -I` because `_run_batch` imported `roster_edit` from the edit checkout (absent from the self-test's throwaway clone) and ignored the `editor` it was passed. One resolution now serves both paths: `resolve_editor` is `--editor`, else the `roster_edit.py` beside the script; `load_editor` loads that same file for `run --batch` (refusing, unexecuted, a file that has no `batch_edit`), and the single-op path runs that same file as a subprocess. The edit checkout supplies the roster and the shims only.
2. Red checks: named below, with the cheaper detector.
3. Forward-carry: the deferred items are built where buildable (the marker guard, carry 15, is now built: the carry says "Owner-ordered: no", so nothing waited on an owner), dismissed with a reason, or routed with a `Carry:` and its control stated as a precondition.
4. Carry 8's read-only roster instrument is built: `roster_queue.py show [GROUP] [--ref R] [--stage S]` and `diff REF_A REF_B`, `git show` reads only, `diff` exits 1 when the refs differ, with arms and plants Q10-Q12.

Dispositions by the review packet's 1-based numbering of the 17 roster carries (the review's own labels above and below, "carry 4", "carry 8", "carry 9", "carry 13(2)", "carry 15", "carry 16", are the verdict's and the brief's order, not these): lettered proposal labels, built (Carry 1); the M4-M6 plants, answered by W1-W15 and Q1-Q13 (Carry 2); the stale note, built (Carry 3); closing-destination refusal, built (Carry 4); `pr` in set-resume, built, its data edits are under Forward-carry (Carry 5); the overlap refusal and phase branches, built (Carry 6); `append-group @file`, built (Carry 7); the host-path gate, built (Carry 8); ordering after the schema group, holds, R10-ORCH-ROSTER-SCHEMA being absorbed (Carry 9); the brief-route edit-briefs, data edits under Forward-carry (Carry 10); the trailing-comment grammar, built (Carry 11); the word-start comment rule, built (Carry 12); `--mark` and `all`, built, with the arm for a pass cut short (Carry 13); the s9 bulk defects, docstring, incremental marks, comment parse and `--batch`, built (Carry 14); the loop and its subcommands, plus the read-only `show` and `diff` of this repair, built (Carry 15); the marker guard, now built (Carry 16); `absorbed --into`, op built, data edits under Forward-carry (Carry 17).

Also: carry 13(2) (the drain's timeout loses marks) has its own arm now: a pass that dies mid-queue keeps the marks already written (`run --mark`). The lane marker (`HPO_ROSTER_LANE=queue-runner`) is set by the queue runner, `carry_fold.py` and the two harnesses that call structural ops directly (`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_roster_push_race.sh`, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_which_roster.py`); `set-stage`, `append-group`, `set-resume` and `mark-carry` stay directly callable, as the carry specifies. A caller that sets the variable by hand is out of scope. This changes what a seat may call directly (policy-adjacent): it needs the owner's approving review before merging.

Merged `origin/main` (30638cf0c, 2026-11-06 16:15 UTC) into the branch cleanly; `tools/pr/prepr.sh` is re-run at the head below.

## Head

`ce7ae991b55800a344d1f1bfeeb639654c0d433e` merges main `198b8f7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`d30513cdca74c3c6b768c38395d4fb5c3b19b56c` merges main `af56818` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

2b27bf482e33ab4fd7e1fdb867353a74b8da10a3

## Mutation proof

`python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_roster_ops_mutants.py` (all 105 plants, the driver restores each file byte for byte; it prints `plants: 105, without a FAIL line: ['C6']`). Every plant of this group is killed by at least one FAIL line, none by a crash: W1 12, W2 3, W3 2, W4 1, W5 1, W6 3, W7 1, W8 1, W9 2, W10 2, W11 4, W12 1, W13 1, W14 1, W15 1, Q1 2, Q2 3, Q3 1, Q4 2, Q5 3, Q6 1, Q7 1, S7 2, K8 4, K12 2, H2 1, and the plants this repair adds: Q8 2 (the batch path loads the edit checkout's editor), Q9 1 (the loader executes a file that is no roster_edit), Q10 1 (`diff` blind to removed groups), Q11 3 (`diff` compares a carry by count), Q12 1 (`show --stage` unfiltered), W16 8 (the lane guard dropped), W17 1 (`set-stage` made structural), Q13 1 (the runner does not set the marker).

Failing test first: at the head before the fix, `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test` exits 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'roster_edit'` at `_run_batch`; after it, 52 checks, 0 failed.

Inherited, not this diff's: plant C6 (roster_edit.py, from R10-ROSTER-OPS) is `rc=1` with no FAIL line, a crash (`KeyError: 'carry'` in `op_drop_carry` on the mutated tree); the same result at `origin/main` (30638cf0c, `r10_roster_ops_mutants.py C6` in a detached worktree of it). The plant is killed, by a crash in a later arm; two attempts to turn it into a FAIL line crashed in yet another arm and were reverted. Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: C6 killed by crash, not by FAIL line).

## Null control

Each refusal has its passing twin in the same self-test. New here: a `run --batch` with no `--editor` resolves the roster_edit.py beside the script and never the edit checkout (`resolve_editor` arm); a stub editor passed with `--editor` is the file both the batch's fallback and the single-op path run; `diff` of the same ref twice is empty; `show` without `--stage` lists both groups; `show` and `diff` leave the working tree and index unchanged; `set-stage`, `append-group`, `set-resume` and `mark-carry` need no marker; a structural op with the marker is accepted; a marker with another value is not the lane. Earlier nulls hold: a numbered label and text naming no proposal land; a bare `append-group` path lands; overlap on the index file only lands; append-carry to an open group with no PR lands with no WARN; a queue run without `--mark` leaves the queue byte-identical; a batch of one is byte-identical to the single-op roster; a quoted `'a # b'`, `@/p/b#1.txt` and `s6-batch8.md#P70` keep their `#`; a held line whose batch file is absent stays held. The unmodified base (b36679ce) under `python3 -I`: `roster_queue.py --self-test` 17 checks, 0 failed (the base has no batch path).

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test`: 52 checks, 0 failed at the head (17 at the merge base b36679ce)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py --self-test`: 242 checks, 0 failed (191 at the merge base)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py --self-test`: 63 checks, 0 failed (60 at the merge base)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/r10_roster_ops_mutants.py --self-test`: 321 checks, 0 failed (231 at the merge base)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/carry_fold.py --self-test`: 6 checks, 0 failed
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`: ALL 2637 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED (run before the merge of `origin/main`; rerun by `prepr.sh` at the head)
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: MODE: SCOPED, runs `tests/entities.py` only
- Absorbed groups with no `resume.absorbed_into`, python json over the r10 roster at the merge base: 13 of 13. This is why the write-time check is at the op and brief_lint is unchanged.

## Red checks

At PR head `21be201c`, across all 68 check runs (all pages, `ev/check-runs.tsv` of the review):

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` (concluded failure): the `roster_queue.py --self-test` crash under `python3 -I`, finding 1. Cheaper detector: the same command CI runs, `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test`, about 10 s locally; standing cost: one line in this handoff's figures. The driver `r10_roster_ops_mutants.py` now runs every target's self-test under `-I` too, so a plant is measured the way CI runs it.
- `pr-contract / pr-contract` (concluded failure): refused because `governance / instrument-self-tests` was red and `## Red checks` did not name it; it clears with the repair and this section.

No other check run concluded failure at `21be201c` (the first-pass `gate` run was superseded; the three later `gate` runs concluded success). No open `code-scanning alert` is known at that head.

## Forward-carry

- Carry 13(2), the drain's timeout: Carry: R10-ROSTER-WRITE-SWEEP | dismissed: the drain script is not in the tree and `run --mark` writes each mark as its op pushes, pinned by the arm "a pass that dies mid-queue keeps the marks already written".
- Roster DATA edits these ops enable, which write the roster branch this seat may not write. Each carries its control as a precondition. Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: carry 4, `set-resume --field pr` for every done group lacking `resume.pr`, starting R10-FLOW-RECORD-PITCH = 2836; precondition: the count of done groups lacking `pr` is measured at the roster seat's own base, and a group's `pr` is read from `dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md`, never guessed).
- Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: carry 9, one `edit-brief` per live group whose brief still names `the seat pushes refs only, through tools/audit/seat/handoff_push.sh`; precondition: a python count of that phrase over live groups' briefs is the control, and reads 0 afterwards; 64 groups carry it in total at the review's base, 1 live).
- Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: carry 16 data, `set-stage <G> absorbed --into <host>` for the ten folded groups of the carry and for the 13 absorbed groups with no host; precondition: afterwards `carry_audit.py roster` reports each group's carries as REROUTED to its host, and the lint refusing an absorbed group with no `absorbed_into` is built only after those data edits land, because it would fail the roster as it stands: 13 of 13 lack the field today).
- Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: plant C6 killed by a crash, not by a FAIL line, as above).

Root cause for the v7.1.2 process-worker hang, group R10-RCA-PROCESS-WORKER-HANG (trigger 1, the defect reached a release). The fix is #3232; this branch touches none of #3232's code or test files. Both PRs change `tests/closures.json`, a shared generated ledger with a merge driver: `git merge-tree --write-tree bba5b4d4d HEAD` (#3232's head) exits 0.

- Analysis: `dev/audit/rca/r10-process-worker-hang.md`, cited by the `_rca` entry `R10-RCA-PROCESS-WORKER-HANG` in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`. That entry is also on class `N-reap-lock`'s `rca` list, and the class now carries a `barrier_refusal`, which `fold_ledger.py check` requires once a class has an in-tree RCA.
- **Cause:** `_run_in_process` read the reply with `pickle.load(stdout)` and no deadline while holding `_PROCESS_LOCK`. The read has been unbounded since 8542e51cb (first tag v6.3.15). The worker was computing, not dead: one core stayed busy for about 55 minutes with memory flat. No tool can now say which job it ran, on which inputs, or why it did not finish; the document lists what is known.
- **Why the stop did not free the lock: not reproduced.** At v7.1.2 the kill-first stop path frees the read in 0.00 s, both for a silent job and for a CPU-spinning one.
- **Process state (c).** Round 9's D1 seat read this lock and this read (D1-s2-05), but it measured stop latency against a finite solve. The double in its check ends the read when the worker is killed. D1 step 5 injects exceptions, and a silent peer never raises one. The #511 checks drive only a worker that fails.
- **Countermeasure.** Step 5 of `dev/governance/dimensions/D1.md` becomes "Guards, waits": each peer wait (pipe, child, lock) is driven by a live, silent peer, with the instrument `dev/audit/harnesses/silent_peer_waits.py`, "unless the wait is its own idle state", which admits `run_worker`'s `pickle.load(stdin)` (the idle worker waits for its parent; the parent's close is EOF). The brief was at its line and token caps, so the change is paid for by tightening step 5 and step 6; no cap moved. **This is a policy change: it merges only on the owner's approving review**, and it addresses state (c) by changing the unit that missed the defect.
- **Code-side candidate, not carried.** `ThermalModel._stability_substeps` was raised by D1-s2 and closed by D1-s2-02 in round 9's `leads.json`, as covered by `_FORECAST_FIELD_RANGE`. The substep count stays uncapped (`max(1, ...)` in thermal_model.py). The RCA records it as an unmeasured candidate this seat did not carry.
- **Cost test.** The wait arm costs about 58 s per release against about 475 s per release for the defect. A per-PR static arm costs about 100 s per release and also passes, but only on one instance. It cannot land green before #3232 merges, so it is left to the owner (the document's `## Needs tvofi`).

## Approval

Awaiting the owner's approving review. The diff changes `dev/governance/dimensions/D1.md`, step 5 ("Guards, waits"). That is a change to what a D1 finder must do: drive every wait on a peer with a live, silent peer, unless the wait is its own idle state. It addresses process state (c).

## Head

`61187afe6cfdc4416f161e23111571bc50d25d9c` merges main `294a880` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`e17fadc1795ebbaaf0f01ed067fbb59aeba90dee` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`f914e1d9c79ffd4e5f1017ab43ee6ffbc0b4230e`, the final code head, pushed to `handoff-wip/r10-rca-process-worker-hang`. It contains origin/main `28482eceeb6b9809e44b12d80fc994282cc21645` (merge `04f41926f`), so the merge base is origin/main and main has not moved since that merge. All figures below were taken at this head on 2026-11-06 22:26Z. Drive and scan rows on other trees were taken from `git archive` checkouts of the tree named.

## Mutation proof

This diff adds no production code, so the proofs break the instrument and the fix it reads:
- **Scan arm.** With the harness's `pickle.load` predicate replaced by `if False:` (a scratch copy), the scan over this head's package drops the defect's site: `pickle.load` lines 2 → 0, `RESULT unbounded_sites=6` → `4`.

Owner ruling (tvofi 2026-11-06), verbatim: "The HTML plan seems to incorrectly place some instrument or CI fixes in the core model lane, fix that".

Where the lane is decided: `roster_lane` in `tools/plan/replan.py` writes each group's `lane` into the plan JSON, and `tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py` only draws that field. `roster_lane` placed a group by `kind` (`instrument`, `policy`), then by a list of name prefixes, and **every group neither rule placed fell through to Core model**. So a new CI hotfix, an RCA seat, a tooling chore or a doc group was drawn as core-model work, and the stamp cadence counted it as production.

The fix is at that source, not per group. The kind and name rules keep their precedence, so Learners, Product UX, Replay and Docs placements by name do not change. After them, `roster_lane` reads:
1. **The files the group owns** (`files` + `hot_files`). When every one is an instrument, CI or record path (`tools/`, `tests/`, `.github/`, `.claude/`, `dev/`, `docs/`, or a root record such as `CLAUDE.md`), the group is Instruments. It is Docs instead when it is a `doc` kind, or when it touches user docs (`docs/`, `README.md`) without landing a tool (`tools/`, `.github/`, `.claude/`). A single `custom_components/` file or a bare filename, in either list, keeps it core.
2. **Then a tool-landing kind or roster class**, for a group whose roster names no file: `kind` in `INSTRUMENT_KINDS` (`instrument`, `policy`, `rca`, `tooling`) or `class: instrument`. `work_class` already priced those kinds as instruments. It now reads the same tuple, so the lane and the duration class cannot disagree on which kinds land tools.

Alternatives considered:
- (a) Reading the roster's own `lane` code. It is not a lane in this sense: production groups owning only `custom_components/` files carry `lane: IN`. So it lost.
- (b) Adding the misplaced names to the prefix list. That is a per-group spelling list, and the next CI hotfix would fall out of it again (fixer.md step 17). So it lost too.

**Round 2 (this repair).** The review blocked at `8ff3432a` as mutation-vacuous. Dropping `hot_files` from `_owned_lane` (m8) survived the self-test, because every control put the bare filename or the `custom_components/` path in `files`. The production code is unchanged in this round. The self-test gains four `hot_files` cases on a group with `files: ["tools/x.py"]`:
- an integration hot file (`custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/x.py`) stays Core model;
- a bare `coordinator.py` hot file stays Core model;
- a bare tool basename (`merge_train.py`) in `hot_files` stays Core model, which is the conservatism the brief's rule (1) prescribes and the reviewer's follow-up asked to pin;
- an instrument-path hot file (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) keeps it Instruments.

m8 is now killed by three of them. I re-ran all twelve of the reviewer's mutants myself, and all are killed.

## Head

`c7c5cef52a49bed59ee4c8a42e495ef2dae30db5` is this PR's head, and every figure below was re-taken at it (worktree of the head, 2026-11-07). Its code is the handoff code head `aa5c0505b73c77d1ab5a650af2da58759b8b307a` (`8ff3432a965df930fb54e7aa6ffd52bf210e5f3f`, the reviewed head, plus a merge of origin/main at `f2a015142714383722bf49d7ab20d8398ec9674c` and one commit that adds the self-test cases): `git diff aa5c0505 c7c5cef5 -- tools dev tests` is empty and `replan.py` is byte-identical between them. The three-dot diff against the merge base `f2a015142` touches `tools/plan/replan.py` and `dev/programme/delivery/3265.md` only. `git diff 80016a71f f2a015142 -- tools/plan` is empty, so the main merge reaches nothing `replan.py` reads. origin/main is now `b4ec2f332fe3ab8dcf169bd3066276d3bb8848ab`; the head has not merged it, and the merge base is unchanged. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` ran clean (rc=0) at `aa5c0505`, whose tools are identical to the head's. This body re-take changed no code and pushed nothing to `fix/` or `handoff/`.

## Mutation proof

Method: for each mutant, take a `git archive` copy of the head, apply one exact string substitution to `tools/plan/replan.py` (it must match once), and run `python3 -I tools/plan/replan.py --self-test`. The unmutated copy (m0) exits rc=0 with no lane failure. The FAIL lines are the self-test's own check names.
- m1, delete `if owned := _owned_lane(group): return owned` → rc=1: `lane: a CI-only group is Instruments`, `lane: a tests-and-tools group is Instruments`, `lane: a docs-only doc group is Docs`, `lane: a user-docs group is Docs`, `lane null control: docs plus a tool is Instruments, not Docs`, `lane: user docs with a dev harness are Docs`, `lane: an instrument-path hot file keeps a tool group Instruments`

- m3, drop the `class == "instrument"` arm → rc=1: `lane: a roster class instrument with no files is Instruments`
- m4, `not all(` → `not any(` → rc=1: `lane null control: a mixed group stays Core model`, `lane null control: an integration hot file keeps a tool group Core model`, `lane null control: a bare hot filename keeps a tool group Core model`, `lane null control: a bare tool basename in hot_files stays Core model`
- m5, drop the `not files` guard → rc=1: `lane null control: a group with no files stays Core model`, `lane null control: a production group with no files stays Core model`
- m6, drop the tooling exclusion from `user_docs` → rc=1: `lane null control: docs plus a tool is Instruments, not Docs`

At the reviewed head `8ff3432a`, the same m8 substitution exits rc=0 with no lane failure. That is the block, reproduced, and it is the failing-test-first for this round.
- m9, remove `docs/` from `_NON_PRODUCT_PREFIXES` → rc=1: `lane: a user-docs group is Docs`, `lane null control: docs plus a tool is Instruments, not Docs`, `lane: user docs with a dev harness are Docs`
- m10, empty `_NON_PRODUCT_FILES` → rc=1: `lane: a docs-only doc group is Docs`, `lane: a user-docs group is Docs`, `lane: user docs with a dev harness are Docs`
- m11, remove `rca` from `INSTRUMENT_KINDS` → rc=1: `lane: an RCA group with no files is Instruments`

## Null control

  - a mixed tools + `custom_components/` group;

- Name rules keep precedence: R10-COP-GATE with only a `tools/` file stays Learners, and R10-DEEPLINK-CENSUS with `kind: rca` stays Product UX.

The same holds with a bare `hot_files: ["coordinator.py"]`, and `work_class` flips to `instrument` with it. So the arm that keeps a group touching the integration in the core lane, which is the brief's item-1 null control, is unpinned. The self-test's controls put the bare filename and the `custom_components/` path in `files` only. Yet on the live roster, bare names occur in `hot_files` (for example R10-FAHRENHEIT `hot_files: ["coordinator.py"]`).

- Live effect today: none. All 11 roster groups whose `files` are all non-product but whose `hot_files` are not are `kind: instrument`, so the kind rule places them before `_owned_lane` (`ev/m8-live.txt`). The block concerns the pin, not the current plan.

Today no open group hits this (my enumeration of every Core-model group at the head finds each owns a `custom_components/` file or is product or owner work with no files), and the brief's rule (1) prescribes this conservatism. The residual risk sits in roster data: the roster seat writing `hot_files` as bare names. ## Block

Round: first review of #3267 (R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC), at head `61f1ec71a428b43fc2965379ab08c6747d214e5b`. Role checked: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract I read is current.

The owner ruling the brief quotes is "There should already be tracked sweep templates/scripts for these, update them if needed". The PR body says the opposite: "Tracked counterparts: only `sweep_render.py` and `sweep_template.md` existed". That is false at the merge base `f2a01514`. `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py` (run by `beatd.py` from `beatd.jobs.json`) is the tracked script for the sweep's mechanical steps. Its `ROWS` are `tick-digest, owed-check, roster-drain, plan-beat, pulse, cancel-sweep, disk, opener, head-watch, audit-dispatch` (ev/base-beat_jobs-rows.txt, ev/base-beatd.jobs.json).

The new `tools/audit/seat/sweep_runner.sh` (ev/head-sweep_runner.sh) is a parallel loop. It re-implements six of those ten rows: the roster drain, `pulse.py`, `cancel_superseded.py sweep`, the disk floor with `worktree_gc.sh`, `replan.py` + `state_docs.py --push --mirror --plan` (plan-beat), and `owed_unactioned.py` (owed-check). The new `roster_drain.py` re-implements the `roster-drain` row's drain through `roster_queue.py run`, and its own page has to rule that "the two do not run together on one queue". Running both loops in one session runs `state_docs.py --push` twice against one state ref, with nothing to serialise them.

`sweep_template.md` now names both owners for the same step. (4b) says the beat's `plan-beat` row replans and pushes the state docs every 30 minutes. The new (4b+) says `sweep_runner.sh` re-renders and republishes them every second pass. Its consumer (`sweep_render.py` renders the template for the orchestrator) gets two contradictory instructions.

The sound shape is the one the ruling asks for. Make `sweep_gantt.py` and `verdict_audit.py` new rows of `beat_jobs.py`, with their lines going to the digest the orchestrator already reads. Add the `PLAN MOVED` compare to the `plan-beat` row. Fold the roster-drain differences (exact-line `#refused` + ROSTER-CASCADE/UNRUN) into the existing row or `roster_queue.py`. Do not ship a second loop, a second drain and a template step that duplicates (4b).

Harness: the base tree's `beat_jobs.py` ROWS against the runner's step list. Metric: the number of runner steps that already exist as a beat row, 6 of the runner's 9 steps. Perturbation: delete the runner's six duplicated steps. The template's (1b), (4b) and (4e) steps, run by beatd, still cover every one of them, so they are redundant, not new coverage.

## Findings

- Defect: `sweep_runner.sh` and `roster_drain.py` add a parallel sweep loop and drain beside `beat_jobs.py`/`beatd.py` instead of updating them (the owner's ruling), and `sweep_template.md` (4b+) contradicts (4b) on who replans and pushes the state docs. Claim, evidence, harness and metric are as in `## Block`. Repair: Gantt and verdict audit become `beat_jobs.py` rows, PLAN MOVED goes into `plan-beat`, and the runner and second drain are dropped. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: the body's "Tracked counterparts: only `sweep_render.py` and `sweep_template.md` existed" is false at the merge base (`beat_jobs.py`, `beatd.py`, `beatd.jobs.json`, `tick_loop.sh`), so the body's justification for adding files rather than updating them does not stand. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: alert 51's repair has no local check that reads the file mode. The 0o755 copy of `sweep_runner_selftest.py` (89f08728^) prints `sweep_runner self-test: 11 checks, 0 failed`, the same as the 0o700 head (ev/selftest-0o755.txt, ev/selftests-head.txt). The only detector that moves under the mutation is CodeQL `py/overly-permissive-file` on CI, as the body itself says. The repair is at the root (both `w(...)` callers pass 0o700, with no suppression), but the brief's "a named check goes red" holds only for CI's CodeQL. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: `.github/workflows/governance.yml`'s new step runs `sweep_runner_selftest.py` twice, because `sweep_runner.sh --self-test` already `exec`s it. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC

## Evidence

- HEAD reviewed: `61f1ec71a428b43fc2965379ab08c6747d214e5b` (ev/HEAD.txt); merge base `f2a015142714383722bf49d7ab20d8398ec9674c`; three-dot diff in ev/three-dot.diff (14 files, +813/-1).
- RESULT: self-tests at head: sweep_gantt 16 checks, 0 failed; verdict_audit 14 checks, 0 failed; roster_drain 9 checks, 0 failed; sweep_runner_selftest.py 11 checks, 0 failed; sweep_runner.sh --self-test 11 checks, 0 failed; selftest_wiring --check: 123 self-testing, 123 wired, 0 index gap(s). All five body figures re-derived.
- RESULT: self-test count unchanged by the repair: 11 checks, 0 failed at 0o755 (89f08728^) and at 0o700 (head). `sweep_runner_selftest.py` does not exist at the merge base, so there is no base-side count; the comparison is across the repair commit.

- RESULT: `## Head` names `61f1ec71` as merging code head `89f08728`, which is current. Its second paragraph still carries an older note about 89f08728 and prepr.
- Scope: no production code is touched. The scope is the sweep instruments plus the governance step, which is in the brief.
- Mutation proofs the body names (LIVE_H, the `held` guard, `--handoff-rows`, `#refused`) are pure-instrument mutants. They do not bear on the block, so I did not re-run them.
- CI: see the CI section appended below.

The one concluded red is `gate` (check run 128279140047, workflow run 42331132062), which concluded `failure` with an empty output. The code run 42331131423's jobs were still `in_progress` at that time (`tests / fast (3.14)`, `tests / coverage`, `tests / closures`, `governance / instrument-self-tests`, `codeql / Analyze (python)` among them), which matches the edit-run deferral R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER, so run 42331131423's gate decides. I could not read the gate's deferral text, because its check-run output is empty. ## Block

Round: second review of #3267 (R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC), at head `14a73c15e5f060069f0fd4831eb46a436bd14f1d`, merge base `294a880dae608502b62055775e34a5db93217b98`. `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` is empty.

The re-cut answers round 1's architecture finding. `sweep_runner.sh`, `sweep_runner_selftest.py` and `roster_drain.py` are gone. Gantt and verdict audit are now `beat_jobs.py` rows with `beatd.jobs.json` entries. `PLAN MOVED` is in `plan-beat`. (4b+) is gone, and (4b) has one owner. `git grep "sweep_runner|roster_drain.py" -- tools .github tests` finds only one history comment, in `beat_jobs_selftest.py`.

The re-cut does not keep the rows in sync with the tracked template, though. `Ctx` reads its overlay from `S/sweep-overlay.json`, which its own docstring calls "the same JSON `sweep_render.py` fills the sweep from" (`beat_jobs.py:34`, `:172`). `sweep_render.render` refuses any overlay key that is not in the template's `## Placeholders` table: `unknown: ... not in the placeholder table`. The new rows read `gantt_roster`, `gantt_acks`, `fire_ledger`, `train_glob` and `unheld_skip`. `sweep_template.md` declares none of them. That leaves the orchestrator two outcomes:
- If the overlay leaves the keys out, every gantt pass writes `gantt: UNREADABLE overlay lacks gantt_roster, gantt_acks` (`Ctx.need`), and the verdict audit runs without its ledger, train glob or skip file.
- If the overlay adds the keys, the sweep render is refused.

The owner ruling is to update the tracked templates and scripts, and this updates the script half without the template half.

Harness: `ev/keys.py` lists every overlay key `beat_jobs.py` reads (`ctx.need` and `overlay.get`/`[...]`) and subtracts `sweep_render.declared(sweep_template.md)`. The render probe in `ev/overlay-keys.txt` renders the head's template with only the declared keys, then adds one new key at a time. Metric: the number of undeclared beat keys. It is 0 at the merge base and 5 at the head (`ev/overlay-keys.txt`). Perturbation: add `gantt_roster`, `gantt_acks` or `fire_ledger` to the overlay. The control render with declared keys only prints `OK`. Each single addition prints `REFUSED: unknown: <key> not in the placeholder table`. The harness moves under its own perturbation.

Repair, in this PR: declare the five keys in the `## Placeholders` table and use them in (4b)/(4c). `sweep_render` refuses a declared but unused name, so the sweep text has to cite them. Add a check, in `beat_jobs_selftest.py` or `sweep_render`'s self-test, that every overlay key `beat_jobs.py` reads is a declared placeholder, so this cannot recur unseen.

## Findings

- Defect: `beat_jobs.py` reads five overlay keys (`gantt_roster`, `gantt_acks`, `fire_ledger`, `train_glob`, `unheld_skip`) that `sweep_template.md` does not declare, while `sweep_render.py` refuses an overlay that holds them. The new rows therefore cannot be fed and the sweep rendered from one overlay. The claim, harness, metric (0 at the base, 5 at the head) and perturbation are under `## Block`. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: four mutants on changed `gantt` lines survive `beat_jobs.py --self-test`, which prints 146 checks, 0 failed under each (`ev/mutants-mine.txt`, harness `ev/mut.py`):

  - M4 drops `rc != 0` from the roster `git show` guard.
  - M11 drops the `handoff-wip/*` refspec from the fetch.
  - M12 replaces the copied fire ledger with `""`.
  No case drives a `gh` failure, a roster `git show` failure, a `handoff-wip` tip or a gantt ledger line. M3 and M4 are partly masked, because an empty file then fails `sweep_gantt` and that prints `UNREADABLE sweep_gantt`. M4 is not masked when the fetch fails but an earlier `refs/gantt/roster` exists: the stale roster is read silently. That failed fetch's rc is also unchecked. Repair: one case per guard and input, each with a null. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: `## Red checks` misstates the red history. It says `61f1ec71` had "68 runs (`total_count` 68), all on one page. None concluded `failure`, `cancelled` or `timed_out`". That reading used the API default `filter=latest`. With `filter=all`, `61f1ec71` has 147 runs on 2 pages and 5 reds:
  - `gate` failure 128279140047, 128285014276 and 128290983518
  - `gate` cancelled 128288757875
  - `pr-contract / pr-contract` cancelled 128288387497

  At the head, `gate` failure 128312324401 is unnamed. Its log reads `FAIL run(s) [42340579795] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides`, the edit-run deferral R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER, and gate 128324519569 later concluded success. `arch-score / arch-score` cancelled 128324556485 and 128307712802 are also unnamed: both sit in edit run 42340579009, which was cancelled. Also unnamed are the `pr-contract` failure 128231570697 at `0ae78ac1`, which round 1's body named and this body dropped, and the 6 `gate`/`refresh`/`prelude` cancellations at `aa680f8b` (`ev/red-history-filter-all.txt`). The head's `pr-contract` 128321564289 started at 06:06:36Z, after the last red concluded at 05:22:16Z, and passed. So `defect-root-cause.md`'s trigger is answered by that run, and this is not the block. The brief requires the section to name every red that a later push cleared. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: `review_packet.py render` refuses `red-unanswered: concluded red check arch-score / arch-score is not named in ## Red checks`. The body's "This head's own runs ... Any red there is the next round's to answer" does not answer it, because this head is the head under review. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC

## Evidence

- RESULT: HEAD reviewed is `14a73c15e5f060069f0fd4831eb46a436bd14f1d` (ev/HEAD.txt). `git ls-remote` shows `fix/r10-sweep-template-sync` still at it when this verdict was written. The three-dot diff is ev/three-dot.diff: 13 files, +749/-20.

  - verdict_audit: 14 checks, 0 failed

  At the base, beat_jobs prints 124 checks, 0 failed. The count rises by the new cases and mutants. The body names the instrument rather than a count, which is consistent.
- RESULT: `selftest_wiring.py --check` prints `118 self-testing, 118 wired, 0 unwired; 0 index gap(s)` at the base and `120 self-testing, 120 wired, 0 unwired; 0 index gap(s)` at the head. That fits the two added self-testing files, `sweep_gantt.py` and `verdict_audit.py`.
- RESULT: CodeQL alert 51 (item 1): the site file `sweep_runner_selftest.py` is deleted in this re-cut, so the 0o700 mutation proof has no site at this head. `codeql / Analyze (python)` 128309715588 and `CodeQL` 128310823880 both conclude success at the head. No added helper sets a file mode. I re-derived that by reading the diff: `atomic()` and `mkdir` use default modes.
- RESULT: my mutants on the changed lines (ev/mutants-mine.txt):
  - Killed by behaviour cases: M5 (wrong `--fired` flag), M5b (verdict-audit flags dropped), M10 (`gantt` removed from ROWS), M13 (gantt UNREADABLE line dropped), M14 (empty page hashed as a move) and M15 (CASCADE line dropped).

R10-BUFFER-OPENLOOP (R10-COMBI-TANK PR 0, S; design `a605014bff4478f470853109060f4ff7ef605d4c` §C0, approved by `design-verdict/r10-combi-tank` `56810263b`). Carry 0 (owner ruling tvofi 11-06): without a buffer probe, `_update_current_state` never advanced `buffer_tank_temperature` (class D12-s1-01). It kept the 40 °C `ThermalState` default, or its last value, and every solve started the buffer from it. Refs #3225 (PR B closes it); this PR closes no issue.

What changes (`custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py`):
- **`_seed_store(reading, result, trajectory_attr, now) -> float | None`** is a module-level function beside `_open_loop_plan_value`. It returns the reading if ok, otherwise the previous plan's trajectory at the covering step, otherwise `None`. On `None` the caller leaves the field as it is, so nothing is fabricated. It is one primitive, and PR B reuses it for `combi_tank_seed`.
- **`_update_current_state`**: the DHW seed is re-expressed through `_seed_store` with identical behaviour; the R9 D12-s1-01 checks are its control. The buffer is seeded the same way from `buffer_temp_trajectory`. Both writes land on the private `state` copy before `ctx.publish(self, state)`, which is R10-LIVESTATE's I1/I2. R10-LIVESTATE is on main (`f7567be02`), so this PR is not blocked on it.
- **The observation split (`_update_external_heat_detection`)**:
  - The rise inputs `dhw_temp` and `buffer_temp` take the measured value or `None`. Without this, a planned rise would be read as external-heat evidence.
  - The level input `hp_tank_temp` keeps its text and reads the best estimate, which is the seed. This keeps wood energy and displacement on for a wood install with no buffer probe.
  - Following the verdict's `observation-read-in-place` note, the rise inputs are read with the `reader` that method already builds, the way `outlet` and `wood_top` are. No coordinator attribute is carried between methods.
- **Which buffers.** The seed applies to every buffer whose last plan published a trajectory. The plan publishes one only under a throttling valve (`optimizer.py`, the `buffer_temp_trajectory=` ternary on `mixing_valve.is_throttling`). Without one the level stays where it was. The harness's `solve` arm shows this with the real solver.
- **Observable side effect, publish-only.** On an install with no DHW probe, the external-heat attribute `dhw_rise_c_per_h` (binary sensor attributes, `ExternalHeatState.as_dict`) now reads `None` instead of a rate taken from the constant or the seed. Every reader is publish-only (`grep -rn "dhw_rise_c_per_h\|buffer_rise_c_per_h" custom_components`). The goldens already read `null`.

**Note for PR B. It is not carried, because it is not a measured finding: combi is not reachable yet, so nothing can be measured.** In combi one buffer probe fills both store fields, but the DHW rise input here reads only `CONF_DHW_TEMP_ENTITY`. PR B's `combi_tank_seed` will have to decide whether the combi DHW rise input reads the buffer probe, since it is the same water.

Group carries (roster `R10-COMBI-TANK`, read at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`), one disposition each:
- **Carry 1** (owner ruling 11-06, the no-probe buffer bug): **closed in this PR.** The unprobed buffer is seeded from the previous plan's `buffer_temp_trajectory` through the same seed helper the design adds, `_seed_store` over `_open_loop_plan_value`. PR B reuses that helper for `combi_tank_seed`. Its failing test and its controls are below.
- **Carry 2** (physically sound, general combi-tank types): not reached by PR 0. It adds no heat-transfer path, no tank type and no type branch. The seed is type-agnostic, because it reads whichever trajectory the plan published, so PR A and PR B build on it without a combi special case.
- **Carry 3** (judged on robustness, integration efficiency, architecture and maintainability): answered here as follows:
  - **Robustness.** No reading and no plan leaves the field as it is, never fabricated. The rise inputs are never fed a planned value.
  - **Integration efficiency.** It adds two `InputReader` reads in the same tick and no new coordinator attribute, following the verdict's `observation-read-in-place` note.
  - **Architecture.** One module-level primitive outside the coordinator class. `max_class_loc` and `class_excess_loc` each fall by 1.
  - **Maintainability.** The DHW and buffer seeds share one code path.
- **Carry 4** (web verification of the figures before PR B): binds PR B. PR 0 states no tank figure.
- **Carry 5** (the folded web-verification report): binds PR B, and PR A takes only item 1's UA. PR 0 touches no preset, UA, volume or help text.
- **Carry 6** (re-routed from R10-BUFFER-STORE carry 1, `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch127.md#P395`: seed the `dhw_temp_trajectory` tank seed from the measured tank temperature where one exists, failing test first): **already the behaviour, answered here, no code owed beyond the routing.** `_seed_store` reads an ok DHW probe first and falls to the plan's `dhw_temp_trajectory` only without one, so a measured tank temperature already wins wherever one exists. This PR moves the DHW seed onto that primitive with identical behaviour. Its control is `the open-loop DHW seed reaches the state but not the detector's rise input`, together with the R9 D12-s1-01 checks, and it is killed under the `GUARD_OFF` mutant of the DHW call listed under `## Unpinned sites`. ## Null control

- **Probe present.** A buffer probe reading 36.5 °C gives levels 36.5, 36.5 and a buffer rise input of 36.5 at both ends. The install has no DHW probe, so its DHW rise input moves from 55.0, the never-advanced default, to None. That move is the fix, not a drift. With the wood furnace and a 38 °C probe, `hp_tank_temp` reads 38.0 and wood energy is 29.0000 kWh, displacement 0.5312, identical at base and head.
- **Empty trajectory**, which is the no-valve plan. At both ends the level stays 40.0, 40.0. Wood energy is 26.6800 kWh, displacement 0.5000, identical at base and head. `None` is never invented.
- **`solve` with valve `none`.** The solver's buffer seeds read 40.0 ×4 at both ends, because the previous plan published no buffer trajectory.

## Figures

- `wood_seed seed`: `hp_tank_temp` base 40.0, 40.0 → head 41.0, 43.0. Wood energy 26.6800 → 23.2000 kWh, displacement 0.5000 → 0.4444. These equal the hand formula against 43 °C, and the test computes and compares them.
- `solve valve=manual`: solver buffer seeds base 40.0, 40.0, 40.0, 40.0 → head 40.0, 42.5, 40.9, 40.3. The first solve has no prior plan.

The census rule for the class (step 8): `git grep -n "_open_loop_plan_value(\|_seed_store(" -- custom_components` enumerates every open-loop seed site. Each returned seed site is dispositioned:

R10-HOTFIX-NIGHTLY-PIN-THROUGHPUT: where the 06 Nov nightly's 320 drain draws went, and three changes that raise pins per night.

The owner asked: measure from scheduled nightly run 42139479636's mutation-ledger shard logs where the drawn mutants go, then make the sound changes that raise pins per night. The measurement (`## Figures`) splits the 320 draws into: 90 killed, 44 lives, 1 timed out, 185 not started for `--budget-minutes`. Of the 90 kills, only 20 landed as pins. The other 70 had already been pushed by workflow_dispatch run 42135552492. That run started 33 minutes earlier on the same UTC date, so it drew the same slice under the same date seed 20261106.

Three changes, each tied to one line of that breakdown:

1. **The seed is the run id** (`nightly.yml` mutation-ledger, `--seed "${{ github.run_id }}"`). This is aimed at the 70 duplicate kills. Every run draws from the unpinned stock as it stood at its own checkout. So two runs on one date, a dispatch beside the schedule, drew one slice twice and the later push landed 22% of its kills (20 of 90). A run's four shards share one id, so they stay disjoint. The seed is printed in each `DRAIN SHARD` header, so a night's draw still replays. mutation-nightly keeps its date seed: it records nothing, so a duplicate draw there costs no pin.
2. **Admission charges no reach-free pair** (`drive_pool` and `drive_pin_pool` take `free`; `main()` passes `reach_free`). This is aimed at the 185 unstarted sites. Each mutant was admitted only if the sum of all its shared drivers fit before the deadline, and that sum included pairs `reach_skip` drops without a run. On the same draw those pairs are 37% of the shared pairs and 13% of the charge (`drain_admission_probe.py`). The charge now counts only runs that happen. `drive()` keeps its own check for lazy drivers, whose trace exists only after their deferred baseline.
3. **`--budget-minutes 270`**, the owner-allowed time raise, also aimed at the 185 unstarted sites. At 240 the four shards closed admission 16-80 minutes before the budget deadline, and the longest job ended 225 minutes into its 330-minute timeout. 270 is mutation-nightly's own sizing under the same timeout, leaving the same 60 minutes for runs in flight.

Alternatives considered, and why each lost:
- **More shards or `--jobs`.** The runners have 4 cores (`nproc` 4) and `--jobs 4` already uses them. More shards adds runner-hours without any measured share of the loss that it would recover.
- **Dropping or reordering a costly driver.** `tests/features.py` kills 130 of the 194 kills across both runs' logs, so dropping it loses coverage.
- **Optimistic admission** (charging less than a survivor's full sweep). It would re-open R9-F10.12's overrun and bias the measured prefix toward cheap mutants.
- **Draw de-duplication against existing pins.** It is already in place: `unpinned_sites` excludes every disposed site before `drain_pool`. What was missing was de-duplication between concurrent runs, which change 1 provides.
- **Survivor triage.** It stays manual, per `ci-autofix.md`; nothing here touches it.

The pins-per-night after-figure is owed on a workflow_dispatch nightly from `main` after this merges. The `mutation-ledger` jobs run only on `refs/heads/main` (`if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`), so no dispatch on this branch measures them. No seat instrument requests a nightly dispatch either (`tools/audit/seat/INSTRUMENTS.md` lists none). The before-figure is run 42139479636, plus dispatch 42135552492 as the run it collided with. The after run, owed by the seat that lands this PR (`gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref main`, nightly.yml's own recipe), reads the same way, with `nightly_drain_breakdown.py` over its four shard logs, `--prior` naming any run that pushed during it. A dispatch on the same date as a scheduled run no longer duplicates its draw.

3275.body:
R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-TIMEOUT. `governance / instrument-self-tests` ran its steps in line under `timeout-minutes: 30` and spent most of its wall time in five self-tests: prepr.sh's, beatd.py's, and pr_args.sh's alone and again through open_pr.sh and update_pr.sh, which each run it. Only prepr.sh's of the five keeps a core busy; the other four wait. They start detached in the job's first step, each to its own log and exit-status file. Five steps near the end of the job, under their old names, print each log, fail on its status and grep the same tally lines. The job lasts as long as the longer of its in-line steps and the detached work, instead of the sum of both. The timeout stays 30: no raise.

The three pr_args.sh callers run one after another in a single detached chain, and prepr.sh's self-test runs at `nice -n 10`. With all five at once, pr_args.sh's `mut:unlock` arm failed once in nine observations: it checks for a lock holder inside the 0.2 s poll the holder takes to notice that its parent has gone, and CPU contention shortens that window. Chained, they keep the order they had in line.

Alternatives, and why each lost:
- **Matrix shards** of the job would rename its check runs to `governance / instrument-self-tests (<shard>)`. That name is read in tools/pr/ci_predict.py's `JOB` table and by tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py's `bare()`, and each shard repeats checkout. Separate jobs fail tests/entities.py's census, which ties governance.yml job ids to governance_cost.py's `GOV`, until a file outside this group names them.
- **Dropping the standalone pr_args.sh step** would remove a step, and would leave pr_args.sh's tally to two callers outside this file.
- **Cutting prepr.sh's own cost** was not needed for the headroom: the detached run already takes it off the critical path.

Repair round 3 (review blocked a09ebaeb, mutation-vacuous, mutant W1). Deleting the waiter step `Show the pre-PR self-check refusing its own fixtures` survived every check: the launcher line still counted as wiring for selftest_wiring.py, and the harness read only the bg_* library. In CI, prepr.sh's self-test would have run detached with its exit status unread and the job green. The cure is the one the verdict names, in this group's own file:
- `bg_wait` writes a `<name>.read` marker when it reads a status.
- A new library function, `bg_unread`, lists every `<name>.pid` the launcher wrote with no `.read` beside it, prints `bg_unread: <started> started, <unread> unread`, and fails if any is unread.
- A new last step of the job, `Refuse a detached self-test whose status no step read`, runs `bg_unread` under `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`.

Deleting a waiter step, deleting its `bg_wait` line (the verdict's mutant A), or replacing a waiter with an echo of a fake tally (mutant D) now each leave a name unread, so the job itself goes red on main as well as at review. The harness gains the matching arms and mutants, and a shape check that the job's last step is that one.

## Head

`2ad71eb0e78f65a88f1f43bdcfb04e074e2ddf72` merges main `dee8b41` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`9c83f1ab03c674e6651a9afcca9c7e6acfdb8e93` merges main `53273de` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`763d98319f8a02bb0ef43eae1b22c0e7be7b77de` merges the authored code head `81ccb60da92ba016bd8f445ce43db368f2738d4c`.

Head 81ccb60da92ba016bd8f445ce43db368f2738d4c. It is the reviewed head a09ebaebd4f892729d96f24c7ec930ab6a12a37b, plus three commits:
- the cure commit 2a3a6998c1df6dd6692d7b54d956575c7c91624e;
- ec8c58a9446b68540d5fe2dc638f2461e5e8ce38, merging origin/main 1c1ae100b59e29564c7aec069b257dface6ef50f (fetched 2026-11-07 15:25:51 UTC). Main's commits there change nothing under tools/ or .github/ except tools/policy/agreement.mjs, which no figure below runs;
- 81ccb60da, merging origin/main 4b5d771bdf8feb1f83d7d9443e5117b771a0ab76 (fetched 2026-11-07 16:12:57 UTC), because main moved during the first prepr.sh run. That merge adds only dev/programme/delivery/3272.md and dev/programme/triage/s6-batch128.md.

Both merges were clean. The three-dot diff is unchanged by either: .github/workflows/governance.yml, dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py, dev/programme/delivery/3275.md and tests/closures.json. The harness, the replays, the gate and structure.py were taken at ec8c58a9. 81ccb60da differs from it only by those two record files, which none of them reads. prepr.sh and the body check were re-run at 81ccb60da.

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py` reads the bg_* library out of the launcher step as committed, drives it over planted commands, and checks the job's last step. At the head:
- M0, the library as committed: all 14 lines PASS. That is the 10 arms from earlier rounds, plus `refuse unread`, `names unread`, `control all read` and `shape last step reads bg_unread`. The three new arms start the job's five names, wait on four, refuse and name the fifth (`UNREAD prepr:`), then wait on it and pass.
- W2, the job's last step deleted: KILLED by `shape last step reads bg_unread`.
- M1, `bg_wait` returning 0 in place of the recorded status: KILLED by `refuse slow bad`, `refuse chained bad` and `refuse bad`.
- M2, `bg_wait` returning 0 for a launcher gone with no status: KILLED by `refuse chain killed` and `refuse killed`.
- X8, `bg_wait` returning 0 after its first poll finds the command still running: KILLED by `refuse slow bad` and `control all read`.
- M3, `bg_wait`'s read marker `: > "$d/$1.read"; ` deleted: KILLED by `control all read`.
- M4, `bg_unread`'s verdict `test "$u" -eq 0` replaced by `true`: KILLED by `refuse unread`.
- `RESULT survivors=0`, rc 0.

Failing first: the same harness run from a detached checkout of a09ebaeb (the workflow before the cure) prints `M0 FAIL names unread`, `M0 FAIL control all read`, `M0 FAIL shape last step reads bg_unread`, `M3 NOT APPLIED`, `M4 NOT APPLIED`, `RESULT survivors=2`, rc 1.

The W1 workflow is governance.yml with the prepr waiter step removed by a `yaml.safe_load`/`safe_dump` filter on its name. At the head the last step fails, printing `bg_unread: 5 started, 1 unread` and `UNREAD prepr: no step read its status`, then `RESULT replay_seconds=610 failed=1`.
