## Null control

- Each refusal arm has its passing control in the same run: `control ok`, `control tally`, `control chained tally`, `control slow ok` and, for the new arms, `control all read`. A library that refused everything would fail them.
- The unmutated head replay (`... replay .github/workflows/governance.yml bg`) passes every step, the new last step included: `RESULT replay_seconds=616 failed=0`. So `bg_unread` does not refuse a job whose five statuses were all read. Its refusal under W1 is the other end.
- Every job step still runs and greps its `checks, 0 failed` line. The five waiter steps keep their names, and their grep lines are byte-identical to the base's.
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/selftest_wiring.py --check` prints `118 self-testing, 118 wired, 0 unwired` and `0 index gap(s)`, rc 0.

Seams of the class, a detached self-test whose status nothing reads. The enumerating rule is the started names against the waited names in governance.yml:
- `{ grep -oE '^ +bg_start [a-z-]+ ' .github/workflows/governance.yml | awk '{print $2}'; grep -E '^ +bg_pid "\$!" [a-z]' .github/workflows/governance.yml | sed -E 's/^ +bg_pid "\$!" //' | tr ' ' '\n'; } | sort` gives `beatd open-pr pr-args prepr update-pr`.
- `grep -oE '^ +bg_wait [a-z-]+' .github/workflows/governance.yml | awk '{print $2}' | sort` gives the same five.

All five are closed in this diff: each is read by its waiter step, and `bg_unread` refuses any that is not. The rule's null control is W1, where the started set keeps `prepr` and the waited set loses it, and `bg_unread` names it. In CI, `bg_unread` is the same rule at run time, over the `.pid` files the launcher actually wrote.

## Figures

- Harness at the head: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py` gives 14 of 14 M0 PASS and `RESULT survivors=0` over W2, M1, M2, X8, M3 and M4, rc 0 (Mutation proof). The same file run from a09ebaeb gives `RESULT survivors=2`, rc 1. The harness sha1 at the head is `0196700d5c0e348f72671cc07f8ec82686103285` (`sha1sum`).
- Job replay, head: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py replay .github/workflows/governance.yml bg` gives `RESULT replay_seconds=616 failed=0`. Per step: prepr waiter 365.3 s, PR opener 0.0, PR argument builder 45.0, supervised beat 0.0, PR updater 205.1, the new last step 0.0. The total is the replay's own `replay_seconds` line. Earlier rounds' figures stand as cited there: a base replay of 1870 s, and CI at d6482b704 of 631 s of 1800 s.
- Job replay, W1: 610 s with `failed=1` at the head, and 605 s with `failed=0` at a09ebaeb (Mutation proof).
- CI at a09ebaeb, the reviewed head with the same five-step layout: code run 42380487764, `governance / instrument-self-tests` job 128427022752 ran 14:12:54Z to 14:23:30Z, which is 636 s of the 1800 s timeout. That is completedAt minus startedAt from the PR's check runs. The cure adds one step that reads files and sleeps nothing, timed at 0.0 s in both replays.
- `mut:unlock` chained, under the rule "each pr_args.sh caller's waiter passed its `pr_args self-test: [1-9][0-9]* checks, 0 failed` grep". 13 of 13 before this round, by the verdict's count. This round's three local replays (head, W1 at the head, W1 at a09ebaeb) each passed all three pr_args waiter steps, for 9 of 9. The total is 22 of 22, which bounds the failure rate only to below about 1 in 7 (95%, rule of three: 3/22). It is not a measured rate, and it is carried below.
- Scoped gate: `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) ./tests/run.sh` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run, 31 scoped out.` and `5 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED; 30 SCOPED OUT AND NOT RUN`, rc 0, with `ALL 2645 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` and `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`. `tests/closure.py select` names `tests/entities.py` and `tests/harness_headers.py`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- prepr: `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh` prints `PRE-PR: 81ccb60da92ba016bd8f445ce43db368f2738d4c ... rc=0` at the head. Its `ci predict` line reads `no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted against 4b5d771bdf8f`. origin/main had not moved past 4b5d771bd when it finished, so that run stands. The body passes `tools/pr/prepr.sh --body-check`, and `carry_audit.py check` reads 4 routed, 0 unrouted.

## Red checks

At the reviewed head a09ebaeb, the PR's check runs are 81, all on one page (`pull_request_read get_check_runs`, perPage 100, total_count 81). That tool takes no `filter` argument, so attempts were read per run with `actions_list list_workflow_jobs` and `filter: all`. Concluded reds:

## Block

- Mutant X8 inserts `return 0` after `bg_wait`'s `sleep 5`, so `bg_wait` returns 0 once its first poll finds the test still running. It survives every arm of `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py`. Every arm's command has either finished or been killed before its `bg_wait` runs (the arms `sleep 2` first), so the loop's still-running path is never exercised. The mutant is the same shape as the fixer's M1 and M2: a return replaced by 0, on a line this PR adds.
- The defect it admits is a false green. "Show the pre-PR self-check refusing its own fixtures" is `bg_wait prepr` alone, with no tally grep (prepr.sh prints none). Under X8 that step passes while prepr.sh's self-test is still running, or after it fails late. I added a slow arm (`bg_start slowbad bash -c 'sleep 8; echo partial; exit 5'`, then `bg_wait slowbad` with no grep, as the prepr step does):
  - committed library: `PASS refuse slow bad`, `PASS control slow ok`
  - X8: `FAIL refuse slow bad (prepr-shaped step passes)`, `PASS control slow ok`
  The other four waiter steps grep a tally, so a partial log fails them. The prepr step is the one this mutant reaches.
- The body itself says the job now lasts as long as the longer of the in-line steps and prepr.sh's self-test, so prepr can still be running when its waiter is read. In the head's CI run it had already finished (waiter at 0 s), which is why CI cannot show this.

Chaining restores the base's order, but at this head the chain still runs alongside the in-line steps and a niced prepr.sh. That is more load than the base had (all serial). Nine passes bound the residual rate only loosely, as the body says. The body dismisses it to a comment at the launcher step, which leaves no owner for a flake this PR's concurrency can still trigger on main, where a red cancels a merge-train slot. The re-cut owes either a measured rate under the head's real CI load (more than one CI run's observation) or a roster carry to the group owning tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh, for a deterministic `mut:unlock`. 3276.body:
R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER (reopened), topic r10-gate-busy-defer-2: an edit gate that defers to a sibling run at its head no longer publishes the deferral at once, and no two runs at a head wait on each other.

**Cause.** `prelude.judging()` read the units a run owes from its title's workset. A deferring edit run (C3, `prelude.defer_to`) never expands `pr-contract`: GitHub lists the caller under its bare name `pr-contract`, completed `skipped`, and never lists `pr-contract / pr-contract`. So judging() read every deferring run as busy, to every gate and prelude at its head, forever. #3246 dodged the resulting prelude/gate cycle with an at-once bound in `gate.judge` (the `deferring(...)` clause). That bound is #3263's red: edit run 42338396358 published `FAIL run(s) [42338396871] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides` 2 s into its judge step, beside code run 42338396871 still in progress.

**Fix.** `prelude.judging()` reads a unit whose caller job is listed completed under the unit's bare name as one the run never ran, so it adds no source. A deferring run is then judging once its gate is listed, and nothing waits on it. With the cycle gone, the at-once bound and `deferring()` are deleted, and a deferring edit gate waits on its sibling bounded by `GATE_WAIT_MAX_S`, like every other gate. The order is total:
- a code run's prelude waits on nothing;
- any other prelude waits only on an earlier run, or a code run, that is not judging;
- a gate waits only on runs that are not judging, past `busy()`'s id tie-break.

No judging run waits on a non-judging one, so no cycle closes. The tie-break stays, for a started gate whose listing lags a caller already resolved.

**#3261's pair is a different cause.** 42307493684 and 42307798573 were sweep re-runs at attempt 10. A re-run restores `tools/ci` from the original event's `pull_request.base.sha`, so both ran 28482ece's programs, which predate #3246 (each gate log: `programs restored from 28482eceeb6b9809e44b12d80fc994282cc21645`). The recorded replay reproduces both verdicts on 28482ece and reads PASS at origin/main and here. See Forward-carry for the re-run finding.

**Alternatives not taken.**
- (a) *An edit gate that exits non-failing (PASS) when it defers.* Unsafe. While code run 42338396871 ran, `commits/02e92e7c/check-runs?check_name=gate` listed only the edit run's `gate` check-run: a gate waiting on its `needs` has no check-run yet. A PASS would have read the head green with tests still running.
- (b) *"Only the lowest id decides."* Ids order nothing here: a same-second edit and code run are numbered out of order (sweep.py docstring).
- (c) *Keep the at-once red, add a second exemption.* That stacks a parallel rule on a misread; the misread is the cause.
- (d) *Raise the bound past a code run's span.* Needs `ci.yml`'s `timeout-minutes`, outside this group's files, and holds a runner throughout.

**Residual, stated plainly.** A code run longer than the bound still ends in the documented past-bound deferral red. #3263's code run was still in progress 20 min in, so the replay at this head waits 720 s and then publishes that red. gate-sweep.yml re-judges it once the code run's gate is green. The at-once red is gone for every sibling that finishes inside the bound. Whether to lengthen the bound (`ci.yml`'s gate `timeout-minutes`) is the orchestrator's call. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER

**Departure from the owned files.** `tools/ci/prelude.py` (`judging`, 4 lines and its docstring) is outside the roster's list (gate.py and the two harnesses). It is the one owner of "can this run still add a source": `gate.busy` and `prelude.wait_sources` both read it. A gate-side copy would be a parallel mechanism and would leave the prelude edge of the cycle open. The new fixture `tools/ci/fixtures/gate_busy_defer_runs.json` is the jobs API's record of both heads, fetched via `gh api` at 2026-11-07T04:4xZ, not re-typed.

## Head

`4de88a038e0e0923300cce8a09ec58e93a6ab1c4` merges main `be813ec` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`cecca4391dab34349fe10eb41a6ccfb2c4d3600e` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

cc100c27555e6936dd179293cd8897dae0a3b9ae, measured on a branch cut from origin/main 294a880dae608502b62055775e34a5db93217b98 (origin/main unmoved since the prepr run, read 2026-11-07T04:52Z: no merge and no second run owed).

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_ci_gate_core.py mutants` at the head: `RESULT mutants=21 survivors=0`. The two new mutants:

- **M25** deletes the fix's line in `judging` (`if jobs.get(u, ("",))[0] == "completed": continue` → `pass`). KILLED (self-test rc 1). Red:
  - `busy-defer-2: listed as GitHub lists it (`pr-contract` skipped), neither started gate waits on the other`
  - `busy-defer-2: the higher deferring edit gate beside the lower one listed as GitHub lists it judges at once`
  - `prelude/gate order: beside an earlier started deferring gate and a later edit run in its prelude, it waits on the later run only, then judges`
  - `the cycle's other edge: a deferring run at its gate is judging (its bare `pr-contract` caller skipped), so no prelude or gate waits on it`
  - `#3263: the code run's gate never waits on that deferring edit run (the edge that closed the cycle)`
- **M26** restores the at-once FAIL (`bound = 0` for a deferring workset's deferral). KILLED (self-test rc 1). Red:
  - `C3 (r10-gate-busy-defer-2): a deferring edit gate beside a busy code run waits on it, then judges its sources, no red`
  - `busy-defer: the higher deferring edit gate waits on the lower whose listing lags, then judges, never a red deferral`
  - `prelude/gate order: a deferring gate beside a later edit run still in its prelude waits on it (that run's prelude no longer waits on this one), then judges`
  - `prelude/gate order: a deferring gate beside a later edit run in its prelude, gate listed `waiting` (R3-2) waits on it (that run's prelude no longer waits on this one), then judges`
  - `prelude/gate order: beside an earlier started deferring gate and a later edit run in its prelude, it waits on the later run only, then judges`
  - `#3263 (42338396358 beside code run 42338396871): the deferring edit gate never publishes the deferral before its bound`

M20, M21, M22 and M24 pinned the deleted `deferring(...)` clause; they are removed with it, because their patterns no longer exist.

**Failing test first.** The head's self-test was run over origin/main's production code (`prelude.py`, and `gate.py` above `self_test`). Result: `gate self-test: 74 checks, 9 failed`, the #3263 replay among them (`got (False, True)`: the deferral published with no wait). Over 28482ece's production code: `74 checks, 14 failed`, both #3261 replays among them (each got the pair's deferral, as CI logged).

## Null control

Each of these is in the self-test:
- A lone code run with no sibling still gates normally: `null: no other run at the head, no wait`, `("PASS", [])`.
- A finished sibling still decides: `C3: the deferred gate re-judged once the code run ended (green|its pr-contract red) is that run's verdict` reads PASS, and `FAIL pr-contract / pr-contract: failure (run 99)`.
- A real red is never masked: `a deferring gate published after the decider's red is that red, never a PASS`.
- The bound still holds: `past the bound, the deferral FAILs (for gate-sweep.yml), and the wait stays inside the bound`.
- The fix's own null: `... null: a caller still running (not completed) still owes its unit` reads `judging` False.
- At the harness level, `single` reads `UNDECIDED-RED 0 ... gate-wait 0 s`.

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/ci/gate.py --self-test`: `gate self-test: 74 checks, 0 failed`. `python3 -I tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test`: `62 checks, 0 failed`.
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_race.py --ci "$X/tools/ci" fixture`, with `$X` a `git archive <sha> tools/ci tools/pr` export:
  - at 28482ece: all three recorded gates read as CI logged them, the deferral after 0 s;
  - at 294a880d (origin/main): 42338396358 the deferral after 0 s, the #3261 pair `PASS`;
  - at the head (no `--ci`): 42338396358 the deferral after 720 s (the bound; its code run never finishes in the record), the #3261 pair `PASS` after 0 s.
  - Null for the replay itself: at 28482ece it reproduces CI's three logged verdicts verbatim.
- The same harness, `prelude` scenario: `UNDECIDED-RED 1` at 28482ece and at 294a880d; `UNDECIDED-RED 0 ... DEADLOCK no CYCLE 0` at the head. Every scenario at the head reads `UNDECIDED-RED 0`, `MASKED 0`, `DEADLOCK no` and `RESIDUAL-RED 0`.
- The class's seams (fixer step 8). The rule: every non-self-test reader of a title's workset, `grep -n "workset(" tools/ci/prelude.py tools/ci/gate.py tools/ci/sweep.py tools/ci/sweep_selftest.py`, with hits inside `def self_test` excluded. It returns 4 seams:
  - `prelude.py` `workset` (the definition);
  - `prelude.judging` (closed in this diff);
  - `prelude.outputs` (the producer: it writes the run's own workset, which `defer_to` narrows; it reads no other run);
  - `gate.gate`'s source loop (already guarded: `a unit that run deferred (C3) judged nothing: no source`, the all-skipped `continue`, with self-test `C3: a unit a run deferred is no source even under its full job name (skipped)`).
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: `MODE: FULL` (a `tools/ci/` gate file: nothing scoped to reproduce locally).
- `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh`: `PRE-PR: cc100c27555e ... rc=0` (every step ok or a named skip; `ci predict`: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted)

## Red checks

none predicted. A red at the PR is CI's, past the handoff.

## Forward-carry

- **A gate re-run executes the programs of its event's original base, not of main.** `ci.yml`'s gate step restores `tools/ci/*.py` from `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`, and a re-run (gate-sweep.yml's included) replays that event. So a PR whose last event predates a gate fix keeps running the old gate on every sweep re-run. #3261's pair at attempt 10 ran 28482ece, before #3246. That changes how the orchestrator reads a red re-run gate after a gate fix merges: re-judge such a PR only after a fresh event (a push, an edit, a review), or read the `programs restored from` line first. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is outside this group. This fixer writes no roster or brief, so it routes the finding to this group for the orchestrator to place (its gate-fix merge step in `dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md` is the proposed home). Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER

R10-RCA-LIVEHEAD-CANCEL, the root-cause seat. The two whole-run cancels at live heads on #3241 (run 42332985078, attempt 1) and #3232 (run 42329221705, attempt 2) were not `concurrency:` cancels, runner loss or `cancel_superseded.py`. GitHub annotates every cancelled job `The run was canceled by @tvofi.`: a cancel POSTed under the owner's credential, from outside every in-tree canceller, and followed by a rerun under the same credential. The class is routine: 155 such cancels at live heads in 76 h.

This PR lands:
- `dev/audit/rca/r10-livehead-cancel.md`: cause, process state (a), class reach, cost test, countermeasure and refusals;
- `dev/audit/harnesses/livehead_cancels.py`: the detector, which attributes every cancelled `ci.yml` attempt to its canceller and tests it against the live head;
- the class `N-livehead-operator-cancel` and the `_rca` record `R10-RCA-LIVEHEAD-CANCEL` in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`;
- the class id registered in `finding.schema.json`'s `class_guess` enum, and in `.claude/workflows/audit-find.js`'s `CLASS_GUESS` and `FINDING_REPORT`, the readers the `agreement` lane pairs with the ledger;
- one `inert_reads` line in `tests/closures.json`, written by `ci_predict.py --apply-inert`.

The process that sent the cancels cannot be named from GitHub data. The orchestrator's seat transcripts can name it (RCA section 6).

## Head

`ee9f5ced95f2b84095c7103ffd23e58e03bc9805` merges main `08fd676` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`2a8b8f0ccdf5ce4f3ed2f8101e201de7caf7354a` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

The merge brought in no change to `ci.yml`, `cancel_superseded.py` or the harness inputs, which are GitHub API reads over a closed window ending 2026-11-07T04:00:00Z. The figures do not depend on main's tip.

## Mutation proof

Two mutants of `dev/audit/harnesses/livehead_cancels.py`, each restored afterwards (`git status` clean):
- `in_class` without `and BOT not in row["by"]`: `--selftest` prints `selftest: FAILED`, and over the cache `NULLCONTROL-BOT class=204` (unmutated: 0).
- `classify`'s live test replaced by `True`: `--selftest` prints `selftest: FAILED` (`'2/1': ('@github-actions[bot]', True)`), and `CLASS live-head external cancels: 184` (unmutated: 155).

## Null control

## Figures

- `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/check-runs/<job>/annotations`: `The run was canceled by @tvofi.` on jobs 128283882523 and 128284504740 (run 42332985078/1), and on 128288382623, 128288382597 and 128288382585 (run 42329221705/2).

## Round

## Findings

- Surviving mutant in the detector's selftest. The mutant: in `canceller()`, the `higher priority waiting request` branch is disabled and `"@concurrency"` is returned in its place, so a `concurrency:` cancel is attributed to an operator login. `--selftest` still prints `ok`, and over the cache the CLASS line stays 155, because the selftest has no concurrency-annotated attempt and the 76 h window holds no concurrency cancel at all (there is no `by=concurrency` row). The unmutated code does attribute correctly: perturbation P-concurrency, which rewrites every `@tvofi` annotation to the concurrency line, prints `CLASS ... 0` (ev/perturb.txt). But nothing in the tree pins it. A regression would go unseen as soon as a concurrency group becomes able to cancel a `ci.yml` run, and that is exactly when the reading after a countermeasure would be taken. Claim: the concurrency branch is unpinned. Evidence: ev/mutants.txt, mutant 4. Harness: `livehead_cancels.py --selftest`. Metric: selftest result and CLASS count. Perturbation: the mutant itself, under which both stay flat. Owed: one synthetic `Canceling since a higher priority waiting request` attempt in `selftest()`, expected `by=concurrency` and out of class. That is a precondition for reading the CLASS line after the bounded pause lands. Carry: R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE
- `NULLCONTROL-HEAD` and `NULLCONTROL-BOT` force the classified rows (`dict(r, live=False)` and `dict(r, by="@github-actions[bot]")`) after `classify()` and `canceller()` have already run. So they pin only the two terms of `in_class`, and never the attribution or the live-head computation. Under every one of the five mutants (ev/mutants.txt), including `live: True` (CLASS 184) and `head_at` without its time bound (CLASS 23), `NULLCONTROL-HEAD` printed `live=0 class=0`. The body's "So the class count is not something the classifier produces whatever its input" (RCA section 4) therefore overstates what these lines show. The property itself holds under perturbations of the inputs, which I ran on copies of the cache: P-concurrency, P-bot and P-superseded (a newer-head run injected 1 s before each cancel) each print `CLASS ... 0` (ev/perturb.txt). So the class count stands, and the in-tree control is weaker than described. Owed: replace the two forced-row lines with perturbations of the inputs (rewrite the annotation, inject a newer head) inside the harness, so that every reading carries them. Carry: R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE

## Evidence

- RESULT judge(1) root-cause record: named cause (a whole-run cancel POSTed under the `tvofi` credential, outside every in-tree canceller), process state (a), cost test with numbers (155 cancels, 2864.7 runner-min, restart median 906 s), countermeasure (detector, 0 s standing cost), refusals of candidates 1-4, and the parts missing (the sending process) all present in dev/audit/rca/r10-livehead-cancel.md and in the `_rca` record.

All five cited jobs (128283882523, 128284504740, 128288382623, 128288382597, 128288382585) are annotated `The run was canceled by @tvofi.`
- RESULT detector at the head, my own fetch at 06:06-06:26Z (ev/harness-head.txt): `CLASS live-head external cancels: 155, minutes lost 2864.7`; CANCELLED rows identical to the body's (182/154/29/32/1/1/1/17/2); FOLLOW restarted 81 (1861.2), duplicate 5 (153.0), dropped 69 (850.5); restart gap min 22, median 906, max 7496, 18 within 120 s; NULLCONTROL lines 0. Both brief events are in `--list`. The brief hour (`--since 2026-11-07T02:30:00Z`) gives 7 class cancels at 02:38, 02:54, 03:16, 03:25, 03:35, 03:41 and 03:49, as the body states. `record/autofix` has 40 of the 155.
- RESULT completeness: `total_count` 1217, and the cache holds 1217 distinct runs. Figure not re-derivable: the body's "1960 attempts". My fetch holds 1975, because reruns after the fixer's fetch added attempts to runs created in the window (1929 of them updated by 04:00Z). The class figures filter on cancel time, so they do not depend on this number.
- RESULT judge(2) perturbations of the inputs (ev/perturb.txt): unperturbed 155; every `@tvofi` annotation rewritten to the concurrency line → 0 (154 `by=concurrency` live); rewritten to the `@github-actions[bot]` line → 0; a newer-head run injected 1 s before every cancel → 0. The harness moves under each perturbation, so the finding is not void.
- RESULT mutation proof (ev/mutants.txt): `in_class` without the BOT term → selftest FAILED, NULLCONTROL-BOT 204; `live: True` → FAILED, CLASS 184; `canceller` never reads the `@login` line → FAILED, CLASS 0; `head_at` without `created_at <= t` → FAILED, CLASS 23; concurrency branch read as a login → survives (Findings). 3278.body:
R10-RCA-GATE-BUSY-DEFER-2, the root-cause seat for R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER (topic r10-gate-busy-defer-2). It ran beside that fixer and did not edit `tools/ci/`. Part of #201. The analysis is `dev/audit/rca/r10-gate-busy-defer-2.md`, indexed in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` as `_rca.R10-RCA-GATE-BUSY-DEFER-2`.

## Re-cut note

Repair round 2, after a blocked verdict (`rca-claim-false`): the first record called #3263's edit/code-run red "designed, not the race", and main's #3276 (`812bb8747`) had fixed it as a defect. This body is re-taken whole at the head below.

- **Stale pin (unchanged finding).** ci.yml restores `tools/ci/*.py` from the payload's `pull_request.base.sha`, and a job re-run replays that payload. So each re-run of a run created before #3246 merged (`355d9965`) ran the pre-fix `gate.py`. The six mutual-deferral gates (#3261, #3265, #3255 pairs, pinned `28482ece`, `f2a01514`, `80016a71`) all ran such a copy. Process state (c).
- **#3263 (corrected).** Run 42338396358's 2-second red is the edit/code-run deferral, a second defect with its own cause. `prelude.judging()` read a deferring edit run's skipped `pr-contract` caller (listed completed under its bare name) as owed, so that run looked busy to every gate at its head, and gate.py's at-once bound dodged the wait cycle that made. #3276 fixed `judging()` and deleted the bound. RCA section 1 gives the cause, section 3 the process state (c: the self-test and #3246's `prelude` scene pinned the at-once red as the specification, not the property "a deferring run is judging") and the cost; the countermeasure is landed by #3276 and scored here.
- **Instrument.** The replay arm's exit code ignored the single-gate class, so it read rc 0 for the at-once red at `294a880d`. `DEFECTS` now counts `C3-AT-ONCE`; a single gate that waited and then deferred is `DEFERRED`, the bounded wait, not a defect. The arm's remaining blindness (the wait cycle itself) is stated in its docstring and RCA section 1.
- **Countermeasure, proposed and not built.** A re-run of a gate whose pinned programs differ from the base tip becomes a ci.yml dispatch (`tools/ci`, the gate fixer's and the orchestrator's).

## Head

`71710c566283e302de7db598c8a6fc3045a41dbf` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`b38e5c08bddba4817e362c450e7369ddd1b819ae`, branch `fix/r10-rca-gate-busy-defer-2`: the reviewed head `d5c4a06b` plus origin/main (merged by the bot as `510b2a108`; origin/main `b4ec2f332` is an ancestor) plus one repair commit. origin/main was `b4ec2f332` at 2026-11-07 15:07Z, at the final `tools/pr/prepr.sh` run, so no further merge was owed. The three-dot diff adds the harness and its fixture, the RCA document, the `_rca` entry, the harness's `tests/closures.json` INERT READS entry and the delivery row.

## Mutation proof

This PR adds no production line. The detector it adds is the `replay` arm, proven against real program copies (`git archive <sha> tools/ci tools/pr`) and two mutants:

- Red on the defect: `replay --ci` at `28482ece`, `f2a01514` and `80016a71` gives rc 1, `DEADLOCK` on the three pairs. At `294a880d` it gives rc 1, `C3-AT-ONCE` on the three edit/code-run scenes.
- Green on the fixes: rc 0 at `812bb8747` and at this head's `tools/ci`, the pairs `DECIDED` (naps 0 and 0 in #3261) and the C3 scenes `DEFERRED` with naps 12.
- Scoring mutant: a copy of the harness with `DEFECTS = ("DEADLOCK", "HALF-DEFERRED")` gives rc 0 at `294a880d`; the unmutated copy, relocated the same way, gives rc 1.
- M17 (busy()'s later-started-gate tie-break deleted) on this head's `gate.py` **survives** the arm, rc 0: under #3276's `judging()` the pair no longer reads each other busy. `gate.py --self-test`'s M17 row pins it; the arm does not replace the self-test. M24 named code #3276 deleted and is not run.

## Null control

- Pre-#3246 programs give rc 1 and #3246's gives rc 0 on the same listings; the fixed program decides the pairs the stale program deadlocks.
- At `294a880d` the C3 scenes read `C3-AT-ONCE` with naps 0, at `812bb8747` and this head `DEFERRED` with naps 12, so the class separates the at-once publication from the bounded wait (`GATE_WAIT_MAX_S` 720 s at `POLL_S` 60 s, the recorded code run still unfinished at 29 minutes).
- The arm refuses, and does not go green, on a fixture whose pair gates did not overlap in time or whose gate never started.
- The compare the countermeasure would run, `git diff --quiet 28482ece 294a880d -- <restored paths>`, gives rc 1; the same sha on both sides gives rc 0.

## Figures

- Replay at each program: `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.py replay --ci <export>/tools/ci`, with `<export>` from `git archive <sha> tools/ci tools/pr`. rc 1 at `28482ece`, `f2a01514`, `80016a71` and `294a880d`; rc 0 at `812bb8747`; `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.py replay` at this head prints `RESULT replay ... defects=no`.
- Pins of the 9 recorded gates: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.py pins` prints `RESULT pins gates=9 stale=6`.
- Fixture: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.json`, sha1 f926d6a67b5582c172f49cb436a09e7ff7b63b70 (`sha1sum`), unchanged by this repair.
- Census (the first handoff's figures, from `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.py census --since 2026-11-07T03:45:14Z --until 2026-11-07T04:50:21Z`). **Re-derived in this repair** at 2026-11-07 after the review's run failed on proxy resets; the same command printed the same three rows: stale `gates=46 {'defer': 21, 'other-red': 1, 'pass': 24}`, 7 PRs, `reruns=36`; fixed `gates=3 {'defer': 3}`, all the at-once edit/code-run red, now #3276-class; unpinned `gates=5`.
- Recurrence, rule pinned at a time: `git log --first-parent --format=%h --since=2026-10-23T00:00:00Z origin/main -- 'tools/ci/*.py' tools/pr/codeql_scope.py tests/closure.py tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py | wc -l` gives 30 at origin/main `b4ec2f332` (15 with `--since=2026-10-31T00:00:00Z`). The same rule over `tools/ci/gate.py tools/ci/prelude.py` since `2026-10-31T00:00:00Z` lists 4 merges (#3276, #3246, #3230, #3205). The count moves with each merge to those paths; the rule is the record.
- Ledger: `python3 tools/audit/fold_ledger.py check` prints `0 violation(s)`, 137 rca entries.
- Scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`, the script `tests/entities.py`. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` prints `ALL 2645 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`; `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- Seam enumeration (fixer step 8). Rule: the `git checkout "$PINNED" --` lines in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, each naming programs a run restores from its payload base. Each returned seam (prelude/gate: `tools/ci/*.py`, `tools/pr/codeql_scope.py`, `tests/closure.py`; cancel-superseded: `tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py`; refresh: `tools/ci/*.py`) is in the class, open, dispositioned in RCA section 3 and covered by the proposed countermeasure 5.2.
- Instrument blindness: the single-gate scenes judge one gate beside a code run listed as recorded, so the replay scores the at-once publication and not the wait cycle `judging()` made; #3276's fixture self-test in `gate.py` pins the cycle (RCA section 1).

## Red checks

Read with `pull_request_read get_check_runs` on PR 3278 at 15:07Z, all 86 check runs in one page, at head `510b2a108` (the bot merge this repair builds on). The repair commit `b38e5c08` had no check runs at the time of writing.

- `tests / nightly-status` failure (run 42383179334, job 128435471085): not this PR's; its diff does not reach what nightly-status reads, and it was red on the previous head too. Answer: the cheaper detector is the nightly job itself, standing cost nil here (`fix-review.md` 11).
- `gate` cancelled (run 42383179334, job 128439401244, with `tests / coverage`, `tests / closures`, `tests / fast (3.14)`, `governance / instrument-self-tests` and the other cancelled lanes): the run was superseded at 15:05:24Z by run 42383590829, whose `gate` job 128439014625 is in progress. Cleared by the newer run, class: superseded run, not a failure of this diff. The earlier head `d5c4a06b` had the edit-gate deferral `gate` red (job 128409314146, run 42374407743, "FAIL run(s) [42372899314, 42373060299] ... still being judged"), cleared when the code runs classified GREEN at 13:25:08Z, and the same `tests / nightly-status` red (job 128405124320, run 42372899314).
- No open `code-scanning alert` at the read.

## Forward-carry

- Carry 1, to the R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER fixer (topic r10-gate-busy-defer-2): #3263's red was not designed; #3276 fixed it and RCA section 1 records the cause, process state and cost. `replay --ci <export>` now fails on `C3-AT-ONCE` (dev/audit/rca/r10-gate-busy-defer-2.md, Carries). Carry: #201
- Carry 2, to the orchestrator: the stale-pin re-run countermeasure in `refresh()` and `sweep.py` (RCA 5.2) is a `tools/ci` change for the gate's owner. Until it lands, after any pinned-program merge, dispatch ci.yml (`pr=N base=main`) for each PR whose latest gate is a stale-pinned red (RCA 5.3). Carry: #201

## Friction

- PROMPT.md: contradiction: the payload pins git identity `seat` and the brief says `hpo-fixer` and never `seat`; `hpo-fixer` was used, set in the environment because the exported toolchain sets the author variables to `seat`. Carry: dismissed: identity settled per brief, as on #3246
- frugal-routing-hook: cost: an inline-search budget of 5 per prompt blocked plain reads of files this seat was editing, forcing delegations. Carry: dismissed: seat-harness configuration, outside this repository

3280.body:
stamp.py `record_flush` waited for a record merge while a live `refs/heads/train-hold` made every beat it dispatched exit `skip-train-hold`. Its three dispatches were spent under the hold, and the timeout named no hold. It now reads the hold itself and spends no dispatch under one. A second change, in `merge_train.py`, keeps the hold DELETE from being skipped by a second TERM or HUP during the unwind, and (repair round 2) delivers a first stop that lands in a batch's closing release instead of discarding it.

Repair round 2 (verdict/3280, blocked d65bcee9bdfb): `Train.batch` calls `unwind()` in the `finally` of every batch, and the round-1 `stop_ignored` set `SIG_IGN`, which discards a signal. A first TERM in batch k's release was lost and batch k+1 merged. `stop_ignored` now records the signal in a handler that does not raise, restores the handlers, and delivers the first recorded signal through the restored handler after the hold DELETE. Entered with a stop already unwinding (a `SystemExit` in flight), further signals are dropped, as the brief requires. The duplicate `import contextlib` is removed.

Alternatives: masking with `signal.pthread_sigmask` was not taken (it leaves the signal pending to the kernel, with no hook to say when the stop is already unwinding). No `train.sh` trap change. One `Train.unwind` method serves `train` and `batch`. The hold is an injected collaborator `held`, defaulting to `train_hold` (zero REST), the bound read from `nightly.yml`'s `HOLD_MAX_AGE_S=`, never a second literal. A hold never refuses the flush; an unreadable hold or bound reads as no hold.

`record_flush` gives a dispatch back (`count - 1`) whenever a hold appears after one, even if that beat had already run. A hold that flaps can therefore re-dispatch more than `FLUSH_MAX_DISPATCHES` beats in total; the 7200 s deadline bounds it, which is accepted.

Shared file: `tools/release/stamp.py` is also changed by the hotfix R10-FLY-STAMP-FLUSH-COST (topic r10-fly-stamp-flush-cost). This round changes no line of stamp.py; its stamp.py change is round 1's `record_flush`/hold reading. Whichever lands second merges `origin/main` and reruns `stamp.py --self-test`; no ordering is required by this PR.

Closes: triage batch 131 P402 (`dev/programme/triage/s6-batch131.md`, which exists only at triage ref `cd88cf6bd00d`, not at origin/main or this head).

## Head

`1f2fb65262eaeab2cd970c54403c51d513a9a72b` merges main `4b5d771` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`720220f19e40aeacf59fac0b8c9ca58221275c97` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

60b97bb5d872e151563f2e7c0307605f2fb11804, on origin/main a37c58e5f (merged in; `prepr.sh` rc=0 at this head, 2026-11-07T14:20Z).

## Mutation proof

Mutants are the source with one marked line replaced, run for real by the self-test driver:

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked d65bcee9bdfb2cc11302d1c96d4bf00659ec24db class-open: Train.batch runs unwind after every batch, so a first TERM or HUP landing in a between-batch release is discarded by SIG_IGN and the train goes on to merge the next batch

bus-nonce: 206cf0ae7035dcafbdd6b18a4ab76231

## Block

Round 1. `stop_ignored` sets `SIG_IGN` for TERM and HUP, which **discards** a signal and does not defer it. `Train.unwind` is documented as running "once a stop is already unwinding it", and in `train()` that holds. `Train.batch` (merge_train.py:3205-3208 at the head) is different: it calls `self.unwind()` in the `finally` of **every** batch, including one that completed normally. A first, and only, operator TERM or HUP that lands while batch k releases its worktrees and hold is therefore thrown away. The loop then goes on to `queue_take` and `_batch(k+1)`, and that batch merges.

I measured this with my own probe, not the finder's or the fixer's. It is `ev/probe/batch_swallow.py` and `ev/probe/run.sh`: two batches, stubbed `run` with a 2 s `git worktree remove`, and one TERM sent 0.3 s into batch 1's unwind.
- At the head (`ev/probe-batch-swallow-head.txt`): `BATCH T` … DELETE, then **`BATCH T-b2`** … DELETE, then `RETURNED rc=0`. The stop was lost and the second batch ran.
- Null control, with the base's unwind and the same driver (`ev/probe-batch-swallow-null.txt`): `SYSTEMEXIT 143` after batch 1, so the stop is honoured. That run shows the original hold-DELETE skip, which is the bug the PR fixes.

The fix trades the hold-ref leak for a lost stop request on the path that merges pull requests. That is the worse failure. The brief asked for the unwind to ignore further signals "once it starts", meaning once a stop is unwinding, and not on every batch boundary. The self-test `_unwind_self_test` drives only `train()`, so this seam is untested.

The cure is the fixer's to choose. One sound shape: keep the signal but defer it. Inside the block, record the signal number in a handler that does not raise, or mask it with `signal.pthread_sigmask(SIG_BLOCK, …)`. Re-raise or unmask it after the hold DELETE, so a pending stop is delivered then. Add a batch-path arm: one TERM during batch 1's unwind, assert there is no `BATCH T-b2` and a non-zero exit, with this probe's mutant as the control.

A hold that flaps can therefore re-dispatch more than `FLUSH_MAX_DISPATCHES` beats in total within the 7200 s deadline. The deadline bounds it, so I judge this acceptable, but the body should say so. R10-RCA-FLUSH-DISPATCH: the root-cause seat for the owner's ruling of 2026-11-07. The stamp's record flush dispatches all of Nightly to run the one-minute `record-autofix` job. This seat ran beside R10-FLY-STAMP-FLUSH-COST and never inside it, so this diff does not touch `tools/release/stamp.py` or `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`.

What lands:

- the class id registered where the agreement lane reads it: `dev/audit/config/finding.schema.json` and `.claude/workflows/audit-find.js`.

The four results:
- **Cause.** The flush rule took a job as the unit of dispatch, and the API dispatches a workflow.
  - Triage P88 (`dev/programme/triage/s6-batch19.md`) and the R10-FLOW-RECORD-PITCH carry both say "dispatches `record-autofix`".
  - `record-autofix` had lived in `nightly.yml`, beside every heavy lane gated on `github.event_name != 'push'`, since `abf4f40b7` (2026-10-21).
  - `6b1aa629f` (#2836) implemented the carry. It recorded the every-lane fact only as a code comment on `FLUSH_MAX_DISPATCHES`.
- **Process state: (c).** The triage cost gate (`proposal-triage.md`, whose cost list names "CI runners") was obeyed: P88 has a `Cost:` line. But it priced the stamp step under the job unit.
  - The flush self-tests and mutants drive a `dispatch=` double and never read what the dispatch starts.
  - The fix review of #2836 was asked about no runner cost.

R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER, third PR (topic r10-gate-busy-defer-3). A deferring gate no longer holds a runner. `gate.judge()` publishes the deferral at once. `gate-sweep.yml` (`tools/ci/sweep.py`) re-runs that gate without a human once the deciding run completes. The existing green, newest-covering branch handles most heads. A new `settle` branch handles a head that no green gate follows: two gates that deferred to each other, or a decider that ended red or cancelled.

**What the runs say about the brief's cause.** The brief says nothing re-judges the deferring gate when the deciding run concludes. Today's runs do not support that as stated. On #3282 the sweep did fire for code run 42367457479. That run concluded at 11:48:41Z, and tvofi re-ran edit gate 42367457809 at 11:48:45Z. The sweep's read at 11:48:53Z then found that gate already re-queued and left it (`SWEEP-DONE run=42367457479 reruns=0`). The replay below shows that, without the human re-run, main's sweep re-runs the gate and it passes. The defects the runs do show are the following:
1. **The wait held a runner and ended red anyway.** Since #3276 merged (08:36:40Z), every deferral FAIL held its runner for the full ~12 min before publishing (`held_ge_600` = `deferral_fails` in the census below).
2. **The sweep's SKIP branch had no exit when nothing green follows.** This is a mutual deferral, or a decider that ended red or cancelled. These reds stayed until a human acted. Examples: #3265's pair at 04:06–04:08Z, and #3255's pair, both re-run attempts. The RCA of #3278 shows those ran pre-fix programs. `settle` covers the shape for whichever program the gate runs.

**The fix and the alternatives considered.**
- **Keep the wait and fix only the sweep.** This would leave a runner held ~12 min per deferral, which the brief forbids. It also feeds the runner queue that delayed the sweep's own re-runs by 7–26 min today, for example sweep 42353870719, created 08:04:01Z and run at 08:18:20Z.
- **Mark a deferral with a `ci.yml` step, or with an annotation the sweep reads.** `tests/entities.py` pins the gate job's last step (rev3 R3-1) and the sweep job's permissions (`checks: read` is absent). Either would change a pin.
- **Have the sweep read gate logs.** That needs a raw-body mode in `ghapi`.

`settle` instead decides from data the sweep already reads, the `filter=latest` jobs listing. A red gate is re-run when it started before another run's job (its gate aside) finished, or when a higher-id run's gate started while it judged. In the second case only the lower id is re-run, because `busy()`'s tie-break makes the lower id the one that decides. The third case is that same pair seen from its higher side: a red gate whose lower-id peer's gate judged beside it and ended green deferred to that decider, so the higher is re-run. A red lower is re-run by the second arm and the higher is not, so the pair is never both re-run. A re-run judges after every source finished and after the peer gate concluded, so it is never re-run again, and the branch cannot loop. The new harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_busy_defer_3.py` (record, replay, census) lands with the fixture rows for #3282.

**Round 2 repair (verdict/3287 at 29ee7261, `settle-unjudged`).** At 520538cc, a higher-id gate that deferred by `busy()`'s tie-break to a lower run whose listing lagged stayed red whenever the lower's green gate did not cover the newest event, that is, the higher run was created after the lower's gate started. The sweep then took `settle`, where `undecided()` re-ran only the lower id of an overlapping pair, and the lower was green. At the base that gate waited one poll and passed, so the change introduced this. The repair is one arm of `undecided()` (`tools/ci/sweep.py`): a LOWER-id run whose gate overlapped this one (`started_at <= this completed_at`, `completed_at >= this started_at`) and ended `success`. No other production line moves. The sweep self-test gains the verdict's ordering from both sides, the no-loop second sweep, two nulls and a census of the pair's eight orderings (below).

## Head

`fcea2880305d5638a44e7fa2664d6751576f65b1` merges main `aaaec21` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`16452e45300be5507d6f979e5033676052d0f4e8` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

f6c1866ba8564989a34cc3d09f001cdb5133ecbe. This is the PR head 520538ccfad01bee373382e9d56fc036c8c87ea0, plus the repair commit, plus origin/main 4b5d771bdf8feb1f83d7d9443e5117b771a0ab76 merged at 2026-11-07T15:47Z. That main delta touches no `tools/ci/`, `tools/pr/` or `.github/` path: `git diff --quiet 88e1140b7764571118943c5e92ef64bb21a054f0 HEAD -- tools/ci/gate.py tools/ci/prelude.py .github` exits 0, and the only `tools/ci` change since 88e1140b is this repair's `sweep.py` and `sweep_selftest.py`.

## Mutation proof

**Round 2, the repair.** The failing test came first. The head's self-test over 520538cc's `sweep.py` (`git show 520538ccfad01bee373382e9d56fc036c8c87ea0:tools/ci/sweep.py` in place, `python3 -B tools/ci/sweep.py --self-test`) prints `sweep self-test: 52 checks, 3 failed`:
- `FAIL settle: the higher of a lagging pair, deferred to a lower gate that ended green but does not cover the newest event, is re-run, swept from run 1` (and from run 2)
- `FAIL census: an overlapping deferral is re-run (lower success, higher created 52, its gate 55-56)`

Each mutant below was applied in place to the new arm `or (i < run_id and g.get("conclusion") == "success" and gs <= t1 and ge >= t0)`, then `python3 -B tools/ci/sweep.py --self-test` was run, and the tree was restored. `-B` matters here. A first driver without it printed mutant 3's failures under mutant 4, because the two mutants have the same file size and were written in the same second, so a stale `.pyc` was imported. That run is disclosed and discarded.
- **R1, the arm deleted.** 3 failed: the two `the higher of a lagging pair … is re-run` checks, and `census: an overlapping deferral is re-run (lower success, higher created 52, its gate 55-56)`.
- **R2, `conclusion == "success"` dropped**, so both sides of a red pair are re-run. 2 failed: `FAIL settle: a lagging-listing pair (sources done, gates overlapping) re-runs the lower id only, swept from run 1` (and from run 2).
- **R3, `ge >= t0` dropped**, so a gate that started after the lower concluded counts as overlapping. 7 failed, among them `FAIL settle null: that higher re-judged red after the lower's gate concluded is final, swept again from run 1 (no loop)` (and run 2) and `FAIL settle null: a higher red gate that started after the lower's green gate concluded is final, never re-run`.
- **R4, `gs <= t1` dropped.** 1 failed: `FAIL a lower green gate that started after the higher red concluded: settle from run 2 re-runs nothing, the lower's own newest-covering sweep re-runs it (swept from run 2)`. This check was added after R4 first survived, as the null that kills it.

**Round 1, re-run at this head** (the same driver and `-B`) for the mutants in `undecided()`, the function the repair edits:
- **M3, the late-source arm removed.** 3 failed, the same three checks as at 88e1140b.
- **M4, the overlapping-gate arm removed.** 4 failed: the two `lagging-listing pair … re-runs the lower id only` checks, and `census: an overlapping deferral is re-run (lower failure, higher created 45|52, its gate 55-56)`.
- **M5, the overlap arm without the id tie-break.** 2 failed: the two `lagging-listing pair` checks.

**Round 1, carried from 88e1140b and not re-run.** M1 (`gate.judge()`'s wait restored) mutates `gate.py`, which is byte-identical between 88e1140b and this head (the `git diff --quiet` in `## Head`). M2, M6 and M7 mutate `settle`'s loop and SKIP, which this diff does not touch. Their result, as measured at 88e1140b:
- **M1.** Gate self-test 77 checks, 14 failed, including `FAIL #3282: the deferring edit gate publishes CI's deferral at once and holds no runner`.
- **M2, `settle` removed.** Sweep self-test 33 checks, 10 failed, at round 1's count.
- **M6.** 2 failed, `settle: a run whose gate is still queued|waiting owns convergence`.
- **M7.** 1 failed, `settle: a gate still running is polled …`.

## Null control

- **The reviewer's probe, the finder's harness at both ends.** `refs/heads/verdict/3287:evidence/probe_settle.py` (sha1 3d9425dabc3883a3834a743765d4fd47341b98e5, byte-identical to the copy run) was run from a `tools/ci` export, `python3 -B probe_settle.py`, with `cd` into the export so that its `sys.path` "." resolves. At 520538cc it prints `swept from run 1: posts=[] out='SWEEP-DONE run=1 reruns=0'` and `swept from run 2: posts=[] out='SWEEP-DONE run=2 reruns=0'`, which is the verdict's figure reproduced. At this head it prints `posts=['repos/o/r/actions/jobs/20/rerun'] … reruns=1` from both runs. Its own null, the higher created at 45, before the lower gate started, prints `posts=['repos/o/r/actions/jobs/20/rerun']` at both ends, through the green branch.
- **No loop: the sweep run twice posts nothing the second time.** The check `settle null: that higher re-judged red after the lower's gate concluded is final, swept again from run 1|2 (no loop)` applies the first sweep's re-run (attempt 2, gate 70-71, kept red) and sweeps again. It reads `posts == []` and `reruns=0` from both runs. Its perturbation, R3, turns it red.
- **A real red after the lower concluded is final.** `settle null: a higher red gate that started after the lower's green gate concluded is final, never re-run` passes. So does the R4 null, where a lower green gate started after the higher concluded: settle from run 2 posts nothing, and the lower's own newest-covering sweep re-runs it, posting `[…/jobs/20/rerun]`.
- **The pair with a red lower still re-runs only the lower.** The round-1 checks `a lagging-listing pair … re-runs the lower id only, swept from run 1|2` pass unchanged, and R2 is their perturbation.
- **Round 1's nulls are unchanged and pass at this head.** These are `settle null: a lone red gate at its head is never re-run`, `settle null: the same reds judged after every source finished, apart, are final`, and the gate self-test's `null: no other run at the head, no wait` and `busy-defer null: a genuinely earlier run still adding sources is still deferred to`.

## Figures

- **Self-tests at this head:**
  - `python3 -B tools/ci/sweep.py --self-test`: 52 checks, 0 failed.
  - `python3 -B tools/ci/gate.py --self-test`: 77 checks, 0 failed.
  - The same sweep self-test over 520538cc's `sweep.py`: 52 checks, 3 failed (named under `## Mutation proof`).
- **Census of a lagging pair's orderings (fixer step 8, the class's seams).** The rule that enumerates them is the `itertools.product` loop in `tools/ci/sweep_selftest.py` (the comment "The census of a lagging pair's orderings"). It covers the lower gate's conclusion {success, failure}, the higher run created before (45) or after (52) the lower gate started at 50, and the higher gate inside (55-56) or after (65-66) the lower gate's 50-60. That makes 8 orderings, each swept from both runs. Over the 4 overlapping orderings it checks that the deferral is re-run, the lower where it is red, else the higher. Over all 8 it checks that the sweeps fired by the re-runs' completions post nothing (`census: the second round posts nothing`), with each re-run judging after both gates and kept red. That is 12 checks. Every seam with its disposition:
  - lower success, higher created 45, inside: re-run by the green branch at both ends. Already guarded.
  - lower success, higher created 52, inside: **closed in this diff.** This is the verdict's seam. It fails at 520538cc and passes here.
  - lower failure, higher created 45 or 52, inside: the lower is re-run by the round-1 arm, already guarded, and the higher is never re-run as well.
  - higher gate after the lower concluded, all four: a final red, re-run only by a green branch where one covers the newest event. Already guarded.
  - The second round posts nothing in all 8 at this head.

  A cost of the census's shape, stated: its round two sweeps only from runs that were re-run, because a sweep runs per CI completion. Sweeping again from a run that did not complete again re-enters the green branch, which re-runs every red gate by design (DESIGN-P2.md 4.3). That is not a loop, since that run does not complete again.
- **The class's other seam, named and left.** Two sweeps that fire close together, one per completion, can each post the same re-run before either sees the run re-queued. This was already so for round 1's arms. GitHub refuses a job re-run in a run that is not completed, and `judge()` reads `run.status` before posting, so the second post is either skipped or refused. Not measured here, and not a loop.

The check runs of the PR head 520538ccfad01bee373382e9d56fc036c8c87ea0 were read at 2026-11-07T15:50Z: 58 runs (`total_count` 58, one page of 100, no `latest` filter). Exactly one had concluded red:

The cause is main's nightly lane, not a path this PR touches, and its owner is the nightly dispatch on `main`, which goes green on its next concluded run. The others were success, skipped, queued or in progress at the read. The blocked verdict itself is a review finding, not a check, and is answered by the repair above. Fix review: blocked 520538ccfad01bee373382e9d56fc036c8c87ea0 settle-unjudged: a higher-id gate that deferred to a lagging lower run whose green gate does not cover the newest event is never re-run

bus-nonce: 2e16118cc29e36b0964fe90175304e15

Round 1 (first-round adversarial review), head 520538ccfad01bee373382e9d56fc036c8c87ea0, merge base b4ec2f332fe3ab8dcf169bd3066276d3bb8848ab.

## Block

Brief focus (2) and (4). `undecided()` re-runs a red gate in two cases. The first is when another run's non-gate job finished after the gate started, using real timestamps. The second is when a HIGHER-id run's gate started while it judged, and then only the lower id is re-run. But `busy()`'s tie-break, in the gate self-test check "busy-defer: the higher deferring edit gate defers at once to the lower whose listing lags", makes the HIGHER run defer to the LOWER one. Neither arm catches that red. It is only re-run when the lower's green gate covers the newest event, through the green branch. If the higher run was created after the lower's gate started (for example, a body edit landing during the lower gate), `covers_newest` is false and the sweep goes to `settle`. There the lower's sources finished before the higher gate started, and the lower id is not higher. So no sweep re-runs the higher's red deferral. It stays red at a head where a later green gate exists, until a human re-runs it. At the base the same gate waited one poll and judged PASS (the removed check "the higher deferring edit gate waits on the lower whose listing lags, then judges, never a red deferral"), so this is a regression the change introduces.

Reproduction (the reviewer's own instrument, disclosed; ev/probe_settle.py over sweep_selftest's World): lower run 1 created 10, units done 40, gate 50-60 green; higher run 2 created 52, gate 55-56 red (the deferral). Swept from run 1: `posts=[] SWEEP-DONE run=1 reruns=0`; swept from run 2: `posts=[] SWEEP-DONE run=2 reruns=0`. Null control: the same with run 2 created at 45, before the lower gate started, so the green branch applies: `posts=['repos/o/r/actions/jobs/20/rerun']`.

To repair it, settle needs to catch the higher side of a lagging pair, or any red gate whose run overlapped another run's gate start in either order, without reintroducing a loop. The fixer and design own the shape. A gate or sweep self-test case for this ordering should fail first.

## Findings

- settle leaves the higher-id deferral to a lagging lower green gate unjudged when that green gate does not cover the newest event (the Block above); repair in this PR. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER

## Evidence

- RESULT replay at head: `RESULT replay wait_s=0 first=FAIL swept=yes final=PASS`; at base (git archive b4ec2f33 tools/ci tools/pr): `RESULT replay wait_s=720 first=FAIL swept=yes final=PASS` (ev/replay_head.txt, ev/replay_base.txt). The #3282 replay matches the body. Note that the base also ends PASS by the sweep: the base defect the replay reproduces is the 720 s held runner, not a missing re-judge, which agrees with the body's own account of the brief's cause.
- Race harness r10_gate_defer_race.py, head against base: the four fixture rows read wait 0 s at head and 720 s at base for 42367457809 and 42338396358; 42307493684 and 42307798573 read PASS at both ends (ev/race_head.txt, ev/race_base.txt).
- Self-tests at head: gate 77 checks, 0 failed; sweep 33 checks, 0 failed (ev/selftests_head.txt). These match the body.
- Reviewer mutants (ev/mutants.txt): overlap arm removed: sweep 2 failed (matches the body's M4). Late-source arm removed: sweep 3 failed (matches M3). A null mutant (comment line only): 33 checks, 0 failed. A judge-wait mutant did not finish in ~4 min; it was stopped and is not counted. The body's M1 covers that line.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`: rc 0, tree a63dd482, no conflict.
- Roles drift `git diff merge-base...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/`: empty.
- Diff paths: VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md and every *_budgets.json are untouched. dev/programme/delivery/3287.md is in the diff. The new harness is classified INERT in tests/closures.json; the fixture lies under tools/ci (MODE FULL, per the body).
- The `## Head` section names 520538cc, the head reviewed.
- CI: `merge_train.py classify` read WAIT (`pending: gate red: none`) on every poll from 15:25Z to 15:28Z. Every check run at the head was queued or skipped (7 check runs, none concluded red). The verdict is returned before CI concluded because the block is a code defect independent of CI, and returning it now keeps the hotfix's critical path moving. The CI state is not judged.
- Not re-derived: the census figures (live API, sliding window) and the race harness table's per-scenario gate-wait seconds beyond the fixture rows above.

## Verdict

PR #3287 (R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER, r10-gate-busy-defer-3) at head 16452e45300be5507d6f979e5033676052d0f4e8, merge base and origin/main 4b5d771bdf8feb1f83d7d9443e5117b771a0ab76. This is review round 2: an earlier verdict/3287 at 29ee7261 was `settle-unjudged`, and this head carries its repair. The review ran from a detached worktree at the head, by the three-dot diff. The finder's harnesses were run at both ends: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_busy_defer_3.py replay` and `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_race.py`, the latter also as main's unmodified copy. Every production line the PR adds or changes was mutated, with a null control. CI on this head is GREEN.

Answers to the brief's four focus questions:
1. The #3282 replay reproduces the defect at the base and passes at the head. Base: `RESULT replay wait_s=720 first=FAIL swept=yes final=PASS`. Head: `wait_s=0 first=FAIL swept=yes final=PASS`. `final` stays flat because the sweep did fire at the base too, as the body says. The metric the replay moves is `wait_s`, the runner hold. Mutant G1, which restores the wait, puts head back to `wait_s=720`. The null mutant leaves it at 0. CI showed the defect live at this head: edit gate 128458265063 ran on main's program (`programs restored from 4b5d771b`), held its runner 16:36:00–16:48:08Z, and then published `FAIL run(s) [42388999905] at this head are still being judged`.
2. `settle` leaves nothing unjudged and loops nowhere in the cases I checked. Mutual deferral, a red decider, a cancelled decider, a red lower or green lower in a lagging pair, and real reds all behave. My mutants S2–S7 each turn a named settle check red. Every re-run judges after every source and the peer gate concluded, so no `undecided()` arm fires again (S3 and S4 kill the no-loop nulls). One gap remains, and it is not a regression: a head with a completed `ci.yml` run that has no `gate` job (see Findings).
3. `gate.judge` has one bound left, `lag_bound(why)`, for the run's own listing lag. The deferral-specific `GATE_WAIT_MAX_S` branch is gone, and `deferral()` is the only producer of the text. There is no second copy of the busy/wait rule in `tools/ci`. Two stale descriptions and one copied text pattern live outside the diff; they are carried below.
4. A deferral red at a head that a later green code run covers is re-run by the green branch (unchanged) or by `settle`. Live at this head, both edit gates were re-run and green within about 30 s of code gate 128470411243 going green (17:11:32Z → 17:12:23Z and 17:12:34Z).

## Findings

- Follow-up: two new `settle` lines survive their deletion with every self-test and the replay green (ev/mutants.txt). S9 drops the poll on a gate that completed while its run is still open. S10 drops the `live()` head-moved stop inside settle's poll. Neither breaks liveness. Under S9, `judge()` leaves that run ("run still busy") and that run's own completion sweep settles it. Under S10, a sweep re-runs gates at a superseded head, which wastes runners but leaves no red at the live head. They are still untested branches on lines this PR adds, and the PR names neither in its mutation proof. Owed: a settle self-test that kills each one. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER
- Follow-up: settle never ends when the head holds a `ci.yml` run that completed with no `gate` job listed, for example a `startup_failure`. `gates[i]` is `{}`, so `unconcluded` names that run and settle prints "their completion sweeps", but that run's completion has already happened. Probe ev/probe.py, ev/probe_nogate_run.txt: posts=[] at this head with that third run, posts=[jobs/10/rerun] without it. The base gives the same SKIP outcome, so this is not a regression. It is still a head where a deferral nothing re-runs stays red. Owed: settle keys `unconcluded` on gates whose run is not completed. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER
- Follow-up: one consumer still describes the superseded wait. `tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py:1161` tells the orchestrator, for a gate red beside a running sibling, "rerun the failed jobs once siblings settle (the gate defers up to 720s, GATE_WAIT_MAX_S)". At this head a deferral is published at once and gate-sweep.yml re-runs it, so the line points a seat at the hand re-run that raced the sweep on #3282 (body, brief-cause). Its self-test pins the constant's name at :3811-3824. `tools/ci/sweep.py:8`'s "the higher-id code run's gate the one that waits" is the same stale wording. Owed: reword the tick line to "the sweep re-runs it once the decider completes", together with its pinned check. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER
- Follow-up: the new harness holds its own copy of the deferral text. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_busy_defer_3.py:61` `DEFERRAL = re.compile(r"FAIL run\(s\) \[([0-9, ]+)\] at this head are still being judged")` matches the string `gate.deferral()` builds rather than deriving from it. A reworded deferral would make `census` print `deferral_fails=0` silently, which reads as the after-merge prediction `held_ge_600=0` passing. Owed: derive the pattern from `gate.deferral` (the harness already imports `gate`), or pin it with a self-check. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER
- Follow-up: the roster carry on this group (orchestrator, 2026-11-06 ~23:27Z) binds "a deferral resolve itself to the code run's conclusion, with no red and no hand rerun". This design publishes the deferral red at once and relies on gate-sweep.yml to turn it green. That means a transient red, with no hand re-run. The 11-07 dispatch brief sanctions this ("publish its deferral at once"; focus 4 asks only that no red survive a later green code run). The body never answers the carry's "no red" clause by name, though. The orchestrator should record the supersession on the group. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER

Main's unmodified copy, run against the head's tools/ci, gives the same gate-wait 0 and RESIDUAL-RED 0 in every scenario (ev/race_mainharness_at_head.txt), so the head's result does not depend on that edit.

3290.body:
The merge train treated a red `gate` as a final verdict while the head's code run was still running, and skipped pull requests that would have gone green. This is a hotfix-tier change because it blocks merges. It is CI-throughput lever 1, approved by the owner (tvofi, 2026-11-07, #201 comment 6707834331).

How it happens: an edit run's gate fails at once, deferring to the code run (tools/ci/gate.py `deferral`: "run(s) [..] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides"). The code run publishes no `gate` check run until every unit has finished. So `latest_runs` sees only the edit gate, and `classify` counts it red. Then `wait_ci` returns it, and `at_head` logs `ci red=['gate']` and SKIPs. The brief's s12 CI-throughput study (2026-11-05 13:26Z to 2026-11-07 13:26Z) counted 56 such SKIPs; in 32 the code run later concluded success. This seat did not re-take those figures; they come from the brief. #3293 at fefaa492 (2026-11-07 21:07:58Z, `SKIP #3293 ci: red at the head: gate` on main's tools at dee8b413) is a fresh instance, and this body replays it.

The fix (tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py, tools/audit/seat/proof_watch.py, tools/audit/seat/ci-watch.sh):
- `classify(latest, required, busy=())`: a red GATE is pending while `busy` is non-empty. Every other context, and every caller that passes no `busy`, behaves as before.
- `gate_busy(ci_runs, check_runs)`: tools/ci/gate.py's own `busy`, imported from its tree path and never copied. Each run's jobs come from its own check suite's check runs, so no read per run is needed.
- `Train._gate_busy`: one `actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=` listing, made only on a red gate. An unreadable listing reads no run busy, logged, so the red stands. **Round 3:** it also returns `gate_rerunning` over the same listing. 3302.body:
R10-CI-OWN-DELIVERY-ROW (owner-approved CI-throughput lever 2, #201 comment 6707834331). R10-CI-SLIM's C7(a) stands the machinery lanes down only on an all-product pull request. Every pull request carries its own delivery row `dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md`, which is not product, so the idling could not fire on any of them.

**Step 1's recording changed the scope of this fix.** The brief said to exempt the row only for the lanes that read no row. `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py` ran every `run:` step of each machinery lane under strace, in a fresh clone of the head (f020f31c). It counted each open, directory listing and exec that names a row of the clone, or of a copy of the tree. The result is `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.recording.json`:

- `tests / arch-instrument` reads **no** row. No syscall in any of its three run steps names `dev/programme`, under any root. `arch_score.py` and `arch_score_head.py` ran to `ALL TEST SCRIPTS PASSED`.
- `tests / closures` reads rows in its re-record step: the `tests/entities.py` recording, `policy_lint.mjs --record`, and `policy_lint`'s tree-wide `git grep -I -l`.
- `governance / env-matrix` reads rows. It copies the pull request's tree into `$RUNNER_TEMP/envmatrix/{pr,push-main,no-remote,shallow,…}` and runs `policy_lint` in each copy, which opens and lists every row.
- `governance / instrument-self-tests` reads rows. Step 2 (`policy_lint_mutants.mjs`, which runs `policy_lint.mjs --record --since` and its `git grep`) opens and lists the clone's rows. This lane's trace was still running when the recording was summarized (49 of its 100 run steps closed). A partial lane can only add readers, never clear one, so the verdict stands.

So this pull request does **not** idle all four lanes on a package-plus-own-row diff. `prelude.outputs` now emits two outputs:
- `machinery`: unchanged, the strict C7(a) rule. It gates the three lanes that read rows.
- `machinery_rowblind`: the same rule with exactly this pull request's own row ignored. It gates `tests / arch-instrument` alone, through a new `tests.yml` input that `ci.yml` passes.

`LANE_GATE` records which output each lane gates on, and the self-test `lane_gates` check pins it against the workflow text. A lane that reads rows therefore cannot drift to the row-blind input unseen.

The brief estimated 1,380 runner-minutes a day for idling all four lanes. That estimate does not carry over: what remains is arch-instrument's share alone, and that share is not re-measured here. Taking the row out of the other three lanes needs their row reads either shown irrelevant or removed. That is a separate change, and its seams are the readers listed above.

Transition: `ci.yml`'s prelude job restores `tools/ci/*.py` from the base, so on this pull request the base prelude runs and emits no `machinery_rowblind`. arch-instrument's steps test `!= 'false'`, so an empty input runs them (fail closed).

**Repair round (the `tests / fast (3.14)` red).** `tests/harness_headers.py` failed on its own check `every inlined walk matches the canonical helper and no depth root remains`. It printed `FAIL depth seams: dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py:50: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`. Main is green because that harness is new in this diff: `depth_root_seams()` scans every harness file, and a fixed `parents[N]` root is a depth seam it refuses. ef830f662 replaces that line with the canonical `repo_root(__file__)` walk, inlined byte-for-byte from `tools/audit/repo_root.py` as every sibling harness does it. No assertion or harness was changed.

## Head

`da510c74b86849dba15ec596457f1d880842a192` merges main `48af086` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`3dd5a3556fde58a9bc46961ef19e6724e2b6d567` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

ef830f662b648d3113dadae22e23f903e6ea03fe, a fast-forward of the PR head 2a7dcd6cf. The earlier step evidence below was measured at f8c052779. The repair commit touches only `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py`'s root line. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict, so main is not merged in, per the owner's 2026-11-07 ruling.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant applied to `tools/ci/prelude.py` (M5 to `.github/workflows/tests.yml`), checked with `python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test`, then restored:

- M2, the brief's mutant (every file under `dev/programme/delivery/` exempted): 4 failed. These are `C7a-row: ANOTHER pull request's row still counts as machinery`, `C7a-row: ... and so does the row when the event names no number`, `C7a-row: ... and runs the lanes that read rows` and `C7a-row: ... and row 8 on pull request 7 runs them`.

Failing test first: c35565f94 is the self-test against the unchanged production code, and it fails with `TypeError: machinery() takes from 1 to 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`.

## Null control

Repair: at the PR head 2a7dcd6cf, `cd tests && python3 -c "import harness_headers; raise SystemExit(harness_headers.inline_scan())"` prints the depth-seam FAIL above with rc=1. At ef830f662 it prints nothing, rc=0. Restoring `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]` makes it red again: that is the mutation proof for this repair.

At the base, `machinery` has no PR number, so a package file plus its own row runs every machinery lane (the c35565f94 red above). At the head:
- a row beside `tools/ci/gate.py` still runs the lanes;
- a row of ANOTHER pull request still counts as machinery;
- the row when the event names no number still counts;
- the own row alone runs them;
- an empty or unread changed list runs them;
- an unreadable script table runs them;
- a push runs them, for both outputs.

These are the `C7a-row:` checks in `python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test` (76 checks, 0 failed).

The `--refresh-index` arm (`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py --refresh-index --lanes closures --out <dir>`) refreshes the clone's index before any step runs, which removes git's rehash of a fresh checkout. Under it the closures re-record step still prints `open=128508 list=18`, so its reads are the steps' own and not that rehash.

The recording's own controls are in the `control` lane: a planted reader of a row (`cat`, plus `git show HEAD:<row>`), a planted copy of the row directory read whole, and a one-row fixture. They print `RESULT control_hits=3 copy_reader=True fixture_reader=False` (`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py --lanes control --out <dir>`). So a tracer recording nothing would not read as clean, and a fixture repository is not counted as the clone. The fixture control caught two scan errors in the inherited harness, both fixed in 245cb2055. Copies of the tree went uncounted, which hid env-matrix's reads, and an absolute argv into a fixture was counted.

## Figures

- Lane read verdicts: `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.recording.json` `verdict`, from `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py --lanes <lane> --out <dir>` per lane, then `--summarize`. The rule is in the file's `rule` field.

- Self-test: `python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test` prints `prelude self-test: 76 checks, 0 failed`.
- Diff mutants: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff <merge-base>...HEAD --cmd "python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test" --max-mutants 0 --report-only` ran 19 mutants on the added lines of `tools/ci/prelude.py` in 5 s wall (at f8c052779). 5 SURVIVED, listed under `## Unpinned sites`; the other 14 were killed.

- `tools/pr/prepr.sh` with `MUTANT_CMD="python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test" MUTANT_MAX=0` and this body: rc=0 at ef830f662, 355 s wall. Its diff-mutant step ran the same 19 mutants (the harness lines are outside the driver's scope) and left the same 5 survivors, all answered under `## Unpinned sites`. Main has not been merged in. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict, and the owner's 2026-11-07 ruling says to hand off at the first clean head.
- Repair: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 tests/harness_headers.py` prints `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED` at ef830f662. `cd tests && python3 -c "import harness_headers; raise SystemExit(harness_headers.inline_scan())"` exits 0 in 0.7 s at ef830f662 and 1 at 2a7dcd6cf.

Cheaper detector: `harness_headers.inline_scan()` alone takes 0.7 s and measures nothing about the machine. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` leaves all of `harness_headers.py` to CI, because the script holds the EXCLUSIVE gate lease (`gate_lock.py needs-lease` answers `lease`). So the structural check rides inside a lease-deferred run, and no seat-side step runs it. Countermeasure not built here: it changes `prepr.sh`, which is outside this group. Carried below.

They stop the own-row exemption from reaching those three lanes. Fix review: merge 3dd5a3556fde58a9bc46961ef19e6724e2b6d567
